By "Whoever does not abide in form, does not abide in feeling," and so on, with respect to these, the cause is the knowledge of the path itself, and that, too, through the distinction of stages like heat and so on, appropriately abandons oneself and others. As it is said: "The path of the disciple and rhinoceros, / and this and others' qualities, / the path of seeing which has great benefits, / acting and aspiring, / praising, exalting, and commending, / dedicating and rejoicing, / supreme mental engagements, / accomplishing and utterly pure, / this is the path of meditation; / by wise bodhisattvas / the knowledge of the path itself is explained like that." Thus, these minor sections, from the aspect of non-apprehension of the dharmas that show nirvāṇa through the three vehicles, are the clear realizations that make one realize wisdom, therefore they are taught from that aspect. Regarding this from "Whoever [does not abide] in form" up to "does not abide in the stages": moreover, whichever bodhisattva does not abide in form by way of adhering to it as appearance and reality; does not abide in feeling either; whoever does not abide in discrimination either, meaning they do not abide in volition, which is formations; and does not abide in any consciousness by way of adhering to it as appearance and reality, they abide in the signless dharmatā; this lack of adherence is acting in the supreme perfection of wisdom. Likewise, they do not abide in particulars such as permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, self and the suchness of selflessness that negates it, and what is called emptiness of suchness. They do not abide in the attainment of the fruits such as stream-enterer, and they do not abide in the stage and signs of a foe-destroyer and so on, and they do not abide in the stage of a solitary conqueror or likewise in the stage of a completely perfect buddha.

By "Whoever does not abide in form, does not abide in feeling," and so on, with respect to these, the cause is the knowledge of the path itself, and that, too, through the distinction of stages like heat and so on, appropriately abandons oneself and others. As it is said: "The path of the disciple and rhinoceros, / and this and others' qualities, / the path of seeing which has great benefits, / acting and aspiring, / praising, exalting, and commending, / dedicating and rejoicing, / supreme mental engagements, / accomplishing and utterly pure, / this is the path of meditation; / by wise bodhisattvas / the knowledge of the path itself is explained like that." Thus, these minor sections, from the aspect of non-apprehension of the dharmas that show nirvāṇa through the three vehicles, are the clear realizations that make one realize wisdom, therefore they are taught from that aspect. Regarding this from "Whoever [does not abide] in form" up to "does not abide in the stages": moreover, whichever bodhisattva does not abide in form by way of adhering to it as appearance and reality; does not abide in feeling either; whoever does not abide in discrimination either, meaning they do not abide in volition, which is formations; and does not abide in any consciousness by way of adhering to it as appearance and reality, they abide in the signless dharmatā; this lack of adherence is acting in the supreme perfection of wisdom. Likewise, they do not abide in particulars such as permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, self and the suchness of selflessness that negates it, and what is called emptiness of suchness. They do not abide in the attainment of the fruits such as stream-enterer, and they do not abide in the stage and signs of a foe-destroyer and so on, and they do not abide in the stage of a solitary conqueror or likewise in the stage of a completely perfect buddha.

By "Whoever does not abide in form, does not abide in feeling," and so on, with respect to these, the cause is the knowledge of the path itself, and that, too, through the distinction of stages like heat and so on, appropriately abandons oneself and others. As it is said: "The path of the disciple and rhinoceros, / and this and others' qualities, / the path of seeing which has great benefits, / acting and aspiring, / praising, exalting, and commending, / dedicating and rejoicing, / supreme mental engagements, / accomplishing and utterly pure, / this is the path of meditation; / by wise bodhisattvas / the knowledge of the path itself is explained like that." Thus, these minor sections, from the aspect of non-apprehension of the dharmas that show nirvāṇa through the three vehicles, are the clear realizations that make one realize wisdom, therefore they are taught from that aspect. Regarding this from "Whoever [does not abide] in form" up to "does not abide in the stages": moreover, whichever bodhisattva does not abide in form by way of adhering to it as appearance and reality; does not abide in feeling either; whoever does not abide in discrimination either, meaning they do not abide in volition, which is formations; and does not abide in any consciousness by way of adhering to it as appearance and reality, they abide in the signless dharmatā; this lack of adherence is acting in the supreme perfection of wisdom. Likewise, they do not abide in particulars such as permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, self and the suchness of selflessness that negates it, and what is called emptiness of suchness. They do not abide in the attainment of the fruits such as stream-enterer, and they do not abide in the stage and signs of a foe-destroyer and so on, and they do not abide in the stage of a solitary conqueror or likewise in the stage of a completely perfect buddha.

By "Whoever does not abide in form, does not abide in feeling," and so on, with respect to these, the cause is the knowledge of the path itself, and that, too, through the distinction of stages like heat and so on, appropriately abandons oneself and others. As it is said: "The path of the disciple and rhinoceros, / and this and others' qualities, / the path of seeing which has great benefits, / acting and aspiring, / praising, exalting, and commending, / dedicating and rejoicing, / supreme mental engagements, / accomplishing and utterly pure, / this is the path of meditation; / by wise bodhisattvas / the knowledge of the path itself is explained like that." Thus, these minor sections, from the aspect of non-apprehension of the dharmas that show nirvāṇa through the three vehicles, are the clear realizations that make one realize wisdom, therefore they are taught from that aspect. Regarding this from "Whoever [does not abide] in form" up to "does not abide in the stages": moreover, whichever bodhisattva does not abide in form by way of adhering to it as appearance and reality; does not abide in feeling either; whoever does not abide in discrimination either, meaning they do not abide in volition, which is formations; and does not abide in any consciousness by way of adhering to it as appearance and reality, they abide in the signless dharmatā; this lack of adherence is acting in the supreme perfection of wisdom. Likewise, they do not abide in particulars such as permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, self and the suchness of selflessness that negates it, and what is called emptiness of suchness. They do not abide in the attainment of the fruits such as stream-enterer, and they do not abide in the stage and signs of a foe-destroyer and so on, and they do not abide in the stage of a solitary conqueror or likewise in the stage of a completely perfect buddha.

heading: **འདུ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་མ་འཇིགས་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "Discrimination is this shore" up to "abides in the word": the Buddha, the guide, has completely proclaimed that discriminating self and other or saṃsāra and nirvāṇa as truly dual is this shore, saṃsāra; and reversing that, having destroyed discrimination by means of scripture and reasoning, the bodhisattva who abandons grasping at truth goes to the other shore, nirvāṇa; and those who are free from the discrimination of true appearance, whatever subsequent realization they obtain, exactly that abides in the word of definitive meaning which teaches abiding in the path, the perfection of wisdom.

heading: **དེ་དག་གི་འཐད་པ་བསྟན་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "If by the Teacher" up to "acts": even if the Teacher, the Buddha, were to remain for eons numbering as many as the grains of sand on the banks of the Ganges and proclaim the sound of the dharma to sentient beings, how could sentient beings, who are pure and unestablished from the very beginning, be born and arise? Therefore, this being free from the discrimination of difference is acting in the supreme perfection of wisdom.

source: ལ་ལས་བདེ་གཤེགས་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནས། ཆར་མི་ཕོད་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། གང་ཟག་གང་ལ་ལས་བདེ་བར་གཤེགས་པ་ཡོངས་སུ་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པའི་མཆོད་རྟེན་ཁྱད་པར་གསུམ་དང་ལྡན་པ་ལས། རྒྱུའི་ཁྱད་པར་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་སྣ་བདུན་ལས་བྱས་ཤིང་དེ་ལ་མཆོད་པར་བྱེད་ལ། གྲངས་ཀྱི་ཁྱད་པར་བདེ་བར་གཤེགས་པའི་མཆོད་རྟེན་དེ་དག་ཆུ་བོ་གངྒཱའི་འགྲམ་གྱི་བྱེ་མའི་གྲངས་སྙེད་ཀྱིས་བྱེ་བ་ཕྲག་སྟོང་དང་མཉམ་པའི་ཞིང་ཁམས་ཐམས་ཅད་བཀང་སྟེ། མཆོད་པའི་ཁྱད་པར་ལས་མཆོད་བྱེད་ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟག་པའི་ཐབས་བཟུང་ན་སྔར་གྱི་ཞིང་ཁམས་བྱེ་བ་མཐའ་ཡས་ན་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་བྱེད་པ། གྲུབ་པ་རྣམས་ཆུད་མི་ཟ་བར་བྱེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རིགས་སྔགས་ཆེན་པོའོ། །འདུས་བྱས་འཁོར་བའི་བདེ་བ་དང༌། འདུས་མ་བྱས་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པའི་བདེ་བ་གང་གྲངས་ཇི་སྙེད་འཁོད་པ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱིས་མཆོད་པ་ལས་གཞན་པའི་ལས་མི་བྱེད་པར་མཆོད་པའི་རྫས་ལྷའི་མེ་ཏོག་དང་སྤོས་རབ་དང་ཙན་དན་ལ་སོགས་པའི་བྱུག་པས་དུས་སྔ་དྲོ་གུང་ཕྱི་དྲོ་གསུམ་དུ་ཡུན་རིང་བ་བསྐལ་པའམ། དེ་བས་ཀྱང་ལྷག་པར་མཆོད་པར་བྱེད་ལ། གང་ཟག་གང་ལ་ལ་ཞིག་གིས་ཆོས་གང་ཉམས་སུ་བླངས་པ་ལས་རྣམ་པར་འདྲེན་པ་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སྟོབས་བཅུ་འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར་ལ། བདེ་བར་གཤེགས་པ་བསྐྱེད་པའི་ཡུམ་འདི་གླེགས་བམ་ལ་ཡི་གེར་བྲིས་ཏེ། ལག་ཏུ་འཆང་ཞིང་མཆོད་པའི་ཁྱད་པར་མེ་ཏོག་དང་བྱུག་པ་བསྟི་སྟང་སྟེ་མཆོད་པ་བྱེད་པར་གྱུར་ལ། སྔར་གྱི་མཆོད་རྟེན་བྱས་ནས་དེ་མཆོད་པའི་བསོད་ནམས་ཅི་ཡོད་པ་དེ་བས་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་གླེགས་བམ་ལ་བྲིས་ཏེ་མཆོད་ན་བསོད་ནམས་དེའི་བརྒྱའི་ཆར་ཡང་ཉེ་བར་མི་འགྲོ། སྟོང་གི་ཆར་ཡང་མི་འགྲོ། དེ་བཞིན་དུ་བརྒྱ་སྟོང་གི་ཆ་དང༌། བྱེ་བའི་ཆ་དང༌། བྱེ་བ་བརྒྱའི་ཆ་དང༌། བྱེ་བ་བརྒྱ་སྟོང་ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་གི་ཚད་ཡང་མི་ཕོད་ལ། གྲངས་དང་དཔེ་དང་རྒྱུའི་བར་དུ་ཡང་མི་ཕོད་དོ། །
translation: Regarding this from "Someone the Sugata" up to "does not match the fraction": whatever person builds stupas of the Sugatas who have completely passed into nirvāṇa, possessing three special qualities—from the special quality of cause, they are made of the seven precious things, and one makes offerings to them; as the special quality of number, filling all the buddha-fields equaling a thousand ten millions times the number of grains of sand on the banks of the river Ganges with those stupas of the Sugatas; and from the special quality of offering, if one grasps the method of fully analyzing the offerer, since it prevents the actions and accomplishments of sentient beings in the previous infinite ten millions of buddha fields from going to waste, it is the great mantra of awareness. And whatever number of beings there are abiding in the happiness of conditioned saṃsāra and the happiness of unconditioned nirvāṇa, all of them doing no other work than offering, making offerings with offering substances of divine flowers, excellent incense, and ointments of sandalwood and so forth, in the three times of morning, noon, and afternoon for a long duration of an eon, or even more than that; and whatever person puts into practice the dharma from which the ten powers of the Buddha, the guide, arise, and having written this Mother who gives birth to the Sugatas as letters in a volume, holds it in their hands, and as the special quality of offering, makes offerings showing reverence with flowers and ointments; then whatever merit there is from having built the former stupas and offered to them, compared to that, if one writes the perfection of wisdom in a volume and makes offerings, it does not approach even a hundredth fraction of that merit. It does not approach even a thousandth fraction. Likewise, it does not match even the measure of a hundred-thousandth fraction, a ten-millionth fraction, a hundred ten-millionth fraction, or a hundred-thousand ten-million niyuta fraction; and it does not match up to a number, example, or cause.

source: ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། ཡང་རིགས་སྔགས་ཆེ་བའི་རྒྱུ་མཚན་སྟོན་ཏེ། དེ་ལྟར་ཡང་ཤེར་སྙིང་ལས། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་སྔགས། རིག་པ་ཆེན་པོའི་སྔགས། བླ་ན་མེད་པའི་སྔགས། མི་མཉམ་པ་དང་མཉམ་པའི་སྔགས། སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཐམས་ཅད་རབ་ཏུ་ཞི་བར་བྱེད་པའི་སྔགས། ཞེས་བཤད་དོ། །
translation: Thus it is said: Furthermore, it teaches the reason why it is the great mantra of awareness. Thus also in the Heart of Wisdom it is explained: "The mantra of the perfection of wisdom, the mantra of great awareness, the unsurpassed mantra, the mantra equal to the unequaled, the mantra that completely pacifies all suffering."

source: སེམས་ཅན་ཁམས་མང་ཞེས་པ་ནས། ཆོས་ཀུན་འགྲོ་བར་འགྱུར་ཞེས་པའི་བར་གྱིས། ཚུལ་གང་ཞེ་ན་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་ཁམས་མང་པོའི་སེམས་ཀྱི་མྱ་ངན་དང་ན་ཚ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་གྱི་ཆོས་ཞི་བར་བྱེད་པ་དང༌། སངས་རྒྱས་གང་དག་སྔར་འདས་པ་རྣམས་དང༌། གང་དག་ད་ལྟར་ཕྱོགས་བཅུ་ན་བཞུགས་པའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་མགོན་པོ་རྣམས་རིགས་སྔགས་ཆེན་པོ་འདི་ལ་བསླབས་པས་བདག་གཞན་གྱི་ཉོན་མོངས་ཀྱི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་མཐའ་དག་སེལ་བའི་སྨན་པའི་རྒྱལ་པོ་བླ་ན་མེད་པར་འགྱུར་ལ། མ་འོངས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་གང་དག་སེམས་ཅན་ལ་ཕན་པ་དང་སྙིང་རྗེ་དང་བཅས་པར་སྤྱད་པ་སྤྱོད་པ་དེ་དག་ཀྱང༌། རིགས་སྔགས་ཆེན་མོ་འདི་ལ་ཐོས་བསམ་སྒོམ་གསུམ་གྱིས་སམ་ཆོས་སྤྱོད་བཅུས་བསླབས་ནས་མཁས་པར་གྱུར་པས་བྱང་ཆུབ་ལ་རེག་པར་གྱུར་བ་ཡིན་ནོ། །རྒྱལ་བའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་འདི་རིགས་སྔགས་ཆེ། །ཞེས་པའི་དོན་དེ་ལ། དེ་ལྟར་བསོད་ནམས་ཆེ་བའི་རྒྱུ་མཚན་ཅིས་ཆེ་ན། རྒྱལ་བའི་ཡུམ་ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདི་ཡིས། སེམས་ཅན་སྡུག་བསྔལ་བའི་རང་བཞིན་ཅན། ཐམས་ཅད་བདེ་བའི་གནས་སུ་འདྲེན་པ་དང༌། མ་གྲུབ་པ་རྣམས་གྲུབ་པར་ཡིན་པའི་བདེ་བ་དེ་ཀུན། རིགས་སྔགས་ཆེན་མོ་འདི་ལས་བྱུང་བར་རིག་པར་བྱའོ། །དཔེར་ན་རྒྱུ་ས་བོན་བཏབ་ནས་ས་གཞི་ལ་གནས་ཏེ། འབྲས་བུ་མྱུ་གུ་འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར་བ་སྟེ། རྒྱུ་རྐྱེན་གྱི་ཚོགས་པ་ཚང་བར་སྙེད་ནས་མྱུ་གུ་རྣམས་མང་གི་གཟུགས་དག་རྣམ་པར་སྐྱེ་བ་ལྟར་དུ། རྒྱུའི་དུས་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་དང་འབྲས་བུའི་དུས་ན་བྱང་ཆུབ་གསུམ་གྱི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཇི་སྙེད་ཡོད་པ། དེ་དག་ཀུན་ཀྱང་འཁོར་གསུམ་དུ་མི་རྟོག་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལས་སྐྱེ་བར་འགྱུར་རོ། །ཡང་དཔེར་ན་འཁོར་ལོས་བསྒྱུར་བའི་རྒྱལ་པོ་ལམ་གང་དང་གང་ནས་རྟག་ཏུ་འགྲོ་བའི་ལམ་དེ་དང་དེ་ཉིད་ལས་ནི་འཁོར་ལོ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་རིན་ཆེན་སྣ་བདུན་པོ་དང༌། རྟ་དང་རྐང་ཐང་དང༌། དམག་མི་དང་དཔུང་བུ་ཆུང་གི་ཚོགས་ཏེ། དཔུང་གི་ཚོགས་བཞི་པོ་ཀུན་འགྲོ་བ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ། ལམ་གང་ནས་རྒྱལ་བ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་རྟོགས་ནས་གསུངས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདི་འགྲོ་བ་དེ་ཉིད་ནས་ནི་སྤངས་པ་དང་རྟོགས་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་ཆོས་ཀུན་ཀྱང་འགྲོ་བར་འགྱུར་རོ། །
translation: Regarding this from "Many realms of beings" up to "all dharmas go": What is the way? Pacifying the dharmas of suffering, such as the sorrow and sickness of the minds of the many realms of beings; and whatever buddhas have previously passed away, and whatever protectors of the world currently abide in the ten directions, by training in this great mantra of awareness, they become the unsurpassed kings of physicians who remove all the suffering of afflictions for themselves and others; and whatever future buddhas engage in conduct endowed with benefit and compassion for sentient beings, they also, having trained in this great mantra of awareness through the three of hearing, thinking, and meditating, or through the ten Dharma activities, become wise and touch enlightenment. Regarding the meaning of "This perfection of wisdom of the Conquerors is the great mantra of awareness": if one asks, "Why is the reason for its merit being so great in that way?" Because by this perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Conquerors, all sentient beings possessing the nature of suffering are led to the state of happiness, and all that happiness of establishing those who are unestablished, one should know to have arisen from this great mantra of awareness. For example, having planted a cause, a seed, it abides in the earth, and the result, a sprout, arises; finding the collection of causes and conditions to be complete, just as the forms of many sprouts are produced; whatever qualities there are of the five perfections at the time of the cause and the three enlightenments at the time of the result, all of those are produced from the perfection of wisdom that does not conceptualize the three spheres. Furthermore, for example, along whatever path a wheel-turning king constantly travels, along that very path the seven precious things such as the wheel, and the assembly of cavalry, infantry, soldiers, and minor forces—that is, all four divisions of the army—travel; likewise, along whatever path this perfection of wisdom, realized and taught by the Conquerors, travels, along that very path all the dharmas of the qualities of abandonment and realization also go.

heading: **མདོར་བསྟན་པ།**
translation: Regarding this from "The Conqueror to Śakra" up to "take that very one": the Conqueror Buddha asked Śakra, the lord of the gods, "If you were offered this volume of the perfection of wisdom of the Tathāgata and the bodily relics of the Tathāgata, which of those two parts would you take?" In answer to being fully asked that, Śakra said, "If I were offered that part which is the volume, and even if together with that I were offered buddha-fields equaling the number of grains of sand of the river Ganges, all of them fully filled to the brim with the relics of the Conqueror, I would take this very volume of the perfection of wisdom."

Regarding this from "Someone the Sugata" up to "does not match the fraction": whatever person builds stupas of the Sugatas who have completely passed into nirvāṇa, possessing three special qualities—from the special quality of cause, they are made of the seven precious things, and one makes offerings to them; as the special quality of number, filling all the buddha-fields equaling a thousand ten millions times the number of grains of sand on the banks of the river Ganges with those stupas of the Sugatas; and from the special quality of offering, if one grasps the method of fully analyzing the offerer, since it prevents the actions and accomplishments of sentient beings in the previous infinite ten millions of buddha fields from going to waste, it is the great mantra of awareness. And whatever number of beings there are abiding in the happiness of conditioned saṃsāra and the happiness of unconditioned nirvāṇa, all of them doing no other work than offering, making offerings with offering substances of divine flowers, excellent incense, and ointments of sandalwood and so forth, in the three times of morning, noon, and afternoon for a long duration of an eon, or even more than that; and whatever person puts into practice the dharma from which the ten powers of the Buddha, the guide, arise, and having written this Mother who gives birth to the Sugatas as letters in a volume, holds it in their hands, and as the special quality of offering, makes offerings showing reverence with flowers and ointments; then whatever merit there is from having built the former stupas and offered to them, compared to that, if one writes the perfection of wisdom in a volume and makes offerings, it does not approach even a hundredth fraction of that merit. It does not approach even a thousandth fraction. Likewise, it does not match even the measure of a hundred-thousandth fraction, a ten-millionth fraction, a hundred ten-millionth fraction, or a hundred-thousand ten-million niyuta fraction; and it does not match up to a number, example, or cause.

source: ནས། འཛིན་པ་ཡིན་ཞེས་པའི་བར། སྦྱིན་པ་ཞེས་ཟང་ཟིང་དང༌། ཆོས་དང༌། མི་འཇིགས་པ་སྐྱབས་ཏེ། སྦྱིན་པ་གསུམ་ཡང༌། བདག་མེད་ཀྱི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་སྦྱིན་ན་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པར་འགྱུར་ཏེ། དྲུག་ལྡན་དུ་ཉམས་སུ་བླང་ངོ༌། །དེ་ཡང་འགྲོ་བ་ལ་མ་ཆགས་པར་སྦྱིན་པའི་མ་དག་པས་ཡོངས་སུ་མ་གོས་པའི་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས། ཁོང་ཁྲོ་བ་མེད་པའི་བཟོད་པ། མྱུར་དུ་བསྒྲུབ་པའི་བརྩོན་འགྲུས། རྩེ་གཅིག་ཏུ་བསམ་པའི་བསམ་གཏན། དམིགས་པ་མེད་པའི་རང་བཞིན་དུ་བསྔོ་བའི་ཤེས་རབ་སྟེ། འདི་ལ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གང་ཞིག་གིས། དམིགས་ཡུལ་སེམས་ཅན་ཡང་བདེན་མེད་དུ་ཤེས་ལ། སྦྱིན་པ་དངོས་བྱིན་པའི་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ངོ་བོ་དམིགས་སུ་མེད་པ་ཡིན་ཀྱང༌། བློ་དམན་པའི་སྐྱེས་བུ་དག་གིས་སྦྱིན་པའི་དངོས་པོ་ལ་ཆགས་པ་མེད་པར་ཡུལ་ནམ་མཁའི་མཐའ་དང་མཉམ་པ་ནས་བློས་བླངས་ལ་བསླབ་བོ། །ཅིའི་ཕྱིར་ཞེ་ན། དམིགས་མེད་ཀྱི་ཆར་གྱུར་ཏེ། དམིགས་ཙམ་ཡོད་ཀྱི་དམན་པའི་ཕྱིར་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །དེ་བཞིན་དུ་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་དང་བཟོད་པ་དང༌། བརྩོན་འགྲུས་དང་བསམ་གཏན་ཀྱང་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པར་བྱེད་པ་ལ་དེ་ལྟ་བུའི་དམིགས་མེད་དེ་སྔོན་དུ་འགྲོ་བ་ཡིན་ནོ། །དེ་སྔོན་དུ་འགྲོ་བས་ཅི་བྱེད་ཞེ་ན། བསོད་ནམས་དགེ་བའི་ཆོས་མི་དམིགས་པར་བསྔོས་པས་ཆུད་མི་གསོན་པའི་ཕྱིར་ཡོངས་སུ་འཛིན་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །
translation: up to "is holding": Although there are three givings—the giving of material goods, of Dharma, and of protection from fear—if one gives with the wisdom of selflessness, it becomes a perfection, and one should practice it endowed with the six. Furthermore, giving without attachment to beings; discipline completely untainted by impurity; patience without anger; diligence that accomplishes quickly; concentration that thinks one-pointedly; and wisdom that dedicates with a non-referential nature—here, whatever bodhisattva knows the object, sentient beings, to also be without truth, and although the essence of the merit of giving the thing given is non-referential, persons of inferior minds should train in giving without attachment to the thing given, taking it mentally from objects equal to the limits of space. If one asks why: because it becomes a part of non-apprehension, and not because of the inferiority of having mere apprehension. Likewise, for discipline, patience, diligence, and concentration to become perfections, such non-apprehension precedes them. If one asks what is done by that preceding: it is fully held because by dedicating the dharmas of merit and virtue without apprehension, they are not wasted.

Regarding this from "Many realms of beings" up to "all dharmas go": What is the way? Pacifying the dharmas of suffering, such as the sorrow and sickness of the minds of the many realms of beings; and whatever buddhas have previously passed away, and whatever protectors of the world currently abide in the ten directions, by training in this great mantra of awareness, they become the unsurpassed kings of physicians who remove all the suffering of afflictions for themselves and others; and whatever future buddhas engage in conduct endowed with benefit and compassion for sentient beings, they also, having trained in this great mantra of awareness through the three of hearing, thinking, and meditating, or through the ten Dharma activities, become wise and touch enlightenment. Regarding the meaning of "This perfection of wisdom of the Conquerors is the great mantra of awareness": if one asks, "Why is the reason for its merit being so great in that way?" Because by this perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Conquerors, all sentient beings possessing the nature of suffering are led to the state of happiness, and all that happiness of establishing those who are unestablished, one should know to have arisen from this great mantra of awareness. For example, having planted a cause, a seed, it abides in the earth, and the result, a sprout, arises; finding the collection of causes and conditions to be complete, just as the forms of many sprouts are produced; whatever qualities there are of the five perfections at the time of the cause and the three enlightenments at the time of the result, all of those are produced from the perfection of wisdom that does not conceptualize the three spheres. Furthermore, for example, along whatever path a wheel-turning king constantly travels, along that very path the seven precious things such as the wheel, and the assembly of cavalry, infantry, soldiers, and minor forces—that is, all four divisions of the army—travel; likewise, along whatever path this perfection of wisdom, realized and taught by the Conquerors, travels, along that very path all the dharmas of the qualities of abandonment and realization also go.

Regarding this from "The Conqueror to Śakra" up to "take that very one": the Conqueror Buddha asked Śakra, the lord of the gods, "If you were offered this volume of the perfection of wisdom of the Tathāgata and the bodily relics of the Tathāgata, which of those two parts would you take?" In answer to being fully asked that, Śakra said, "If I were offered that part which is the volume, and even if together with that I were offered buddha-fields equaling the number of grains of sand of the river Ganges, all of them fully filled to the brim with the relics of the Conqueror, I would take this very volume of the perfection of wisdom."

Regarding this from "Many realms of beings" up to "all dharmas go": What is the way? Pacifying the dharmas of suffering, such as the sorrow and sickness of the minds of the many realms of beings; and whatever buddhas have previously passed away, and whatever protectors of the world currently abide in the ten directions, by training in this great mantra of awareness, they become the unsurpassed kings of physicians who remove all the suffering of afflictions for themselves and others; and whatever future buddhas engage in conduct endowed with benefit and compassion for sentient beings, they also, having trained in this great mantra of awareness through the three of hearing, thinking, and meditating, or through the ten Dharma activities, become wise and touch enlightenment. Regarding the meaning of "This perfection of wisdom of the Conquerors is the great mantra of awareness": if one asks, "Why is the reason for its merit being so great in that way?" Because by this perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Conquerors, all sentient beings possessing the nature of suffering are led to the state of happiness, and all that happiness of establishing those who are unestablished, one should know to have arisen from this great mantra of awareness. For example, having planted a cause, a seed, it abides in the earth, and the result, a sprout, arises; finding the collection of causes and conditions to be complete, just as the forms of many sprouts are produced; whatever qualities there are of the five perfections at the time of the cause and the three enlightenments at the time of the result, all of those are produced from the perfection of wisdom that does not conceptualize the three spheres. Furthermore, for example, along whatever path a wheel-turning king constantly travels, along that very path the seven precious things such as the wheel, and the assembly of cavalry, infantry, soldiers, and minor forces—that is, all four divisions of the army—travel; likewise, along whatever path this perfection of wisdom, realized and taught by the Conquerors, travels, along that very path all the dharmas of the qualities of abandonment and realization also go.

Regarding this from "The Conqueror to Śakra" up to "take that very one": the Conqueror Buddha asked Śakra, the lord of the gods, "If you were offered this volume of the perfection of wisdom of the Tathāgata and the bodily relics of the Tathāgata, which of those two parts would you take?" In answer to being fully asked that, Śakra said, "If I were offered that part which is the volume, and even if together with that I were offered buddha-fields equaling the number of grains of sand of the river Ganges, all of them fully filled to the brim with the relics of the Conqueror, I would take this very volume of the perfection of wisdom."

Regarding this from "Many realms of beings" up to "all dharmas go": What is the way? Pacifying the dharmas of suffering, such as the sorrow and sickness of the minds of the many realms of beings; and whatever buddhas have previously passed away, and whatever protectors of the world currently abide in the ten directions, by training in this great mantra of awareness, they become the unsurpassed kings of physicians who remove all the suffering of afflictions for themselves and others; and whatever future buddhas engage in conduct endowed with benefit and compassion for sentient beings, they also, having trained in this great mantra of awareness through the three of hearing, thinking, and meditating, or through the ten Dharma activities, become wise and touch enlightenment. Regarding the meaning of "This perfection of wisdom of the Conquerors is the great mantra of awareness": if one asks, "Why is the reason for its merit being so great in that way?" Because by this perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Conquerors, all sentient beings possessing the nature of suffering are led to the state of happiness, and all that happiness of establishing those who are unestablished, one should know to have arisen from this great mantra of awareness. For example, having planted a cause, a seed, it abides in the earth, and the result, a sprout, arises; finding the collection of causes and conditions to be complete, just as the forms of many sprouts are produced; whatever qualities there are of the five perfections at the time of the cause and the three enlightenments at the time of the result, all of those are produced from the perfection of wisdom that does not conceptualize the three spheres. Furthermore, for example, along whatever path a wheel-turning king constantly travels, along that very path the seven precious things such as the wheel, and the assembly of cavalry, infantry, soldiers, and minor forces—that is, all four divisions of the army—travel; likewise, along whatever path this perfection of wisdom, realized and taught by the Conquerors, travels, along that very path all the dharmas of the qualities of abandonment and realization also go.

Regarding this from "The Conqueror to Śakra" up to "take that very one": the Conqueror Buddha asked Śakra, the lord of the gods, "If you were offered this volume of the perfection of wisdom of the Tathāgata and the bodily relics of the Tathāgata, which of those two parts would you take?" In answer to being fully asked that, Śakra said, "If I were offered that part which is the volume, and even if together with that I were offered buddha-fields equaling the number of grains of sand of the river Ganges, all of them fully filled to the brim with the relics of the Conqueror, I would take this very volume of the perfection of wisdom."

སེམས་ཅན་ཁམས་མང་ཞེས་པ་ནས། ཆོས་ཀུན་འགྲོ་བར་འགྱུར་ཞེས་པའི་བར་གྱིས། ཚུལ་གང་ཞེ་ན་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་ཁམས་མང་པོའི་སེམས་ཀྱི་མྱ་ངན་དང་ན་ཚ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་གྱི་ཆོས་ཞི་བར་བྱེད་པ་དང༌། སངས་རྒྱས་གང་དག་སྔར་འདས་པ་རྣམས་དང༌། གང་དག་ད་ལྟར་ཕྱོགས་བཅུ་ན་བཞུགས་པའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་མགོན་པོ་རྣམས་རིགས་སྔགས་ཆེན་པོ་འདི་ལ་བསླབས་པས་བདག་གཞན་གྱི་ཉོན་མོངས་ཀྱི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་མཐའ་དག་སེལ་བའི་སྨན་པའི་རྒྱལ་པོ་བླ་ན་མེད་པར་འགྱུར་ལ། མ་འོངས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་གང་དག་སེམས་ཅན་ལ་ཕན་པ་དང་སྙིང་རྗེ་དང་བཅས་པར་སྤྱད་པ་སྤྱོད་པ་དེ་དག་ཀྱང༌། རིགས་སྔགས་ཆེན་མོ་འདི་ལ་ཐོས་བསམ་སྒོམ་གསུམ་གྱིས་སམ་ཆོས་སྤྱོད་བཅུས་བསླབས་ནས་མཁས་པར་གྱུར་པས་བྱང་ཆུབ་ལ་རེག་པར་གྱུར་བ་ཡིན་ནོ། །རྒྱལ་བའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་འདི་རིགས་སྔགས་ཆེ། །ཞེས་པའི་དོན་དེ་ལ། དེ་ལྟར་བསོད་ནམས་ཆེ་བའི་རྒྱུ་མཚན་ཅིས་ཆེ་ན། རྒྱལ་བའི་ཡུམ་ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདི་ཡིས། སེམས་ཅན་སྡུག་བསྔལ་བའི་རང་བཞིན་ཅན། ཐམས་ཅད་བདེ་བའི་གནས་སུ་འདྲེན་པ་དང༌། མ་གྲུབ་པ་རྣམས་གྲུབ་པར་ཡིན་པའི་བདེ་བ་དེ་ཀུན། རིགས་སྔགས་ཆེན་མོ་འདི་ལས་བྱུང་བར་རིག་པར་བྱའོ། །དཔེར་ན་རྒྱུ་ས་བོན་བཏབ་ནས་ས་གཞི་ལ་གནས་ཏེ། འབྲས་བུ་མྱུ་གུ་འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར་བ་སྟེ། རྒྱུ་རྐྱེན་གྱི་ཚོགས་པ་ཚང་བར་སྙེད་ནས་མྱུ་གུ་རྣམས་མང་གི་གཟུགས་དག་རྣམ་པར་སྐྱེ་བ་ལྟར་དུ། རྒྱུའི་དུས་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་དང་འབྲས་བུའི་དུས་ན་བྱང་ཆུབ་གསུམ་གྱི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཇི་སྙེད་ཡོད་པ། དེ་དག་ཀུན་ཀྱང་འཁོར་གསུམ་དུ་མི་རྟོག་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལས་སྐྱེ་བར་འགྱུར་རོ། །ཡང་དཔེར་ན་འཁོར་ལོས་བསྒྱུར་བའི་རྒྱལ་པོ་ལམ་གང་དང་གང་ནས་རྟག་ཏུ་འགྲོ་བའི་ལམ་དེ་དང་དེ་ཉིད་ལས་ནི་འཁོར་ལོ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་རིན་ཆེན་སྣ་བདུན་པོ་དང༌། རྟ་དང་རྐང་ཐང་དང༌། དམག་མི་དང་དཔུང་བུ་ཆུང་གི་ཚོགས་ཏེ། དཔུང་གི་ཚོགས་བཞི་པོ་ཀུན་འགྲོ་བ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ། ལམ་གང་ནས་རྒྱལ་བ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་རྟོགས་ནས་གསུངས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདི་འགྲོ་བ་དེ་ཉིད་ནས་ནི་སྤངས་པ་དང་རྟོགས་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་ཆོས་ཀུན་ཀྱང་འགྲོ་བར་འགྱུར་རོ། །
[2-56] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "Many realms of beings" up to "all dharmas go": What is the way? Pacifying the dharmas of suffering, such as the sorrow and sickness of the minds of the many realms of beings; and whatever buddhas have previously passed away, and whatever protectors of the world currently abide in the ten directions, by training in this great mantra of awareness, they become the unsurpassed kings of physicians who remove all the suffering of afflictions for themselves and others; and whatever future buddhas engage in conduct endowed with benefit and compassion for sentient beings, they also, having trained in this great mantra of awareness through the three of hearing, thinking, and meditating, or through the ten Dharma activities, become wise and touch enlightenment. Regarding the meaning of "This perfection of wisdom of the Conquerors is the great mantra of awareness": if one asks, "Why is the reason for its merit being so great in that way?" Because by this perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Conquerors, all sentient beings possessing the nature of suffering are led to the state of happiness, and all that happiness of establishing those who are unestablished, one should know to have arisen from this great mantra of awareness. For example, having planted a cause, a seed, it abides in the earth, and the result, a sprout, arises; finding the collection of causes and conditions to be complete, just as the forms of many sprouts are produced; whatever qualities there are of the five perfections at the time of the cause and the three enlightenments at the time of the result, all of those are produced from the perfection of wisdom that does not conceptualize the three spheres. Furthermore, for example, along whatever path a wheel-turning king constantly travels, along that very path the seven precious things such as the wheel, and the assembly of cavalry, infantry, soldiers, and minor forces—that is, all four divisions of the army—travel; likewise, along whatever path this perfection of wisdom, realized and taught by the Conquerors, travels, along that very path all the dharmas of the qualities of abandonment and realization also go.

[2-58] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "The Conqueror to Śakra" up to "take that very one": the Conqueror Buddha asked Śakra, the lord of the gods, "If you were offered this volume of the perfection of wisdom of the Tathāgata and the bodily relics of the Tathāgata, which of those two parts would you take?" In answer to being fully asked that, Śakra said, "If I were offered that part which is the volume, and even if together with that I were offered buddha-fields equaling the number of grains of sand of the river Ganges, all of them fully filled to the brim with the relics of the Conqueror, I would take this very volume of the perfection of wisdom."

source: བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཞེས་པ་ནས། མི་བྱེད་དོ་ཞེས་པའི་བར་གྱིས། ཡང་བཟློག་པ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་བློ་ཆུང་བ་འགའ་ཞིག་གལ་ཏེ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་དོན་ཅི་ལྟ་བ་བཞིན་དུ་སྟོན་པ་དང༌། དེ་བཞིན་དུ་གཟུགས་དང༌། འདུ་ཤེས། ཚོར་བ་དང་སེམས་དཔའ་དང༌། རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་པ་མི་རྟག་པ་དང༌། སྡུག་བསྔལ་བ་དང༌། སྟོང་པ་དང་བདག་མེད་པར་འཛིན་ཅིང༌། གཞན་ལ་ཡང་དེ་ལྟར་ཡོངས་སུ་སྟོན་པ་ནི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་བཅོས་མ་སྤྱོད་པ་སྟེ། དེ་ཅི་ནས་ཡང་དག་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་ཤེས་པའི་མཁས་པ་རྣམས་ནི། དུས་ནམ་དུ་ཡང་ཆོས་རྣམས་འཇིག་པར་མི་བྱེད་དེ་དེ་རང་བཞིན་སྐྱེ་མེད་དུ་ཤེས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །
translation: Regarding this from "bodhisattva" up to "do not": conversely, if some bodhisattva of small mind teaches the meaning of the perfection of wisdom exactly as it is, and likewise apprehends form, perception, feeling, formations, and consciousness as impermanent, suffering, empty, and selfless, and also fully teaches them like that to others, this is practicing a fabricated perfection of wisdom; why is that? because the wise who know the authentic perfection of wisdom never destroy dharmas, as they know them to be birthless by nature.

སེམས་ཅན་ཁམས་མང་ཞེས་པ་ནས། ཆོས་ཀུན་འགྲོ་བར་འགྱུར་ཞེས་པའི་བར་གྱིས། ཚུལ་གང་ཞེ་ན་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་ཁམས་མང་པོའི་སེམས་ཀྱི་མྱ་ངན་དང་ན་ཚ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་གྱི་ཆོས་ཞི་བར་བྱེད་པ་དང༌། སངས་རྒྱས་གང་དག་སྔར་འདས་པ་རྣམས་དང༌། གང་དག་ད་ལྟར་ཕྱོགས་བཅུ་ན་བཞུགས་པའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་མགོན་པོ་རྣམས་རིགས་སྔགས་ཆེན་པོ་འདི་ལ་བསླབས་པས་བདག་གཞན་གྱི་ཉོན་མོངས་ཀྱི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་མཐའ་དག་སེལ་བའི་སྨན་པའི་རྒྱལ་པོ་བླ་ན་མེད་པར་འགྱུར་ལ། མ་འོངས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་གང་དག་སེམས་ཅན་ལ་ཕན་པ་དང་སྙིང་རྗེ་དང་བཅས་པར་སྤྱད་པ་སྤྱོད་པ་དེ་དག་ཀྱང༌། རིགས་སྔགས་ཆེན་མོ་འདི་ལ་ཐོས་བསམ་སྒོམ་གསུམ་གྱིས་སམ་ཆོས་སྤྱོད་བཅུས་བསླབས་ནས་མཁས་པར་གྱུར་པས་བྱང་ཆུབ་ལ་རེག་པར་གྱུར་བ་ཡིན་ནོ། །རྒྱལ་བའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་འདི་རིགས་སྔགས་ཆེ། །ཞེས་པའི་དོན་དེ་ལ། དེ་ལྟར་བསོད་ནམས་ཆེ་བའི་རྒྱུ་མཚན་ཅིས་ཆེ་ན། རྒྱལ་བའི་ཡུམ་ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདི་ཡིས། སེམས་ཅན་སྡུག་བསྔལ་བའི་རང་བཞིན་ཅན། ཐམས་ཅད་བདེ་བའི་གནས་སུ་འདྲེན་པ་དང༌། མ་གྲུབ་པ་རྣམས་གྲུབ་པར་ཡིན་པའི་བདེ་བ་དེ་ཀུན། རིགས་སྔགས་ཆེན་མོ་འདི་ལས་བྱུང་བར་རིག་པར་བྱའོ། །དཔེར་ན་རྒྱུ་ས་བོན་བཏབ་ནས་ས་གཞི་ལ་གནས་ཏེ། འབྲས་བུ་མྱུ་གུ་འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར་བ་སྟེ། རྒྱུ་རྐྱེན་གྱི་ཚོགས་པ་ཚང་བར་སྙེད་ནས་མྱུ་གུ་རྣམས་མང་གི་གཟུགས་དག་རྣམ་པར་སྐྱེ་བ་ལྟར་དུ། རྒྱུའི་དུས་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་དང་འབྲས་བུའི་དུས་ན་བྱང་ཆུབ་གསུམ་གྱི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཇི་སྙེད་ཡོད་པ། དེ་དག་ཀུན་ཀྱང་འཁོར་གསུམ་དུ་མི་རྟོག་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལས་སྐྱེ་བར་འགྱུར་རོ། །ཡང་དཔེར་ན་འཁོར་ལོས་བསྒྱུར་བའི་རྒྱལ་པོ་ལམ་གང་དང་གང་ནས་རྟག་ཏུ་འགྲོ་བའི་ལམ་དེ་དང་དེ་ཉིད་ལས་ནི་འཁོར་ལོ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་རིན་ཆེན་སྣ་བདུན་པོ་དང༌། རྟ་དང་རྐང་ཐང་དང༌། དམག་མི་དང་དཔུང་བུ་ཆུང་གི་ཚོགས་ཏེ། དཔུང་གི་ཚོགས་བཞི་པོ་ཀུན་འགྲོ་བ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ། ལམ་གང་ནས་རྒྱལ་བ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་རྟོགས་ནས་གསུངས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདི་འགྲོ་བ་དེ་ཉིད་ནས་ནི་སྤངས་པ་དང་རྟོགས་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་ཆོས་ཀུན་ཀྱང་འགྲོ་བར་འགྱུར་རོ། །

Regarding this from "Many realms of beings" up to "all dharmas go": What is the way? Pacifying the dharmas of suffering, such as the sorrow and sickness of the minds of the many realms of beings; and whatever buddhas have previously passed away, and whatever protectors of the world currently abide in the ten directions, by training in this great mantra of awareness, they become the unsurpassed kings of physicians who remove all the suffering of afflictions for themselves and others; and whatever future buddhas engage in conduct endowed with benefit and compassion for sentient beings, they also, having trained in this great mantra of awareness through the three of hearing, thinking, and meditating, or through the ten Dharma activities, become wise and touch enlightenment. Regarding the meaning of "This perfection of wisdom of the Conquerors is the great mantra of awareness": if one asks, "Why is the reason for its merit being so great in that way?" Because by this perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Conquerors, all sentient beings possessing the nature of suffering are led to the state of happiness, and all that happiness of establishing those who are unestablished, one should know to have arisen from this great mantra of awareness. For example, having planted a cause, a seed, it abides in the earth, and the result, a sprout, arises; finding the collection of causes and conditions to be complete, just as the forms of many sprouts are produced; whatever qualities there are of the five perfections at the time of the cause and the three enlightenments at the time of the result, all of those are produced from the perfection of wisdom that does not conceptualize the three spheres. Furthermore, for example, along whatever path a wheel-turning king constantly travels, along that very path the seven precious things such as the wheel, and the assembly of cavalry, infantry, soldiers, and minor forces—that is, all four divisions of the army—travel; likewise, along whatever path this perfection of wisdom, realized and taught by the Conquerors, travels, along that very path all the dharmas of the qualities of abandonment and realization also go.

Regarding this from "The Conqueror to Śakra" up to "take that very one": the Conqueror Buddha asked Śakra, the lord of the gods, "If you were offered this volume of the perfection of wisdom of the Tathāgata and the bodily relics of the Tathāgata, which of those two parts would you take?" Regarding this from "Many realms of beings" up to "all dharmas go": What is the way? Pacifying the dharmas of suffering, such as the sorrow and sickness of the minds of the many realms of beings; and whatever buddhas have previously passed away, and whatever protectors of the world currently abide in the ten directions, by training in this great mantra of awareness, they become the unsurpassed kings of physicians who remove all the suffering of afflictions for themselves and others; and whatever future buddhas engage in conduct endowed with benefit and compassion for sentient beings, they also, having trained in this great mantra of awareness through the three of hearing, thinking, and meditating, or through the ten Dharma activities, become wise and touch enlightenment. Regarding the meaning of "This perfection of wisdom of the Conquerors is the great mantra of awareness": if one asks, "Why is the reason for its merit being so great in that way?" Because by this perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Conquerors, all sentient beings possessing the nature of suffering are led to the state of happiness, and all that happiness of establishing those who are unestablished, one should know to have arisen from this great mantra of awareness. For example, having planted a cause, a seed, it abides in the earth, and the result, a sprout, arises; finding the collection of causes and conditions to be complete, just as the forms of many sprouts are produced; whatever qualities there are of the five perfections at the time of the cause and the three enlightenments at the time of the result, all of those are produced from the perfection of wisdom that does not conceptualize the three spheres. Furthermore, for example, along whatever path a wheel-turning king constantly travels, along that very path the seven precious things such as the wheel, and the assembly of cavalry, infantry, soldiers, and minor forces—that is, all four divisions of the army—travel; likewise, along whatever path this perfection of wisdom, realized and taught by the Conquerors, travels, along that very path all the dharmas of the qualities of abandonment and realization also go.

heading: **དོན་དགོད་པ།**
translation: Regarding this from "To whom it is not form" up to "is practicing the supreme perfection": practicing the authentic perfection of wisdom is not that which apprehends form as "permanent" or "impermanent" and so forth. Likewise, it is not apprehending feeling. It does not apprehend perception, does not apprehend consciousness, does not apprehend formations, and just as one thoroughly knows all the dharmas of afflicted saṃsāra and the dharmas of purified nirvāṇa to be from the beginning birthless and empty, teaching it to others as well is practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom.

Regarding this from "Many realms of beings" up to "all dharmas go": What is the way? Pacifying the dharmas of suffering, such as the sorrow and sickness of the minds of the many realms of beings; and whatever buddhas have previously passed away, and whatever protectors of the world currently abide in the ten directions, by training in this great mantra of awareness, they become the unsurpassed kings of physicians who remove all the suffering of afflictions for themselves and others; and whatever future buddhas engage in conduct endowed with benefit and compassion for sentient beings, they also, having trained in this great mantra of awareness through the three of hearing, thinking, and meditating, or through the ten Dharma activities, become wise and touch enlightenment. Regarding the meaning of "This perfection of wisdom of the Conquerors is the great mantra of awareness": if one asks, "Why is the reason for its merit being so great in that way?" Because by this perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Conquerors, all sentient beings possessing the nature of suffering are led to the state of happiness, and all that happiness of establishing those who are unestablished, one should know to have arisen from this great mantra of awareness. For example, having planted a cause, a seed, it abides in the earth, and the result, a sprout, arises; finding the collection of causes and conditions to be complete, just as the forms of many sprouts are produced; whatever qualities there are of the five perfections at the time of the cause and the three enlightenments at the time of the result, all of those are produced from the perfection of wisdom that does not conceptualize the three spheres. Furthermore, for example, along whatever path a wheel-turning king constantly travels, along that very path the seven precious things such as the wheel, and the assembly of cavalry, infantry, soldiers, and minor forces—that is, all four divisions of the army—travel; likewise, along whatever path this perfection of wisdom, realized and taught by the Conquerors, travels, along that very path all the dharmas of the qualities of abandonment and realization also go.

Regarding this from "Many realms of beings" up to "all dharmas go": What is the way? Pacifying the dharmas of suffering, such as the sorrow and sickness of the minds of the many realms of beings; and whatever buddhas have previously passed away, and whatever protectors of the world currently abide in the ten directions, by training in this great mantra of awareness, they become the unsurpassed kings of physicians who remove all the suffering of afflictions for themselves and others; and whatever future buddhas engage in conduct endowed with benefit and compassion for sentient beings, they also, having trained in this great mantra of awareness through the three of hearing, thinking, and meditating, or through the ten Dharma activities, become wise and touch enlightenment. Regarding the meaning of "This perfection of wisdom of the Conquerors is the great mantra of awareness": if one asks, "Why is the reason for its merit being so great in that way?" Because by this perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Conquerors, all sentient beings possessing the nature of suffering are led to the state of happiness, and all that happiness of establishing those who are unestablished, one should know to have arisen from this great mantra of awareness. For example, having planted a cause, a seed, it abides in the earth, and the result, a sprout, arises; finding the collection of causes and conditions to be complete, just as the forms of many sprouts are produced; whatever qualities there are of the five perfections at the time of the cause and the three enlightenments at the time of the result, all of those are produced from the perfection of wisdom that does not conceptualize the three spheres. Furthermore, for example, along whatever path a wheel-turning king constantly travels, along that very path the seven precious things such as the wheel, and the assembly of cavalry, infantry, soldiers, and minor forces—that is, all four divisions of the army—travel; likewise, along whatever path this perfection of wisdom, realized and taught by the Conquerors, travels, along that very path all the dharmas of the qualities of abandonment and realization also go.

translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "if thus" up to "taught by the Victor": contrary to that, one thoroughly understands thus: since these phenomena of what is to be dedicated and the dedication are momentary, they do not remain in the three times but cease, are exhausted, and are non-existent; and the enlightenment into which the dedication is fully dedicated is also exhausted and ceased; and by the virtuous phenomena to be dedicated, in reality, there is never anything to be dedicated to the dedicating phenomena, so they are not dedicated. By thoroughly understanding in that way, one perfectly and fully dedicates without apprehension towards that. Contrary to that, if one makes what is to be dedicated and the dedication into entities and signs, that virtue is not made into a dedication; whereas if there is no sign of grasping at it as a self, it is made into a dedication for enlightenment. How is it if one dedicates with apprehension? For example, when eating good food mixed with poison, although the taste is delicious at the time of the cause, it generates suffering at the time of digestion or at the time of the result. Similarly, apprehending white phenomena is like eating poisonous food: although it is joyful at the time of the cause, it is taught by the Victor that, because it is with apprehension, it generates the suffering of saṃsāra.

translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "therefore, thus" up to "thus fully dedicate": therefore, one should train in fully dedicating in that way. translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "thus merit" up to "outshines all": if one fully dedicates for enlightenment without apprehension those merits of rejoicing in that way without apprehension, one is without the poison of apprehension, and by practicing according to the teachings, one does not abandon the Buddha and also speaks to others just as the Victor has taught. translation: without a guide" up to "like not receiving wages": like the example of a person blind from birth, if there is no actual wisdom of non-apprehension, one lacks the eyes to go to the stage of buddhahood, and therefore these five perfections, generosity and so forth, lack the guide of wisdom to lead them, so they are not able to reach the result of enlightenment. Whenever one is perfectly embraced by the actual perfection of wisdom of non-apprehension, at that time one gains eyes and also attains the name "perfection." The example for not attaining the result if the eyes of wisdom are lacking, even if other virtues are complete, is, for instance, a painting being fully completed but lacking the pupils of the eyes. This example means that, just as long as the pupils of the eyes are not completed, the deity painter does not receive their wages.

heading: **རྣམ་དཔྱོད་ཀྱི་རིག་པ་ཡིན་པར་བསྟན་པ།**
translation: Regarding this from "when conditioned" up to "does not practice": If one asks, what is the nature of that wisdom? Whenever conditioned saṃsāra and unconditioned nirvāṇa, and all white virtuous and black non-virtuous phenomena, are broken down by the intellect of wisdom that investigates the ultimate, and upon searching one does not apprehend even a mere sub-atomic particle, at that time, because one realizes that ultimately nothing is established, one goes to the count of what is called the "perfection of wisdom" in the worlds. In that way, the example for how the intellect does not dwell on any object whatsoever is somewhat like how space does not dwell on anything whatsoever. If, contrary to that, a bodhisattva thinks, 'I shall practice the perfection of wisdom that the Victors have realized and taught, and I shall liberate many ten millions of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings who are afflicted and touch suffering,' and that being perceives self and sentient beings as separate and fully conceptually grasps them as true, then, because this is with apprehension, they 'do not practice' the supreme perfection of wisdom.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "if thus" up to "taught by the Victor": contrary to that, one thoroughly understands thus: since these phenomena of what is to be dedicated and the dedication are momentary, they do not remain in the three times but cease, are exhausted, and are non-existent; and the enlightenment into which the dedication is fully dedicated is also exhausted and ceased; and by the virtuous phenomena to be dedicated, in reality, there is never anything to be dedicated to the dedicating phenomena, so they are not dedicated. By thoroughly understanding in that way, one perfectly and fully dedicates without apprehension towards that. Contrary to that, if one makes what is to be dedicated and the dedication into entities and signs, that virtue is not made into a dedication; whereas if there is no sign of grasping at it as a self, it is made into a dedication for enlightenment. How is it if one dedicates with apprehension? For example, when eating good food mixed with poison, although the taste is delicious at the time of the cause, it generates suffering at the time of digestion or at the time of the result. Similarly, apprehending white phenomena is like eating poisonous food: although it is joyful at the time of the cause, it is taught by the Victor that, because it is with apprehension, it generates the suffering of saṃsāra.

heading: **སྦྱངས་པའི་དད་པ་ཡིན་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "bodhisattva" up to "would be unfit": if, as a cause, some bodhisattva previously practiced the practice of the mind of enlightenment, was skilled in practicing the path of the perfections, and had no doubt regarding realization, then in this life too, as soon as they hear the perfection of wisdom, they generate the perception thinking, 'That mind of enlightenment is my teacher,' and as the result they will swiftly realize peaceful enlightenment. Contrary to that, when practicing the previous practice, even if they performed the virtue of serving and honoring ten million hundred thousand buddhas, if they lacked faith in the essence, the Mother of the Victors, the perfection of wisdom, and so did not listen to it, then in this life when they listen to it being taught and hear it, that person of small intellect, lacking faith, abandons it, saying, 'This is not the word of the Buddha.' Having abandoned it, becoming without opportunity for another antidote, as a result they will go to the Avīci hell. In summary, therefore, if you wish to touch and attain the supreme pristine wisdom of the Buddha, generate faith in this Mother of the Victors! If one does not generate faith in this, what is the example like? For example, it is like a merchant going to an island of jewels but returning back without having found any jewels.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "if thus" up to "taught by the Victor": contrary to that, one thoroughly understands thus: since these phenomena of what is to be dedicated and the dedication are momentary, they do not remain in the three times but cease, are exhausted, and are non-existent; and the enlightenment into which the dedication is fully dedicated is also exhausted and ceased; and by the virtuous phenomena to be dedicated, in reality, there is never anything to be dedicated to the dedicating phenomena, so they are not dedicated. By thoroughly understanding in that way, one perfectly and fully dedicates without apprehension towards that. Contrary to that, if one makes what is to be dedicated and the dedication into entities and signs, that virtue is not made into a dedication; whereas if there is no sign of grasping at it as a self, it is made into a dedication for enlightenment. How is it if one dedicates with apprehension? For example, when eating good food mixed with poison, although the taste is delicious at the time of the cause, it generates suffering at the time of digestion or at the time of the result. Similarly, apprehending white phenomena is like eating poisonous food: although it is joyful at the time of the cause, it is taught by the Victor that, because it is with apprehension, it generates the suffering of saṃsāra.

without a guide" up to "like not receiving wages": like the example of a person blind from birth, if there is no actual wisdom of non-apprehension, one lacks the eyes to go to the stage of buddhahood, and therefore these five perfections, generosity and so forth, lack the guide of wisdom to lead them, so they are not able to reach the result of enlightenment. Whenever one is perfectly embraced by the actual perfection of wisdom of non-apprehension, at that time one gains eyes and also attains the name "perfection." The example for not attaining the result if the eyes of wisdom are lacking, even if other virtues are complete, is, for instance, a painting being fully completed but lacking the pupils of the eyes. This example means that, just as long as the pupils of the eyes are not completed, the deity painter does not receive their wages.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "if thus" up to "taught by the Victor": contrary to that, one thoroughly understands thus: since these phenomena of what is to be dedicated and the dedication are momentary, they do not remain in the three times but cease, are exhausted, and are non-existent; and the enlightenment into which the dedication is fully dedicated is also exhausted and ceased; and by the virtuous phenomena to be dedicated, in reality, there is never anything to be dedicated to the dedicating phenomena, so they are not dedicated. By thoroughly understanding in that way, one perfectly and fully dedicates without apprehension towards that. Contrary to that, if one makes what is to be dedicated and the dedication into entities and signs, that virtue is not made into a dedication; whereas if there is no sign of grasping at it as a self, it is made into a dedication for enlightenment. How is it if one dedicates with apprehension? For example, when eating good food mixed with poison, although the taste is delicious at the time of the cause, it generates suffering at the time of digestion or at the time of the result. Similarly, apprehending white phenomena is like eating poisonous food: although it is joyful at the time of the cause, it is taught by the Victor that, because it is with apprehension, it generates the suffering of saṃsāra.

without a guide" up to "like not receiving wages": like the example of a person blind from birth, if there is no actual wisdom of non-apprehension, one lacks the eyes to go to the stage of buddhahood, and therefore these five perfections, generosity and so forth, lack the guide of wisdom to lead them, so they are not able to reach the result of enlightenment. translation: Regarding this from "purity of form" up to "indivisible and uncuttable": the object of wisdom is the lack of nature of all phenomena; the object is to be known as the purity of form and the pure results of the four pairs of persons. Thus, it is taught that the four pure results are the example, and the pure subject form and the pure result of the Mahāyāna, omniscience, are pure. Thus, the example for there being no difference among those three—the purity of omniscience, the purity of the four results, and the purity of the subject form—is that they are like the element of space: indivisible in entity and also uncuttable into distinctions by the intellect. Thus it is said: Regarding this from "if thus" up to "taught by the Victor": contrary to that, one thoroughly understands thus: since these phenomena of what is to be dedicated and the dedication are momentary, they do not remain in the three times but cease, are exhausted, and are non-existent; and the enlightenment into which the dedication is fully dedicated is also exhausted and ceased; and by the virtuous phenomena to be dedicated, in reality, there is never anything to be dedicated to the dedicating phenomena, so they are not dedicated. By thoroughly understanding in that way, one perfectly and fully dedicates without apprehension towards that. Contrary to that, if one makes what is to be dedicated and the dedication into entities and signs, that virtue is not made into a dedication; whereas if there is no sign of grasping at it as a self, it is made into a dedication for enlightenment. How is it if one dedicates with apprehension? For example, when eating good food mixed with poison, although the taste is delicious at the time of the cause, it generates suffering at the time of digestion or at the time of the result. Similarly, apprehending white phenomena is like eating poisonous food: although it is joyful at the time of the cause, it is taught by the Victor that, because it is with apprehension, it generates the suffering of saṃsāra.

without a guide" up to "like not receiving wages": like the example of a person blind from birth, if there is no actual wisdom of non-apprehension, one lacks the eyes to go to the stage of buddhahood, and therefore these five perfections, generosity and so forth, lack the guide of wisdom to lead them, so they are not able to reach the result of enlightenment. heading: **རྟོགས་བྱ་ཡུམ་གྱི་རང་བཞིན།**
translation: The essence of the third topic, the knowledge of the bases that knows all, is the realization of the non-apprehension of the phenomena of the aggregates, elements, and sense sources, which have become the supports for the basis and path. Because it is the basis for the arising of superimpositions and the basis for the cutting of superimpositions, it is called the knowledge of the bases. Because it cuts the root of the bases by appropriately realizing the two forms of selflessness, it is the knowledge of the bases. Regarding this, out of two aspects, the pitfall or discordant class is the knowledge of the bases of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and by illustrating and teaching its antidote to be the knowledge of the bases of the Mahāyāna, one practices in the manner of cutting off the pitfall of the inferior vehicle. There are nine phenomena that illustrate this; moreover, as it says, "Through knowledge one does not dwell in existence, / and through compassion one does not dwell in peace; / the discordant class and their antidotes, / application and its equality, / and the path of seeing of the śrāvakas and so forth; / such is asserted as the very knowledge of all." Through this, these subdivisions by minor topics are also incidentally complete; they should be known extensively elsewhere.

without a guide" up to "like not receiving wages": like the example of a person blind from birth, if there is no actual wisdom of non-apprehension, one lacks the eyes to go to the stage of buddhahood, and therefore these five perfections, generosity and so forth, lack the guide of wisdom to lead them, so they are not able to reach the result of enlightenment. Whenever one is perfectly embraced by the actual perfection of wisdom of non-apprehension, at that time one gains eyes and also attains the name "perfection." The example for not attaining the result if the eyes of wisdom are lacking, even if other virtues are complete, is, for instance, a painting being fully completed but lacking the pupils of the eyes. This example means that, just as long as the pupils of the eyes are not completed, the deity painter does not receive their wages.

Regarding this from "when conditioned" up to "does not practice": If one asks, what is the nature of that wisdom? Whenever conditioned saṃsāra and unconditioned nirvāṇa, and all white virtuous and black non-virtuous phenomena, are broken down by the intellect of wisdom that investigates the ultimate, and upon searching one does not apprehend even a mere sub-atomic particle, at that time, because one realizes that ultimately nothing is established, one goes to the count of what is called the "perfection of wisdom" in the worlds. In that way, the example for how the intellect does not dwell on any object whatsoever is somewhat like how space does not dwell on anything whatsoever. If, contrary to that, a bodhisattva thinks, 'I shall practice the perfection of wisdom that the Victors have realized and taught, and I shall liberate many ten millions of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings who are afflicted and touch suffering,' and that being perceives self and sentient beings as separate and fully conceptually grasps them as true, then, because this is with apprehension, they 'do not practice' the supreme perfection of wisdom.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "bodhisattva" up to "would be unfit": if, as a cause, some bodhisattva previously practiced the practice of the mind of enlightenment, was skilled in practicing the path of the perfections, and had no doubt regarding realization, then in this life too, as soon as they hear the perfection of wisdom, they generate the perception thinking, 'That mind of enlightenment is my teacher,' and as the result they will swiftly realize peaceful enlightenment. Contrary to that, when practicing the previous practice, even if they performed the virtue of serving and honoring ten million hundred thousand buddhas, if they lacked faith in the essence, the Mother of the Victors, the perfection of wisdom, and so did not listen to it, then in this life when they listen to it being taught and hear it, that person of small intellect, lacking faith, abandons it, saying, 'This is not the word of the Buddha.' Having abandoned it, becoming without opportunity for another antidote, as a result they will go to the Avīci hell. In summary, therefore, if you wish to touch and attain the supreme pristine wisdom of the Buddha, generate faith in this Mother of the Victors! If one does not generate faith in this, what is the example like? For example, it is like a merchant going to an island of jewels but returning back without having found any jewels.

Work: འཕགས་པ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་སྡུད་པ་ཚིགས་སུ་བཅད་པའི་ཊཱི་ཀ་ཡིད་བཞིན་གྱི་ནོར་བུ་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་ལྟ་བུ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་རྒྱ་མཚོའི་སྡེ། (Commentaries on the Short Prajnaparamita Sutras:The Ocean of Perfection.), author: null. དམིགས་བུ་མེད་ཞེས་པ་ནས། རྔན་པ་མི་ཐོབ་བཞིན་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། དམུས་ལོང་གི་དཔེ་བཞིན་དུ་དངོས་གཞི་མི་དམིགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་མེད་ན་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སར་འགྲོ་བའི་མིག་མེད་པས་སྦྱིན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་པོ་འདི་དག་ལ། རྗེས་སུ་འཁྲིད་པའི་དམིགས་བུ་ཤེས་རབ་མེད་པས་འབྲས་བུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་ལ་རེག་པར་ནུས་པ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །གང་གི་ཚེ་དངོས་གཞི་མི་དམིགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པས་ནི། རབ་ཏུ་ཟིན་པར་གྱུར་བ་དེའི་ཚེ་མིག་སྙེད་པར་འགྱུར་ཞིང་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་མིང་ཡང་འཐོབ་བོ། །དགེ་བ་གཞན་ཚང་ཡང་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་མིག་མེད་ན་འབྲས་བུ་མི་འཐོབ་པའི་དཔེ་ནི། དཔེར་ན་རི་མོའི་ལས་ནི་ཡོངས་སུ་ཟིན་ཀྱང་མིག་འབྲས་མེད་པ་དཔེ་ནི། ཇི་སྲིད་དུ་མིག་འབྲས་མ་ཐོབ་ཀྱི་བར་དུ་ལྷ་བཟོ་བས་རྔན་པ་མི་འཐོབ་པ་བཞིན་ནོ། །
[2-82] translation already produced for this document:
without a guide" up to "like not receiving wages": like the example of a person blind from birth, if there is no actual wisdom of non-apprehension, one lacks the eyes to go to the stage of buddhahood, and therefore these five perfections, generosity and so forth, lack the guide of wisdom to lead them, so they are not able to reach the result of enlightenment. Whenever one is perfectly embraced by the actual perfection of wisdom of non-apprehension, at that time one gains eyes and also attains the name "perfection." The example for not attaining the result if the eyes of wisdom are lacking, even if other virtues are complete, is, for instance, a painting being fully completed but lacking the pupils of the eyes. This example means that, just as long as the pupils of the eyes are not completed, the deity painter does not receive their wages.

[2-84] source:
གང་ཚེ་འདུ་བྱས་ཞེས་པ་ནས། སྤྱོད་མ་ཡིན་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། འོ་ན་ཤེས་རབ་དེའི་རང་བཞིན་གང་ཞེ་ན་གང་གི་ཚེ་འདུ་བྱས་འཁོར་བ་དང་འདུས་མ་བྱས་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ་དང༌། དཀར་པོ་དགེ་བ་དང་ནག་པོ་མི་དགེ་བའི་ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་མཐར་ཐུག་དཔྱོད་པའི་བློ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་རྣམ་པར་བཤིག་ནས་བཙལ་ན་རྡུལ་ཕྲ་རབ་ཙམ་མི་དམིགས་པ་དེའི་ཚེ། དོན་དམ་ཅི་ཡང་མ་གྲུབ་པར་རྟོགས་པས་འཇིག་རྟེན་དག་ན་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་གྲངས་སུ་འགྲོའོ། །དེ་ལྟར་བློ་ཡུལ་ཅི་ལ་ཡང་མི་གནས་པའི་དཔེ་ནམ་མཁའ་གང་ལ་ཡང་མི་གནས་པར་ཅུང་ཟད་དེ་དང་འདྲའོ། །གལ་ཏེ་དེ་ལས་གཞན་དུ་ན་བདག་ནི་རྒྱལ་བ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་རྟོགས་ནས་གསུངས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་སྤྱད་པར་བྱ་ཞིང༌། སེམས་ཅན་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལ་རེག་ཅིང་ཉམས་ཐག་པ་བྱེ་བ་ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་མང་པོ་གྲོལ་བར་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་བདག་དང་སེམས་ཅན་ཐ་དད་དུ་འདུ་ཤེས་ཤིང་བདེན་པར་ཡོངས་སུ་རྟོག་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སྟེ། འདི་ནི་དམིགས་པ་དང་བཅས་པས་ན་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་མཆོག་ལ་སྤྱོད་པ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །
[2-84] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "when conditioned" up to "does not practice": If one asks, what is the nature of that wisdom? Whenever conditioned saṃsāra and unconditioned nirvāṇa, and all white virtuous and black non-virtuous phenomena, are broken down by the intellect of wisdom that investigates the ultimate, and upon searching one does not apprehend even a mere sub-atomic particle, at that time, because one realizes that ultimately nothing is established, one goes to the count of what is called the "perfection of wisdom" in the worlds. In that way, the example for how the intellect does not dwell on any object whatsoever is somewhat like how space does not dwell on anything whatsoever. If, contrary to that, a bodhisattva thinks, 'I shall practice the perfection of wisdom that the Victors have realized and taught, and I shall liberate many ten millions of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings who are afflicted and touch suffering,' and that being perceives self and sentient beings as separate and fully conceptually grasps them as true, then, because this is with apprehension, they 'do not practice' the supreme perfection of wisdom.

[2-85] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཞེས་པ་ནས། གྱུར་ན་མི་རུང་ངོ་ཞེས་པའི་བར་གྱིས། རྒྱུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གང་ལ་ལ་ཞིག་སྔོན་ཆད་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་སེམས་སྤྱད་པར་སྤྱོད་པའི་ཚེ་ན། ལམ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་སྤྱོད་པ་ལ་མཁས་ཤིང་རྟོགས་པ་ལ་སོམ་ཉི་མེད་པ་ལ། ཚེ་འདིར་ཡང་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ཐོས་མ་ཐག་ཏུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་སེམས་དེ་ནི་བདག་གི་སྟོན་པ་ཡིན་ནོ་སྙམ་པའི་འདུ་ཤེས་བསྐྱེད་ལ། འབྲས་བུ་དེས་ནི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཞི་བར་མྱུར་དུ་རྟོགས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །དེ་ལས་བཟློག་པ་སྔོན་སྤྱད་པ་སྤྱོད་པའི་ཚེ་ན། སངས་རྒྱས་བྱེ་བ་ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་ལ་བསྙེན་བཀུར་གྱི་དགེ་བ་བྱས་ཀྱང༌། ངོ་བོ་རྒྱལ་བའི་ཡུམ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་མ་དད་པས་མ་ཉན་ན། ཚེ་འདིར་འཆད་པ་ལ་ཉན་པས་ཐོས་ནས་བློ་ཆུང་དེ་ཡིས་མ་དད་པ་འདི་ནི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་བཀའ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །ཞེས་སྤོང་བར་བྱེད་དེ། སྤངས་ནས་གཉེན་པོ་གཞན་གྱི་སྐབས་མེད་པར་གྱུར་པ་དེ་ནི་འབྲས་བུ་མནར་མེད་པའི་དམྱལ་བར་འགྲོའོ། །དོན་བསྡུ་བ་དེ་ལྟ་བས་ན་གལ་ཏེ་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཡེ་ཤེས་མཆོག་ལ་རེག་ཅིང་ཐོབ་པར་འདོད་ན་རྒྱལ་བའི་ཡུམ་འདིར་དད་པར་གྱིས་ཤིག འདི་ལ་དད་པར་མ་བྱས་ན་དཔེ་ཅི་དང་འདྲ་ན། དཔེར་ན་ཚོང་པ་རིན་ཆེན་གླིང་དུ་སོང་ནས་ནོར་བུ་མ་རྙེད་པར་སླར་ལོག་པ་ལྟ་བུའོ། །
[2-85] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding this from "bodhisattva" up to "would be unfit": if, as a cause, some bodhisattva previously practiced the practice of the mind of enlightenment, was skilled in practicing the path of the perfections, and had no doubt regarding realization, then in this life too, as soon as they hear the perfection of wisdom, they generate the perception thinking, 'That mind of enlightenment is my teacher,' and as the result they will swiftly realize peaceful enlightenment. Contrary to that, when practicing the previous practice, even if they performed the virtue of serving and honoring ten million hundred thousand buddhas, if they lacked faith in the essence, the Mother of the Victors, the perfection of wisdom, and so did not listen to it, then in this life when they listen to it being taught and hear it, that person of small intellect, lacking faith, abandons it, saying, 'This is not the word of the Buddha.' Having abandoned it, becoming without opportunity for another antidote, as a result they will go to the Avīci hell. In summary, therefore, if you wish to touch and attain the supreme pristine wisdom of the Buddha, generate faith in this Mother of the Victors! If one does not generate faith in this, what is the example like? For example, it is like a merchant going to an island of jewels but returning back without having found any jewels.

[2-87] source:
གཟུགས་ཀྱི་དག་པ་ཞེས་པ་ནས། དབྱེར་མེད་གཅད་དུ་མེད་ཞེས་བར་ལ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཡུལ་ནི་ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་རང་བཞིན་མེད་པ་སྟེ། ཡུལ་ནི་གཟུགས་ཀྱི་དག་པ་སྐྱེས་བུ་ཟུང་བཞི་འབྲས་བུ་དག་དང་རིག་པར་བྱའོ། །དེ་ལྟར་འབྲས་བུ་བཞི་དག་དཔེ་དང་ཆོས་ཅན་གཟུགས་དག་པ་དང༌། ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་འབྲས་བུ་ཐམས་ཅད་མཁྱེན་པ་ཉིད་དག་པར་གསུངས་ལ། དེ་ལྟར་ཐམས་ཅད་མཁྱེན་པ་ཉིད་དག་པ་དང༌། འབྲས་བུ་བཞི་དག་པ་དང་ཆོས་ཅན་གཟུགས་དག་པ་གསུམ་པོ་ལ་ཐ་དད་མེད་པའི་དཔེ་ནི། ནམ་མཁའི་ཁམས་དང་མཚུངས་ཏེ་དངོས་པོ་ལ་དབྱེར་མེད་ཅིང་བློས་ཀྱང་ཐ་དད་དུ་གཅད་དུ་མེད་དོ། །དེ་ཡན་ཆད་ཀྱི་ལམ་ཤེས་བཤད་ནས།

Regarding this from "purity of form" up to "indivisible and uncuttable": the object of wisdom is the lack of nature of all phenomena; the object is to be known as the purity of form and the pure results of the four pairs of persons. Thus, it is taught that the four pure results are the example, and the pure subject form and the pure result of the Mahāyāna, omniscience, are pure. Thus, the example for there being no difference among those three—the purity of omniscience, the purity of the four results, and the purity of the subject form—is that they are like the element of space: indivisible in entity and also uncuttable into distinctions by the intellect. Having explained knowledge of the path up to that point,

heading: **སྲིད་ཞིའི་མཐའ་ལ་མི་གནས་པ།**
translation: Regarding this from "how the hero practices" up to "moves about": Moreover, by the power of the hero, the bodhisattva, practicing in whatever way through various methods, and of the perfection of wisdom, they have perfectly transcended the two afflictions that are the causes of the three realms, yet they are not liberated in the manner of the one-sided peace of the śrāvakas. Even though the afflictions of ignorance and views are eliminated, without abandoning even the mere contaminants of desire and craving, they demonstrate birth through skillful means. Likewise for the example, even though they lack aging, sickness, and death, they demonstrate dying and transmigrating and so forth in the perception of the beings to be tamed. These wandering beings who lack such wisdom are attached to the aggregates that are the basis of name, namely the four of feeling, perception, formation, and consciousness, and the aggregate of form—they are attached to those which are like the mud of the five aggregates, difficult to emerge from. For example, just as a continuous bucket water-wheel is moved by the wind, the meaning is that they wander again and again in the wheel of saṃsāra, in the three realms and the six classes of beings. Knowing that those wanderers who are mistaken about the path do not escape from saṃsāra because they are caught in the snare of the four rivers, similarly to the example of a deer caught in a snare that does not escape, the one endowed with the wisdom that knows non-apprehension "moves about" without adhering to or depending upon anything whatsoever, like a bird flying in the sky.

Whenever conditioned saṃsāra and unconditioned nirvāṇa, and all white virtuous and black non-virtuous phenomena, are broken down by the intellect of wisdom that investigates the ultimate, and upon searching one does not apprehend even a mere sub-atomic particle, at that time, because one realizes that ultimately nothing is established, one goes to the count of what is called the "perfection of wisdom" in the worlds. Thus it is said: Regarding this from "bodhisattva" up to "would be unfit": if, as a cause, some bodhisattva previously practiced the practice of the mind of enlightenment, was skilled in practicing the path of the perfections, and had no doubt regarding realization, then in this life too, as soon as they hear the perfection of wisdom, they generate the perception thinking, 'That mind of enlightenment is my teacher,' and as the result they will swiftly realize peaceful enlightenment. Contrary to that, when practicing the previous practice, even if they performed the virtue of serving and honoring ten million hundred thousand buddhas, if they lacked faith in the essence, the Mother of the Victors, the perfection of wisdom, and so did not listen to it, then in this life when they listen to it being taught and hear it, that person of small intellect, lacking faith, abandons it, saying, 'This is not the word of the Buddha.' Having abandoned it, becoming without opportunity for another antidote, as a result they will go to the Avīci hell. In summary, therefore, if you wish to touch and attain the supreme pristine wisdom of the Buddha, generate faith in this Mother of the Victors! If one does not generate faith in this, what is the example like? For example, it is like a merchant going to an island of jewels but returning back without having found any jewels.

heading: **གནས་པའི་མཐའ་འགག་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "perfectly pure practice" up to "goes without attachment": if some bodhisattva with perfectly pure practice does not practice by adhering to the object of form, and similarly does not practice by way of adhering to consciousness, perception, feeling, and volition, then practicing in that way without adherence completely abandons all attachment and aversion, and that intellect going away from attachment and adherence is the Sugatas' practice of wisdom. Practicing in that way by way of not adhering to the five aggregates as appearing to be true, that bodhisattva is skilled because they possess the momentum of training, and being brilliant by realizing the meaning, having severed attachment and adherence from their own continuum, they "go" to the stage of buddhahood without attachment and adherence even to the wandering beings of the three realms.

without a guide" up to "like not receiving wages": like the example of a person blind from birth, if there is no actual wisdom of non-apprehension, one lacks the eyes to go to the stage of buddhahood, and therefore these five perfections, generosity and so forth, lack the guide of wisdom to lead them, so they are not able to reach the result of enlightenment. Regarding this from "when conditioned" up to "does not practice": If one asks, what is the nature of that wisdom? Whenever conditioned saṃsāra and unconditioned nirvāṇa, and all white virtuous and black non-virtuous phenomena, are broken down by the intellect of wisdom that investigates the ultimate, and upon searching one does not apprehend even a mere sub-atomic particle, at that time, because one realizes that ultimately nothing is established, one goes to the count of what is called the "perfection of wisdom" in the worlds. In that way, the example for how the intellect does not dwell on any object whatsoever is somewhat like how space does not dwell on anything whatsoever. Thus it is said: Regarding this from "bodhisattva" up to "would be unfit": if, as a cause, some bodhisattva previously practiced the practice of the mind of enlightenment, was skilled in practicing the path of the perfections, and had no doubt regarding realization, then in this life too, as soon as they hear the perfection of wisdom, they generate the perception thinking, 'That mind of enlightenment is my teacher,' and as the result they will swiftly realize peaceful enlightenment. Having abandoned it, becoming without opportunity for another antidote, as a result they will go to the Avīci hell. In summary, therefore, if you wish to touch and attain the supreme pristine wisdom of the Buddha, generate faith in this Mother of the Victors! heading: **ཇི་ལྟར་རྟོགས་པའི་རྣམ་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "the sun freed from the planet Rāhu" up to "is the supreme practice of the perfection": the example for dispelling the darkness of ignorance and burning the apprehension of entities is: for instance, when the sun is freed from the eclipse of the planet Rāhu, having overpowered the darkness, its light remains brightly shining; and just as things to be burned—grass, wood, forests, and so forth—are burned when a fire is started, similarly, even though all phenomena, the thoroughly afflictive and the antidotal perfectly pure, are pure by nature, so that they are perfectly pure also for the intellect, that bodhisattva looks by relying on the perfection of wisdom that knows the path as non-apprehensible; thereby, without apprehending the agent bodhisattva, one also does not apprehend any of the phenomena of the object to be looked at and the manner of looking. Thus, this knowing of the non-apprehension of the three spheres is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
