Thus it is said: Regarding this from "for example, a monk" up to "there is no fatigue": just like the example of the monk, the learned bodhisattva dwelling in emptiness, the dharmatā that is like space, and having perfected the miraculous ability of pristine wisdom, just as there is no aspect of an objective basis, although demonstrating limitless kinds of activities by the method of working for the benefit of migrators, and although dwelling in saṃsāra for a long time, ten million eons, has no weariness in the mind and has no fatigue even in the body.

[2-184] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་མི་འགའ་ཞེས་པ་ནས། ཆོས་ཀྱང་མཐོང་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། སྐྱེས་བུས་གདུགས་བཟུང་བའི་དཔེས་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དང་ལྡན་པས་མཁས་པ་སྙིང་རྗེ་གནས་པ་དེ་ཡང༌། ཐབས་སྙིང་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོ་དང་ཤེས་རབ་མི་དམིགས་པར་ཤེས་པ་གཉིས་ཀྱིས་གདུགས་གཉིས་ཡོངས་སུ་བཟུང་སྟེ་གང་ཞེ་ན། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་ཉོན་མོངས་འཁོར་བའི་ཆོས་དང་རྣམ་བྱང་གི་ཆོས་རྣམས་རང་རང་གི་ངོ་བོས་སྟོང་པའི་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་དུ་རྒྱུ་སྟོང་པའི་མཚན་མ་མེད་པ་དང་འབྲས་བུས་སྟོང་པའི་སྨོན་པ་མེད་པ་ལ་རྟོག་ཅིང༌། ཐབས་སྙིང་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོ་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ་ལ་རེག་པ་མེད་ལ་ཆོས་རྣམས་ཀྱི་དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད་ཀྱང་མཐོང་ངོ༌། །
[2-184] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding this from "for example, some person" up to "also sees phenomena": just like the example of a person holding an umbrella, that learned bodhisattva endowed with dwelling in compassion, furthermore, thoroughly holds the two umbrellas by way of the two: the method of great compassion and the wisdom knowing non-apprehension; if one asks what they are: by wisdom, they examine the phenomena of afflicted saṃsāra and the phenomena of complete purification as the emptiness empty of their respective intrinsic natures, the signlessness of empty causes, and the wishlessness of empty results, and by the method of great compassion, they do not touch nirvāṇa, and also see the suchness of phenomena.

heading: **ལུང་བསྟན་ཐོབ་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Moreover, if seeing a burning city in a dream or while awake, they say, "by the blessing of the truth of the nature of phenomena, may these heaps of fire be pacified," and they are pacified, that bodhisattva should be known as having been prophesied as irreversible.

ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། གང་ཚེ་འགྲོ་ལ་བྱམས་ཞེས་པ་ནས། གནས་མེད་དོ་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། གང་ཞིག་གི་ཚེ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་འགྲོ་བ་ལ་བྱམས་པ་ཆེན་པོས་རྒྱུན་དུ་རྗེས་སུ་འབྲེལ་བར་བྱས་ནས་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་དང་མཚན་མ་མེད་པ་དང་སྨོན་པ་མེད་པ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པ་དེ་ནི་མཐའ་གཉིས་དང་བྲལ་བས་ཞི་བ་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ་ཐོབ་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །ཞི་བ་འམ་སྲིད་པ་འདུས་མ་བྱས་ལ་གནས་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །ཞེས་བྱ་བར་གདམས་པར་ནུས་པ་དེ་ནི་གནས་དང་སྐབས་མེད་དོ། །

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "at whatever time, loving migrators" up to "there is no occasion": at whatever time the bodhisattva engages in the samādhis of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness having continuously followed up with great love for migrators, since they are free from the two extremes, being able to instruct saying, "they will attain the peace of nirvāṇa, or they dwell in unconditioned peace or existence," is without basis and occasion.

[2-188] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་སྒྱུ་མས་སྤྲུལ་པའི་མི་ལུས་ལ་དངོས་པོ་མེད་ཀྱང་མི་སྣང་བ་མ་ཡིན་ཞིང༌། དེ་ལ་ནི་སྐྱེས་པ་དང་བུད་མེད་ཀྱི་མིང་གིས་ཀྱང་ནི་གདགས་པར་ནུས་པ་ལྟར་དུ། དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་བློས་རྣམ་པར་ཐར་པའི་སྒོ་གསུམ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པ། དེ་ལ་སྲིད་ཞིའི་མིང་གིས་ཀྱང་མིང་གདགས་པར་ནུས་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །དེ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་འབྲས་བུ་སྨོན་པ་ནས་བཟུང་ནས་བསླབ་པའི་རིམ་པ་སོང་ནས།

Thus it is said: For example, although an illusory emanated human body has no real entity, it is not that it does not appear, and just as one is able to designate it with the names of man and woman, just like that example, for the bodhisattva's mind engaging in the three doors of liberation, one is able to designate it with the names of existence and peace too. Having gone through the stages of training starting from the aspiration for those results,

[2-189] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ།

[2-190] source:
གལ་ཏེ་སྤྱོད་པ་དང་ནི་ཞེས་པ་ནས། རིག་པར་བྱ་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། གལ་ཏེ་གཞན་དག་གིས་ཕྱིར་མི་ལྡོག་པ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པ་དང་ནི་དབང་པོ་དང༌། རྟགས་ཇི་ལྟ་བུ་འོང་པ་ལགས་ཞེས་ཡོངས་སུ་དྲིས་པ་ལ། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་རང་གི་མྱོང་བ་དང་སྟོང་པའི་སྟོང་པ་དང་མཚན་མ་མེད་པའི་ཆོས་ཀྱང་ཡོངས་སུ་མི་སྟོན་པ་ལ་ཕྱིར་ལྡོག་པའི་རྟགས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་དྲིས་ཀྱང་མི་འཆད་པ་དེ་ནི་སྔར་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱིས་ལུང་མ་བསྟན་པ་ཡིན་པར་རིག་པར་བྱའོ། །དེ་ཡན་ཆད་ཀྱིས་རྣམ་ཀུན་མངོན་རྫོགས་བཤད་ཟིན་ཏོ།།
[2-190] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "if engaging" up to "should be known": if others thoroughly ask, "if engaging in irreversibility, what kind of faculties and signs come about?", the bodhisattva who does not thoroughly teach their own experience and the phenomena of the emptiness of emptiness and signlessness, and who even when asked about the phenomena of the signs of reversibility does not explain them, should be known as one who was not prophesied by the Buddha previously. heading: **ལུང་བསྟན་ཐོབ་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Moreover, for humans or migrators who have many infectious diseases such as those caused by gods, nāgas, and spirits in some human worlds, since that bodhisattva is endowed with helpfulness and compassion, by expressing the blessing of truth they are completely pacified. Regarding that, nevertheless, the bodhisattva person who does not have the conceit of thinking, "I am endowed with blessings," and in whom no pride is generated, should be known as having been prophesied as irreversible.

heading: **མིང་གི་གཞི།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "from the basis of the name" up to "this is the name": the way Māra prophesies is that in order to look for an opportunity from the basis of the name, Māra approaches that bodhisattva and speaks these words: "Accordingly, here, these are the names of your father and mother, up to your wife and lineage. And just as you have thought, whenever you become a Buddha, this will be your name, Candraprabha." The person who has conceit thinking that is of little intelligence.

ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ་དང་ཞེས་པ་ནས། རིག་པར་བྱ་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། ཐེག་པ་དམན་པ་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པའི་ས་དང་རྐྱེན་གྱི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཡེ་ཤེས་དང༌། ཁམས་གསུམ་གྱི་དཔལ་འབྱོར་དག་ན་རྨི་ལམ་ན་ཡང་མི་འདོད་ཅིང༌། སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་མཐོང་སྟེ་ཁྲི་ལ་བཞུགས་ནས་འགྲོ་བ་ལ་ཆོས་ཀྱང་སྟོན་པར་བྱེད་པ་རྨི་ལམ་དུ་མཐོང་བ་དེ་ནི་སྔར་ནས་ཕྱིར་མི་ལྡོག་པར་ལུང་བསྟན་པ་ཡིན་པར་རིག་པར་བྱའོ། །

heading: **སྦྱངས་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་གཞི།**
source: ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། སྦྱངས་སྟོབས་རྣལ་འབྱོར་ཞེས་པ་ནས། རིག་པར་བྱ་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། ཡང་སྦྱངས་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་བཅུ་གཉིས་ཀྱི་སྡོམ་པ་སྟེ། དགོན་པ་དང༌། བསོད་སྙོམས་པ་དང༌། ཟས་ཕྱིས་མི་ལེན་པ་དང༌། སྟན་ཅིག་པ་དང༌། གཞི་ཇི་བཞིན་པ་དང༌། ཆོས་གོས་གསུམ་པ། དུར་ཁྲོད་པ། ཤིང་དྲུང་བ། ཙོག་པུ་བ། འདོད་པ་ཉུང་ཞིང་ཆོག་ཤེས་པ། རབ་ཏུ་དབེན་པ། རྐང་པ་སྐུད་པ་དང་བྲལ་བར་འཇམ་པོར་སྨྲ་ཞིང་ཚིག་ཉུང་བ་དང་ལྡན་ཞིང་བསྒོམ་པའི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་དང་ལྡན་པ་དང་བལྟ་བ་ཅི་འདྲ་བ་འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར་བ་དེ་ལ། ཁྱོད་ནི་ད་ལྟར་མ་ཟད་ཀྱི་སྔོན་ཡང་ཡོན་ཏན་བཅུ་གཉིས་ཀྱི་ཚུལ་ཡང་ད་ལྟར་འདི་དང་འདྲའོ། །ཞེས་བརྗོད་དེ། བརྗོད་པ་དེས་སྐད་ཐོས་ནས་གང་ཐོབ་པ་ལ་ཡིད་ཆེས་ནས་ཁེངས་ཞིང་རློམ་སེམས་བྱེད་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ནི། བདུད་ཀྱི་སེམས་ཡོངས་སུ་བླང་ཞིང་གང་ཟག་བློ་ཆུང་བར་རིག་པར་བྱའོ། །
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "strength of ascetic practices and yoga" up to "should be known": Furthermore, the summary of the twelve ascetic qualities—dwelling in a hermitage, begging for alms, not accepting food afterwards, eating at a single sitting, whatever is the basis, having three dharma robes, dwelling in charnel grounds, dwelling under a tree, remaining in a squatting posture, having few desires and knowing satisfaction, being thoroughly isolated, free from anointing the feet, speaking gently and having few words, and being endowed with the yoga of meditation—and whatever attitude will arise, it is said to them, "Not only now, but previously too, your manner of the twelve qualities was exactly like this now." Having heard the sound of that being said, the bodhisattva who believes in what was attained and becomes puffed up and acts conceited should be known as one whose mind is completely possessed by Māra and who is a person of little intelligence.

translation: Regarding this from "thoroughly isolated village" up to "should be known as having little intelligence": Moreover, the bodhisattva who thoroughly relies on an empty village thoroughly isolated from people, an empty city, mountain ravines, and forests, and actually or mentally praises themselves and deprecates others, should be known as being completely incited by Māra and having little intelligence.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "arhat and" up to "should be known": they who do not desire even in dreams the lower vehicle ground of an arhat, the pristine wisdom of a pratyekabuddha, and the wealth of the three realms, and see in dreams seeing Buddhas sitting on thrones and also demonstrating the Dharma to migrators, should be known as having been previously prophesied as irreversible.

heading: **བཤད་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "always in villages" up to "taught as isolated": What is the isolation of the Great Vehicle? Dwelling constantly in a place like a village, a great province, or a great town, and apart from striving to practice the six perfections in order to make aspirations for sentient beings and accomplish one's own awakening, not generating other desires such as for the levels of arhats and pratyekabuddhas, or for sensory pleasures; this is taught as being the isolation of those of the Great Vehicle, the sons of the Sugatas.

ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། མིང་གི་གཞི་ལས་ཞེས་པ་ནས། མིང་འདི་ཡིན་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། བདུད་ཀྱིས་ལུང་སྟོན་པའི་ཚུལ་ནི་མིང་གི་གཞི་ལས་གླགས་ལྟ་བའི་ཕྱིར་བདུད་ནི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེའི་དྲུང་དུ་ཉེ་བར་འོངས་ནས། འདི་སྐད་སྨྲས་ཏེ་འདི་བཞིན་དུ་འདི་ན་ཁྱོད་ཀྱི་ཕ་དང་མ་དང༌། ཁྱོད་ཀྱི་བུད་མེད་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་བར་གྱི་མིང་ཡིན་ཞིང༌། ཁོ་རང་གིས་བསམས་པ་ལྟར་དུ་གང་གི་ཚེ་ནམ་ཞིག་ན་ཁྱོད་ནི་སངས་རྒྱས་སུ་འགྱུར་བའི་མིང་ཟླ་འོད་ཅེས་བྱ་བ་འདི་ཡིན་ནོ་སྙམ་ནས་རློམ་སེམས་བྱེད་པའི་གང་ཟག་དེ་བློ་ཆུང་བ་ཡིན་ནོ། །

ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། སྦྱངས་སྟོབས་རྣལ་འབྱོར་ཞེས་པ་ནས། རིག་པར་བྱ་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། ཡང་སྦྱངས་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་བཅུ་གཉིས་ཀྱི་སྡོམ་པ་སྟེ། དགོན་པ་དང༌། བསོད་སྙོམས་པ་དང༌། ཟས་ཕྱིས་མི་ལེན་པ་དང༌། སྟན་ཅིག་པ་དང༌། གཞི་ཇི་བཞིན་པ་དང༌། ཆོས་གོས་གསུམ་པ། དུར་ཁྲོད་པ། ཤིང་དྲུང་བ། ཙོག་པུ་བ། འདོད་པ་ཉུང་ཞིང་ཆོག་ཤེས་པ། རབ་ཏུ་དབེན་པ། རྐང་པ་སྐུད་པ་དང་བྲལ་བར་འཇམ་པོར་སྨྲ་ཞིང་ཚིག་ཉུང་བ་དང་ལྡན་ཞིང་བསྒོམ་པའི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་དང་ལྡན་པ་དང་བལྟ་བ་ཅི་འདྲ་བ་འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར་བ་དེ་ལ། ཁྱོད་ནི་ད་ལྟར་མ་ཟད་ཀྱི་སྔོན་ཡང་ཡོན་ཏན་བཅུ་གཉིས་ཀྱི་ཚུལ་ཡང་ད་ལྟར་འདི་དང་འདྲའོ། །ཞེས་བརྗོད་དེ། བརྗོད་པ་དེས་སྐད་ཐོས་ནས་གང་ཐོབ་པ་ལ་ཡིད་ཆེས་ནས་ཁེངས་ཞིང་རློམ་སེམས་བྱེད་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ནི། བདུད་ཀྱི་སེམས་ཡོངས་སུ་བླང་ཞིང་གང་ཟག་བློ་ཆུང་བར་རིག་པར་བྱའོ། །

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "strength of ascetic practices and yoga" up to "should be known": Furthermore, the summary of the twelve ascetic qualities—dwelling in a hermitage, begging for alms, not accepting food afterwards, eating at a single sitting, whatever is the basis, having three dharma robes, dwelling in charnel grounds, dwelling under a tree, remaining in a squatting posture, having few desires and knowing satisfaction, being thoroughly isolated, free from anointing the feet, speaking gently and having few words, and being endowed with the yoga of meditation—and whatever attitude will arise, it is said to them, "Not only now, but previously too, your manner of the twelve qualities was exactly like this now." Having heard the sound of that being said, the bodhisattva who believes in what was attained and becomes puffed up and acts conceited should be known as one whose mind is completely possessed by Māra and who is a person of little intelligence.

Regarding this from "thoroughly isolated village" up to "should be known as having little intelligence": Moreover, the bodhisattva who thoroughly relies on an empty village thoroughly isolated from people, an empty city, mountain ravines, and forests, and actually or mentally praises themselves and deprecates others, should be known as being completely incited by Māra and having little intelligence.

heading: **བཤད་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Furthermore, some with little intelligence, even though they dwell for up to ten million years in the specific bodily isolation of a mountain ravine five hundred yojanas away from a village, in a place filled with scorpions, snakes, birds, and beasts of prey, yet whose minds are isolated from the realization of existence and peace—this bodhisattva of little intelligence who does not know isolation acquires the overweening pride of mere physical isolation and abides in such things to be abandoned. And regarding the bodhisattva who strives for the benefit of beings and has attained the four dhyānas, the five powers, the five faculties, and the samādhis of the three doors of liberation, the person of little intelligence who despises them, thinking, "This bodhisattva practices in an isolated hermitage," is in the domain of Māra; so the Victor taught.

heading: **བསྡུ་བ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "whoever in a village" up to "themselves degenerate": Whatever bodhisattva, whether their body dwells in a village or in a hermitage, is free from the minds of the two vehicles of hearers and solitary realizers in hearing and reflection, and is certain in unsurpassed awakening, this is the unerring isolation of those engaged in accomplishing the benefit of beings. Not knowing the measure of warmth of other bodhisattvas, that affliction of testing will make themselves degenerate.

heading: **བསྟེན་པའི་ཚུལ།**
translation: Regarding this from "therefore" up to "should be relied upon": Because of that manner, in order to seek genuine awakening through such isolation, by means of skillful methods endowed with intense intention and aspiration, one entirely destroys pride, which is the obstacle to dharma arising in the continuum; for example, just as a host of sick people cherish and rely on a skilled physician to cure their own illnesses, if one asks how the ground for accomplishing this perfection through purpose, thought, action, and so forth is, one should rely continuously with respect and without distraction on the guru, the spiritual friend.

heading: **བསྟན་པ།**
translation: Regarding this from "the awakening of a Buddha" up to "swiftly realize": If one asks what kind of guru to rely upon is taught: Bodhisattvas who have entered into the supreme awakening of the Buddha who teaches, and those endowed with the perfection of skillful means to be relied upon, are taught as spiritual friends of complete holding and skillful means. If one asks how they become spiritual friends: they are the ones who subsequently teach the dharma of the person, and this dharma is the ground to be accomplished. Being taught and accomplished by these two types of reasons in this way, one will swiftly realize the awakening of a Buddha.

heading: **བཤད་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "Victors of the past and" up to "taught as being": Because these six perfections are the path traversed by all Victors—those who passed previously, those who have not yet come later, and those who currently abide in the directions—and there is no other. Thus, the Victor taught that because these six perfections provide the fruit for those abiding in the supreme awakening of the Great Vehicle, they are clarity; because they show the path, they are a lamp; because of realizing by the four, they are illumination; and because they protect from the bad path, they are the supreme teacher.

heading: **ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད།**
translation: Regarding "Just as the perfection of wisdom is empty of characteristics": Just as the defining characteristic of the perfection of wisdom is emptiness, or alternatively, the perfection of wisdom is empty of both characteristic and characterized, because it is empty of a basis for characteristics. Thus, it is also said in the Hundred Thousand: "Characteristics are devoid of the intrinsic nature of characteristics."

heading: **དེ་ཆོས་རྣམས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན་དུ་བསྟན་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "all these dharmas" up to "is practicing": Similarly, having known that all these dharmas comprising the affliction of saṃsāra and the purification of nirvāṇa are also empty like that characteristic of the perfection of wisdom, if one thus thoroughly knows that dharmas are empty of intrinsic nature, and that being empty of a cause is signlessness, and being empty of a fruit is wishlessness, then having realized this thus, practicing that is practicing in the wisdom of the Sugatas.

heading: **དེ་ལས་ཀུན་ཉོན་མོངས་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "beings thoroughly" up to "taught as affliction": If one asks, "If all dharmas are emptiness, how do they become the two—the affliction of saṃsāra and the purification of nirvāṇa?": Through thoroughly conceptualizing clinging to a self, beings desire the food of sensory pleasures, and those endowed with a mind attached to self and what belongs to self, which are the causes of saṃsāra, are continuously wandering in saṃsāra due to being entirely motivated by afflictions caused by that self and accumulating through that; however, the two dharmas—the self to which one is attached and what belongs to self—do not authentically exist and are empty, but childish ordinary beings themselves apprehend them as existing though they are non-existent, for example, similar to casting a knot in the sky. Thus, it is also like, for example, taking poison with the perception of doubt: although that poison has not entered the body in reality, one faints. Similarly through this example, childish ordinary beings who accept self and what belongs to self also, by perceiving that self, are born and die through the power of apprehending it due to being completely impermanent authentically; in short, just as there is apprehension of self and what belongs to self, so it is taught as the affliction of saṃsāra.

heading: **ཚོགས་རྒྱ་ཆེན་པོ་བདེ་བླག་ཏུ་སོག་པ།**
translation: Regarding this from "in Jambudvīpa" up to "should engage": To demonstrate through an example the great benefit of meditating in that way: For example, if all the beings without exception, however many there are in Jambudvīpa, taking it as the supreme support, as a preliminary generate the intention for supreme awakening, and as the main practice of application give extensively and excellently to Buddhas and for ripening beings for a long time of many tens of millions of thousands of years, and subsequently dedicate all the merit as the cause for complete awakening, which is the locus of dedication, for the purpose of the goal, the benefit of beings; yet, if whatever person makes manifest effort in meditating themselves on the perfection of wisdom as explained before and teaching it to others, and does this in accordance with it for even one single day, the previous mass of merit is not capable of being even a hundredth part, up to a cause of this. Because of that cause, one should constantly engage with effort in practicing wisdom, without distraction by laziness and other activities.

heading: **འགྲོ་བ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་སྦྱིན་སོགས་སུ་གྱུར་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "perfection of wisdom" up to "completely enjoys": Furthermore, that yogi practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom, although generating great compassion pervading all beings, has no perception of beings as real. At that time, if one offers to that wise one, beings themselves are not burdened and the merit of others increases, so they become an object of generosity for all beings; therefore, they constantly completely enjoy meaningfully the alms offered by the realm.

Regarding this from "in Jambudvīpa" up to "should engage": To demonstrate through an example the great benefit of meditating in that way: For example, if all the beings without exception, however many there are in Jambudvīpa, taking it as the supreme support, as a preliminary generate the intention for supreme awakening, and as the main practice of application give extensively and excellently to Buddhas and for ripening beings for a long time of many tens of millions of thousands of years, and subsequently dedicate all the merit as the cause for complete awakening, which is the locus of dedication, for the purpose of the goal, the benefit of beings; yet, if whatever person makes manifest effort in meditating themselves on the perfection of wisdom as explained before and teaching it to others, and does this in accordance with it for even one single day, the previous mass of merit is not capable of being even a hundredth part, up to a cause of this. Because of that cause, one should constantly engage with effort in practicing wisdom, without distraction by laziness and other activities.

heading: **གདུལ་བྱའི་ལམ་སྟོན་པར་འགྱུར་བ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "bodhisattva" up to "should make effort": Moreover, whatever bodhisattva desires to teach to the realm of beings this perfection, which is a spacious path because it accommodates anything whatsoever, in order to free beings of the three—gods, humans, and bad destinies—who have been connected from a beginningless long time in this saṃsāra, from suffering along with its causes, they should also as a method for that make effort day and night in the perfection of wisdom through the ten dharma practices.

Regarding this from "in Jambudvīpa" up to "should engage": To demonstrate through an example the great benefit of meditating in that way: For example, if all the beings without exception, however many there are in Jambudvīpa, taking it as the supreme support, as a preliminary generate the intention for supreme awakening, and as the main practice of application give extensively and excellently to Buddhas and for ripening beings for a long time of many tens of millions of thousands of years, and subsequently dedicate all the merit as the cause for complete awakening, which is the locus of dedication, for the purpose of the goal, the benefit of beings; yet, if whatever person makes manifest effort in meditating themselves on the perfection of wisdom as explained before and teaching it to others, and does this in accordance with it for even one single day, the previous mass of merit is not capable of being even a hundredth part, up to a cause of this. Because of that cause, one should constantly engage with effort in practicing wisdom, without distraction by laziness and other activities.

heading: **དཔེའི་སྒོ་ནས་ཇི་ལྟར་མཚོན་པར་བྱ་བ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Through this from "a person previously" up to "just as they become": The necessity of easily and swiftly accomplishing the words teaching wisdom is like the example of finding a jewel; similarly, those who have entered the path of supreme awakening, having found the jewel-like perfection of wisdom and practicing it, whatever yogi is endowed with joyous effort should not abandon it. It is just as having found and taken the previously taught jewel, and having wrapped and hidden it with great effort, one swiftly goes to one's own place, and by that the suffering of beings becomes pacified.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "beings thoroughly" up to "taught as affliction": If one asks, "If all dharmas are emptiness, how do they become the two—the affliction of saṃsāra and the purification of nirvāṇa?": Through thoroughly conceptualizing clinging to a self, beings desire the food of sensory pleasures, and those endowed with a mind attached to self and what belongs to self, which are the causes of saṃsāra, are continuously wandering in saṃsāra due to being entirely motivated by afflictions caused by that self and accumulating through that; however, the two dharmas—the self to which one is attached and what belongs to self—do not authentically exist and are empty, but childish ordinary beings themselves apprehend them as existing though they are non-existent, for example, similar to casting a knot in the sky. Thus, it is also like, for example, taking poison with the perception of doubt: although that poison has not entered the body in reality, one faints. Similarly through this example, childish ordinary beings who accept self and what belongs to self also, by perceiving that self, are born and die through the power of apprehending it due to being completely impermanent authentically; in short, just as there is apprehension of self and what belongs to self, so it is taught as the affliction of saṃsāra.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "beings thoroughly" up to "taught as affliction": If one asks, "If all dharmas are emptiness, how do they become the two—the affliction of saṃsāra and the purification of nirvāṇa?": Through thoroughly conceptualizing clinging to a self, beings desire the food of sensory pleasures, and those endowed with a mind attached to self and what belongs to self, which are the causes of saṃsāra, are continuously wandering in saṃsāra due to being entirely motivated by afflictions caused by that self and accumulating through that; however, the two dharmas—the self to which one is attached and what belongs to self—do not authentically exist and are empty, but childish ordinary beings themselves apprehend them as existing though they are non-existent, for example, similar to casting a knot in the sky. Thus, it is also like, for example, taking poison with the perception of doubt: although that poison has not entered the body in reality, one faints. Similarly through this example, childish ordinary beings who accept self and what belongs to self also, by perceiving that self, are born and die through the power of apprehending it due to being completely impermanent authentically; in short, just as there is apprehension of self and what belongs to self, so it is taught as the affliction of saṃsāra.

Regarding this from "in Jambudvīpa" up to "should engage": To demonstrate through an example the great benefit of meditating in that way: For example, if all the beings without exception, however many there are in Jambudvīpa, taking it as the supreme support, as a preliminary generate the intention for supreme awakening, and as the main practice of application give extensively and excellently to Buddhas and for ripening beings for a long time of many tens of millions of thousands of years, and subsequently dedicate all the merit as the cause for complete awakening, which is the locus of dedication, for the purpose of the goal, the benefit of beings; yet, if whatever person makes manifest effort in meditating themselves on the perfection of wisdom as explained before and teaching it to others, and does this in accordance with it for even one single day, the previous mass of merit is not capable of being even a hundredth part, up to a cause of this. Because of that cause, one should constantly engage with effort in practicing wisdom, without distraction by laziness and other activities.

heading: **བསྒྲུབ་པ་གཞན་ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན་པ།**
translation: Regarding this from "sun free from clouds" up to "outshines": Furthermore, for example, when the sun with its network of light rays free from clouds rises, it destroys all the dense darkness of the discordant class of black darkness, and by that dawn of illumination, the light of all the concordant class of fireflies and elemental creatures, and also all the light of the hosts of stars and the light of the moon, are outshone by the light of the sun; similarly through this example, the bodhisattva practicing the sun-like supreme perfection of wisdom practices emptiness and signlessness, and through skillful means having destroyed the dense darkness of ignorance viewing self and dharmas which is the discordant class, outshines with non-apprehension the many virtues with apprehension of Mahāyāna bodhisattvas, the virtues of pratyekabuddhas and arhats which are virtues conducive to liberation, and the parts conducive to merit of all beings, which are the concordant class.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "beings thoroughly" up to "taught as affliction": If one asks, "If all dharmas are emptiness, how do they become the two—the affliction of saṃsāra and the purification of nirvāṇa?": Through thoroughly conceptualizing clinging to a self, beings desire the food of sensory pleasures, and those endowed with a mind attached to self and what belongs to self, which are the causes of saṃsāra, are continuously wandering in saṃsāra due to being entirely motivated by afflictions caused by that self and accumulating through that; however, the two dharmas—the self to which one is attached and what belongs to self—do not authentically exist and are empty, but childish ordinary beings themselves apprehend them as existing though they are non-existent, for example, similar to casting a knot in the sky. Thus, it is also like, for example, taking poison with the perception of doubt: although that poison has not entered the body in reality, one faints. Similarly through this example, childish ordinary beings who accept self and what belongs to self also, by perceiving that self, are born and die through the power of apprehending it due to being completely impermanent authentically; in short, just as there is apprehension of self and what belongs to self, so it is taught as the affliction of saṃsāra.

འཛམ་བུ་གླིང་ན་ཞེས་པ་ནས། འཇུག་པར་བྱ་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། དེ་ལྟར་བསྒོམས་པའི་ཕན་ཡོན་ཆེ་བ་དཔེ་ཡིས་བསྟན་པ་ནི། དཔེར་ན་འཛམ་བུ་གླིང་ན་སེམས་ཅན་ཇི་སྙེད་ཡོད་པ་མ་ལུས་པ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་བརྟེན་མཆོག་ཏུ་བྱེད་པ་ལ་སྔོན་འགྲོ་བསམ་པ་བྱང་ཆུབ་མཆོག་ཏུ་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་བྱས་ནས། དངོས་གཞི་སྦྱོར་བ་དུས་རིང་བ་ལོ་སྟོང་བྱེ་བ་མང་པོར་སངས་རྒྱས་དང་སེམས་ཅན་ལ་སྨིན་པར་བྱེད་པ་གྱ་ནོམ་པར་མང་པོར་བྱིན་པར་བྱས་ལ། རྗེས་ལ་བསོད་ནམས་ཀུན་ཀྱང་ཆེད་དུ་བྱ་བ་འགྲོ་བའི་དོན་གྱི་ཕྱིར་བསྔོ་ས་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་རྒྱུར་བསྔོ་ཡང༌། གང་ཟག་གང་ལ་ལ་ཞིག་གིས་སྔར་བཤད་པ་ལྟར་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་རང་བསྒོམ་པ་དང་གཞན་ལ་སྟོན་པ་ལ་མངོན་པར་བརྩོན་པར་བྱེད་པ་དེ། ཐ་ན་དུས་ཉི་མ་གཅིག་རྗེས་སུ་མཐུན་པར་བྱེད་ན། དེ་ལ་སྔར་བཤད་པའི་ཕུང་པོས་བསོད་ནམས་བརྒྱའི་ཆ་ནས་རྒྱུའི་བར་གྱི་ཆར་ཡང་མི་ཕོད་དོ། །རྒྱུའི་ཕྱིར་ན་ལེ་ལོ་དང་བྱ་བ་གཞན་གྱིས་གཡེལ་བ་མེད་པར་རྟག་ཏུ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་ཉམས་སུ་ལེན་པ་བརྩོན་པས་འཇུག་པར་བྱའོ། །
[2-215] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "in Jambudvīpa" up to "should engage": To demonstrate through an example the great benefit of meditating in that way: For example, if all the beings without exception, however many there are in Jambudvīpa, taking it as the supreme support, as a preliminary generate the intention for supreme awakening, and as the main practice of application give extensively and excellently to Buddhas and for ripening beings for a long time of many tens of millions of thousands of years, and subsequently dedicate all the merit as the cause for complete awakening, which is the locus of dedication, for the purpose of the goal, the benefit of beings; yet, if whatever person makes manifest effort in meditating themselves on the perfection of wisdom as explained before and teaching it to others, and does this in accordance with it for even one single day, the previous mass of merit is not capable of being even a hundredth part, up to a cause of this. Because of that cause, one should constantly engage with effort in practicing wisdom, without distraction by laziness and other activities.

heading: **ལྷ་མིའི་མགོན་དུ་གྱུར་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Through this from "for example, a son of a king" up to "what need to mention": Practicing the supreme path becoming the glory of gods and humans: just like the example of a young prince, similarly a bodhisattva endowed with skillful means practicing the perfection of wisdom, healing the disease of afflictions, gives generosity like nectar, and by the power of that, gods and humans rejoice and come into their presence, and they generate the hope thinking, "If this bodhisattva makes effort in benefiting many beings even now in the time of being a son of the Victor, when one day they become established in Buddhahood as a king of dharma, what need to mention their accomplishing the benefit of beings!"

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "beings thoroughly" up to "taught as affliction": If one asks, "If all dharmas are emptiness, how do they become the two—the affliction of saṃsāra and the purification of nirvāṇa?": Through thoroughly conceptualizing clinging to a self, beings desire the food of sensory pleasures, and those endowed with a mind attached to self and what belongs to self, which are the causes of saṃsāra, are continuously wandering in saṃsāra due to being entirely motivated by afflictions caused by that self and accumulating through that; however, the two dharmas—the self to which one is attached and what belongs to self—do not authentically exist and are empty, but childish ordinary beings themselves apprehend them as existing though they are non-existent, for example, similar to casting a knot in the sky. Thus, it is also like, for example, taking poison with the perception of doubt: although that poison has not entered the body in reality, one faints. Similarly through this example, childish ordinary beings who accept self and what belongs to self also, by perceiving that self, are born and die through the power of apprehending it due to being completely impermanent authentically; in short, just as there is apprehension of self and what belongs to self, so it is taught as the affliction of saṃsāra.

Because of that cause, one should constantly engage with effort in practicing wisdom, without distraction by laziness and other activities.

heading: **ལྷ་མིའི་མགོན་དུ་གྱུར་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "at that time" up to "sends shooting stars": Furthermore, at that time, Māra, thinking, "This bodhisattva will be victorious over my battle," his mind becomes endowed with a pang of pain, his mind exhausted by sorrow, his body suffering with illness, his feelings mentally unhappy, and he is feeble due to the shrinking of the courage of body and mind. Furthermore, still thinking, "By doing what, how will the mind of this bodhisattva withdraw from the conduct of awakening?", in order to show fear through his actions, he burns the regions in their vicinity with fire and from above sends shooting stars, that is, thunderbolts.

Regarding this from "sun free from clouds" up to "outshines": Furthermore, for example, when the sun with its network of light rays free from clouds rises, it destroys all the dense darkness of the discordant class of black darkness, and by that dawn of illumination, the light of all the concordant class of fireflies and elemental creatures, and also all the light of the hosts of stars and the light of the moon, are outshone by the light of the sun; similarly through this example, the bodhisattva practicing the sun-like supreme perfection of wisdom practices emptiness and signlessness, and through skillful means having destroyed the dense darkness of ignorance viewing self and dharmas which is the discordant class, outshines with non-apprehension the many virtues with apprehension of Mahāyāna bodhisattvas, the virtues of pratyekabuddhas and arhats which are virtues conducive to liberation, and the parts conducive to merit of all beings, which are the concordant class.

heading: **ལྷ་མིའི་མགོན་དུ་གྱུར་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "whenever the wise" up to "how could they": Nevertheless, whenever those wise bodhisattvas, endowed with love and compassion with intense intention, in their application look at the meaning of the supreme perfection of wisdom without difference of day and night. At that time, the body, mind, and speech, the three, of that bodhisattva become free from the two extremes or unharmed, like a bird going in the sky; and even if Māra and the dark partisans included in his retinue look for an opportunity regarding them, how could they find an opportunity? They do not find an opportunity.

heading: **ཞོར་ལ་ཚོགས་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "whenever a bodhisattva" up to "trains in this dharma of the Buddha": Furthermore, at whatever time some bodhisattvas fight with the body and dispute with speech, and mentally disagree with one another and become endowed with angry minds, at that time Māra and his retinue become joyful in mind, experience supreme comfort in body, and think thus: "Those two fighting and disputing bodhisattvas will become far from the wisdom of the Victor, so my purpose is accomplished"—thinking this, they become joyful in mind. In reality as well, the wisdom of those two bodhisattvas becomes distant, and as a cause they will become fierce flesh-eaters, and thus both will degenerate from their previous vows of generating the mind. If one asks, "How will they degenerate?", how could there be awakening for that intention which is hateful and free from patience? There is none. At such a time, Māras along with their factions become utterly joyful in mind; and in particular, if whatever bodhisattva who has not received a prophecy becomes angry in mind and begins to dispute with a bodhisattva who has previously received a prophecy, since they are endowed with the fault of the ashes of afflictions, they must don the armor of patience anew for as many eons as the number of moments of that mind. The antidote to that sin, or the method to avert it, is patience; since all buddhas also touched supreme awakening by meditating on the perfection of patience, if one thinks, "This hateful mind is not good," one generates mindful regret, confesses individually through various antidotes, vows subsequently to refrain from such thoughts and actions, and does not rejoice in mind about what was done previously—that is training in this dharma of the Buddha's teaching.

Regarding this from "sun free from clouds" up to "outshines": Furthermore, for example, when the sun with its network of light rays free from clouds rises, it destroys all the dense darkness of the discordant class of black darkness, and by that dawn of illumination, the light of all the concordant class of fireflies and elemental creatures, and also all the light of the hosts of stars and the light of the moon, are outshone by the light of the sun; similarly through this example, the bodhisattva practicing the sun-like supreme perfection of wisdom practices emptiness and signlessness, and through skillful means having destroyed the dense darkness of ignorance viewing self and dharmas which is the discordant class, outshines with non-apprehension the many virtues with apprehension of Mahāyāna bodhisattvas, the virtues of pratyekabuddhas and arhats which are virtues conducive to liberation, and the parts conducive to merit of all beings, which are the concordant class.

Regarding this from "sun free from clouds" up to "outshines": Furthermore, for example, when the sun with its network of light rays free from clouds rises, it destroys all the dense darkness of the discordant class of black darkness, and by that dawn of illumination, the light of all the concordant class of fireflies and elemental creatures, and also all the light of the hosts of stars and the light of the moon, are outshone by the light of the sun; similarly through this example, the bodhisattva practicing the sun-like supreme perfection of wisdom practices emptiness and signlessness, and through skillful means having destroyed the dense darkness of ignorance viewing self and dharmas which is the discordant class, outshines with non-apprehension the many virtues with apprehension of Mahāyāna bodhisattvas, the virtues of pratyekabuddhas and arhats which are virtues conducive to liberation, and the parts conducive to merit of all beings, which are the concordant class.

heading: **རང་བཞིན།**
translation: Regarding this from "whenever learning" up to "trains in this dharma": When whatever bodhisattva trains in the conduct of awakening, it is because they do not assert any perfect training whatsoever. Thus, not apprehending the trainee and these dharmas to be trained in, and not conceptualizing these two—what is to be trained in and what is not to be trained in—as truly distinct, whoever trains like that, that is training in this dharma of the Buddha's teaching.

ཉི་མ་སྤྲིན་དང་བྲལ་བའི་ཞེས་པ་ནས། ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། ཡང་དཔེར་ན་ཉི་མ་སྤྲིན་དང་བྲལ་བའི་འོད་ཟེར་དྲ་བ་ཅན་ཤར་བས། མི་མཐུན་པའི་ཕྱོགས་མུན་ནག་ཐིབས་པོའི་མུན་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་འཇོམས་ཤིང་སྣང་བ་འཆར་བ་དེས་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་སྲིན་བུ་མེ་ཁྱེར་དང་སྲོག་ཆགས་འབྱུང་པོ་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི་འོད་དང༌། ཡང་སྐར་མའི་ཚོགས་ཀྱི་འོད་དང་ཟླ་བའི་འོད་ཀུན་ཀྱང་ཉི་མའི་འོད་ཀྱིས་ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན་ཏེ། དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཉི་མ་ལྟ་བུའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་མཆོག་ལ་སྤྱོད་པ་ནི་སྟོང་པ་མཚན་མ་མེད་པ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པ་དང༌། ཐབས་མཁས་པས་མི་མཐུན་པའི་ཕྱོགས་བདག་དང་ཆོས་སུ་བལྟ་བའི་མ་རིག་པའི་ཐིབས་པོ་བཅོམ་ནས་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་འགྲོ་བ་ཀུན་གྱི་བསོད་ནམས་ཆ་མཐུན་དང༌། ཐར་པ་ཆ་མཐུན་གྱི་དགེ་བ་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ། རང་རྒྱལ་གྱི་དགེ་བ་དང་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་དགེ་བ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་དམིགས་བཅས་ཀྱི་དགེ་བ་མང་པོ་དམིགས་མེད་ཀྱི་ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན་ནོ། །
[2-220] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "sun free from clouds" up to "outshines": Furthermore, for example, when the sun with its network of light rays free from clouds rises, it destroys all the dense darkness of the discordant class of black darkness, and by that dawn of illumination, the light of all the concordant class of fireflies and elemental creatures, and also all the light of the hosts of stars and the light of the moon, are outshone by the light of the sun; similarly through this example, the bodhisattva practicing the sun-like supreme perfection of wisdom practices emptiness and signlessness, and through skillful means having destroyed the dense darkness of ignorance viewing self and dharmas which is the discordant class, outshines with non-apprehension the many virtues with apprehension of Mahāyāna bodhisattvas, the virtues of pratyekabuddhas and arhats which are virtues conducive to liberation, and the parts conducive to merit of all beings, which are the concordant class.

ཅེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་ཞེས་པ་ནས། ཡོངས་སུ་སྤྱོད་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། གཞན་ཡང་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་མཆོག་ལ་སྤྱོད་པའི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་པ་དེ། སེམས་ཅན་ཀུན་ལ་ཁྱབ་པའི་སྙིང་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོ་བསྐྱེད་ཀྱང་སེམས་ཅན་བདེན་པའི་འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་པའོ། །དེའི་ཚེ་མཁས་པ་དེ་ལ་ཕུལ་ན་འགྲོ་བ་རང་མི་ལྕི་ལ་གཞན་གྱི་དགེ་བ་འཕེལ་བས་འགྲོ་བ་ཀུན་གྱི་སྦྱིན་པའི་གནས་སུ་འགྱུར་བས་ན། རྟག་ཏུ་ཡུལ་འཁོར་གྱིས་ཕུལ་བའི་བསོད་སྙོམས་དོན་ཡོད་པར་ཡོངས་སུ་སྤྱོད་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "perfection of wisdom" up to "completely enjoys": Furthermore, that yogi practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom, although generating great compassion pervading all beings, has no perception of beings as real. At that time, if one offers to that wise one, beings themselves are not burdened and the merit of others increases, so they become an object of generosity for all beings; therefore, they constantly completely enjoy meaningfully the alms offered by the realm.

[2-217] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཞེས་པ་ནས། བརྩོན་པར་བྱ་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། ཡང་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གང་ལ་ལ་ཞིག་འཁོར་བ་འདི་ནས་དུས་ཡུན་རིང་པོ་ཐོག་མ་མེད་པ་ནས་འབྲེལ་བའི་ལྷ་དང་མི་དང་ངན་སོང་གསུམ་གྱི་སེམས་ཅན་སྡུག་བསྔལ་རྒྱུ་དང་བཅས་པ་ལས་གྲོལ་བའི་ཕྱིར། གང་ཡང་ཤོང་བས་ལམ་ཡངས་པ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདི་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་ཁམས་ལ་སྟོན་པར་འདོད་པས་ཀྱང་དེའི་ཐབས་སུ་ཉིན་མཚན་མེད་པར་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་ཆོས་སྤྱོད་བཅུས་བརྩོན་པར་བྱའོ། །

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "bodhisattva" up to "should make effort": Moreover, whatever bodhisattva desires to teach to the realm of beings this perfection, which is a spacious path because it accommodates anything whatsoever, in order to free beings of the three—gods, humans, and bad destinies—who have been connected from a beginningless long time in this saṃsāra, from suffering along with its causes, they should also as a method for that make effort day and night in the perfection of wisdom through the ten dharma practices.

ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། མི་ཞིག་སྔོན་ཆད་ཞེས་པ་ནས། འགྱུར་བ་བཞིན་ཞེས་པའི་བར་གྱིས། ཤེས་རབ་སྟོན་པར་བྱེད་པའི་ཚིག་བདེ་བླག་ཏུ་མྱུར་དུ་བསྒྲུབ་དགོས་པ་ནོར་བུ་རྙེད་པའི་དཔེ་དེ་ལྟར་བྱང་ཆུབ་མཆོག་གི་ལམ་ལ་ཞུགས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་རིན་ཆེན་ལྟ་བུའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་རྙེད་ནས་ཉམས་སུ་ལེན་པ་ལ་རྣལ་འབྱོར་པ་གང་ཞིག་བརྩོན་འགྲུས་དང་ལྡན་པས་དོར་བར་མི་བྱའོ། །སྔར་སྟོན་པའི་རིན་ཆེན་རྙེད་ནས་བླངས་ཏེ་རབ་ཏུ་བརྩོན་པས་དཀྲིས་ཤིང་སྦས་ནས། མྱུར་དུ་རང་གི་གནས་སུ་འགྲོ་བར་བྱེད་པ་དང༌། དེས་འགྲོ་བའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཞི་བར་འགྱུར་བ་བཞིན་ནོ། །

Thus it is said: Through this from "a person previously" up to "just as they become": The necessity of easily and swiftly accomplishing the words teaching wisdom is like the example of finding a jewel; similarly, those who have entered the path of supreme awakening, having found the jewel-like perfection of wisdom and practicing it, whatever yogi is endowed with joyous effort should not abandon it. It is just as having found and taken the previously taught jewel, and having wrapped and hidden it with great effort, one swiftly goes to one's own place, and by that the suffering of beings becomes pacified.

ཉི་མ་སྤྲིན་དང་བྲལ་བའི་ཞེས་པ་ནས། ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། ཡང་དཔེར་ན་ཉི་མ་སྤྲིན་དང་བྲལ་བའི་འོད་ཟེར་དྲ་བ་ཅན་ཤར་བས། མི་མཐུན་པའི་ཕྱོགས་མུན་ནག་ཐིབས་པོའི་མུན་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་འཇོམས་ཤིང་སྣང་བ་འཆར་བ་དེས་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་སྲིན་བུ་མེ་ཁྱེར་དང་སྲོག་ཆགས་འབྱུང་པོ་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི་འོད་དང༌། ཡང་སྐར་མའི་ཚོགས་ཀྱི་འོད་དང་ཟླ་བའི་འོད་ཀུན་ཀྱང་ཉི་མའི་འོད་ཀྱིས་ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན་ཏེ། དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཉི་མ་ལྟ་བུའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་མཆོག་ལ་སྤྱོད་པ་ནི་སྟོང་པ་མཚན་མ་མེད་པ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པ་དང༌། ཐབས་མཁས་པས་མི་མཐུན་པའི་ཕྱོགས་བདག་དང་ཆོས་སུ་བལྟ་བའི་མ་རིག་པའི་ཐིབས་པོ་བཅོམ་ནས་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་འགྲོ་བ་ཀུན་གྱི་བསོད་ནམས་ཆ་མཐུན་དང༌། ཐར་པ་ཆ་མཐུན་གྱི་དགེ་བ་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ། རང་རྒྱལ་གྱི་དགེ་བ་དང་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་དགེ་བ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་དམིགས་བཅས་ཀྱི་དགེ་བ་མང་པོ་དམིགས་མེད་ཀྱི་ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན་ནོ། །
[2-220] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "sun free from clouds" up to "outshines": Furthermore, for example, when the sun with its network of light rays free from clouds rises, it destroys all the dense darkness of the discordant class of black darkness, and by that dawn of illumination, the light of all the concordant class of fireflies and elemental creatures, and also all the light of the hosts of stars and the light of the moon, are outshone by the light of the sun; similarly through this example, the bodhisattva practicing the sun-like supreme perfection of wisdom practices emptiness and signlessness, and through skillful means having destroyed the dense darkness of ignorance viewing self and dharmas which is the discordant class, outshines with non-apprehension the many virtues with apprehension of Mahāyāna bodhisattvas, the virtues of pratyekabuddhas and arhats which are virtues conducive to liberation, and the parts conducive to merit of all beings, which are the concordant class.

[2-221] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་རྒྱལ་པོའི་བུ་ཞིག་ཞེས་པ་ནས། སྨོས་ཅི་དགོས་ཞེས་པའི་བར་གྱིས། ལམ་མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་ཉམས་སུ་ལེན་པ་དེ་ལྷ་མིའི་དཔལ་དུ་འགྱུར་བ་ནི། རྒྱལ་བུ་གཞོན་ནུའི་དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དེ་ལྟར་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་སྤྱོད་ཅིང་ཐབས་མཁས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཉོན་མོངས་པའི་ནད་གསོ་བ་ཡང༌། བདུད་རྩི་ལྟ་བུའི་སྦྱིན་པ་སྦྱིན་པར་བྱེད་ཅིང་དེའི་དབང་གིས་ལྷ་དང་མི་རྣམས་དགའ་བས་དེའི་དྲུང་དུ་འོང་ཞིང༌། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་འདི་ནི་རྒྱལ་སྲས་ཀྱི་དུས་ད་ལྟ་ན་ཡང་སེམས་ཅན་མང་པོ་ལ་ཕན་གདགས་པར་བརྩོན་པར་བྱེད་ན། ནམ་ཞིག་ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོར་སངས་རྒྱས་པ་ལ་གནས་པར་འགྱུར་ན་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་དོན་བྱེད་པ་ལ་སྨོས་ཅི་དགོས་སྙམ་དུ་རེ་བ་བསྐྱེད་དོ། །
[2-221] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Through this from "for example, a son of a king" up to "what need to mention": Practicing the supreme path becoming the glory of gods and humans: just like the example of a young prince, similarly a bodhisattva endowed with skillful means practicing the perfection of wisdom, healing the disease of afflictions, gives generosity like nectar, and by the power of that, gods and humans rejoice and come into their presence, and they generate the hope thinking, "If this bodhisattva makes effort in benefiting many beings even now in the time of being a son of the Victor, when one day they become established in Buddhahood as a king of dharma, what need to mention their accomplishing the benefit of beings!"

heading: **བསླབ་པའི་དོན་ཚང་བ།**
translation: Regarding this from "a bodhisattva" up to "trains thus": Furthermore, whatever base person, a bodhisattva, who knows this training not included in that, will also not degenerate in the two trainings and become corrupted in ethical discipline, because they do not apprehend a cause of degeneration. In order to please through the dharma of the Buddha, they train in this supreme perfection of wisdom, the object; regarding such a training, out of those two—higher mind and ethical discipline—this training is the training of higher mind, so they are wise in it, because of non-apprehension. Thus they train in the non-apprehending wisdom of the light-makers who are wise in dispelling ignorance.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "at that time" up to "sends shooting stars": Furthermore, at that time, Māra, thinking, "This bodhisattva will be victorious over my battle," his mind becomes endowed with a pang of pain, his mind exhausted by sorrow, his body suffering with illness, his feelings mentally unhappy, and he is feeble due to the shrinking of the courage of body and mind. Furthermore, still thinking, "By doing what, how will the mind of this bodhisattva withdraw from the conduct of awakening?", in order to show fear through his actions, he burns the regions in their vicinity with fire and from above sends shooting stars, that is, thunderbolts.

ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། གང་ཚེ་མཁས་པ་ཞེས་པ་ནས། ག་ལ་འགྱུར་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། འོན་ཀྱང་གང་གི་ཚེ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་མཁས་པ་དེ་དག་བསམ་པ་དྲག་པོས་བྱམས་སྙིང་རྗེ་དང་ལྡན་ཞིང༌། སྦྱོར་བ་དུས་ཉིན་མཚན་མེད་པར་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་མཆོག་གི་དོན་ལ་བལྟའོ། །དེའི་ཚེ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེའི་ལུས་དང་སེམས་དང་ངག་དང་གསུམ་ནི་མཁའ་ལ་འགྲོ་བའི་བྱ་ལྟར་དུ་མཐའ་གཉིས་དང་བྲལ་བའམ་གནོད་པ་མེད་པར་འགྱུར་ལ། དེ་ལ་བདུད་དང་ནག་པོའི་རྩ་ལག་དེའི་འཁོར་དུ་གཏོགས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་གླགས་བལྟས་ཀྱང་གླགས་རྙེད་པར་ག་ལ་འགྱུར་ཏེ་གླགས་མི་རྙེད་དོ། །

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "whenever the wise" up to "how could they": Nevertheless, whenever those wise bodhisattvas, endowed with love and compassion with intense intention, in their application look at the meaning of the supreme perfection of wisdom without difference of day and night. At that time, the body, mind, and speech, the three, of that bodhisattva become free from the two extremes or unharmed, like a bird going in the sky; and even if Māra and the dark partisans included in his retinue look for an opportunity regarding them, how could they find an opportunity? Thus it is said: Regarding this from "whenever a bodhisattva" up to "trains in this dharma of the Buddha": Furthermore, at whatever time some bodhisattvas fight with the body and dispute with speech, and mentally disagree with one another and become endowed with angry minds, at that time Māra and his retinue become joyful in mind, experience supreme comfort in body, and think thus: "Those two fighting and disputing bodhisattvas will become far from the wisdom of the Victor, so my purpose is accomplished"—thinking this, they become joyful in mind. In reality as well, the wisdom of those two bodhisattvas becomes distant, and as a cause they will become fierce flesh-eaters, and thus both will degenerate from their previous vows of generating the mind. If one asks, "How will they degenerate?", how could there be awakening for that intention which is hateful and free from patience? There is none. At such a time, Māras along with their factions become utterly joyful in mind; and in particular, if whatever bodhisattva who has not received a prophecy becomes angry in mind and begins to dispute with a bodhisattva who has previously received a prophecy, since they are endowed with the fault of the ashes of afflictions, they must don the armor of patience anew for as many eons as the number of moments of that mind. The antidote to that sin, or the method to avert it, is patience; since all buddhas also touched supreme awakening by meditating on the perfection of patience, if one thinks, "This hateful mind is not good," one generates mindful regret, confesses individually through various antidotes, vows subsequently to refrain from such thoughts and actions, and does not rejoice in mind about what was done previously—that is training in this dharma of the Buddha's teaching.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "whenever the wise" up to "how could they": Nevertheless, whenever those wise bodhisattvas, endowed with love and compassion with intense intention, in their application look at the meaning of the supreme perfection of wisdom without difference of day and night. At that time, the body, mind, and speech, the three, of that bodhisattva become free from the two extremes or unharmed, like a bird going in the sky; and even if Māra and the dark partisans included in his retinue look for an opportunity regarding them, how could they find an opportunity? Thus it is said: Regarding this from "whenever a bodhisattva" up to "trains in this dharma of the Buddha": Furthermore, at whatever time some bodhisattvas fight with the body and dispute with speech, and mentally disagree with one another and become endowed with angry minds, at that time Māra and his retinue become joyful in mind, experience supreme comfort in body, and think thus: "Those two fighting and disputing bodhisattvas will become far from the wisdom of the Victor, so my purpose is accomplished"—thinking this, they become joyful in mind. In reality as well, the wisdom of those two bodhisattvas becomes distant, and as a cause they will become fierce flesh-eaters, and thus both will degenerate from their previous vows of generating the mind. If one asks, "How will they degenerate?", how could there be awakening for that intention which is hateful and free from patience? There is none. At such a time, Māras along with their factions become utterly joyful in mind; and in particular, if whatever bodhisattva who has not received a prophecy becomes angry in mind and begins to dispute with a bodhisattva who has previously received a prophecy, since they are endowed with the fault of the ashes of afflictions, they must don the armor of patience anew for as many eons as the number of moments of that mind. The antidote to that sin, or the method to avert it, is patience; since all buddhas also touched supreme awakening by meditating on the perfection of patience, if one thinks, "This hateful mind is not good," one generates mindful regret, confesses individually through various antidotes, vows subsequently to refrain from such thoughts and actions, and does not rejoice in mind about what was done previously—that is training in this dharma of the Buddha's teaching.

heading: **དགེ་བ་ཐམས་ཅད་བསྡུད་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "perfection of wisdom" up to "is said to be subsumed": Within those trained without apprehension in the perfection of wisdom, which is the subsumer, all five perfections, generosity and so forth, will be subsumed within that wisdom that knows non-apprehension. For example, just as the sixty-two views are subsumed within the view of the transitory collection, similarly to that example, it is said that these five perfections are subsumed within the perfection of wisdom.

[2-224] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding this from "whenever a bodhisattva" up to "trains in this dharma of the Buddha": Furthermore, at whatever time some bodhisattvas fight with the body and dispute with speech, and mentally disagree with one another and become endowed with angry minds, at that time Māra and his retinue become joyful in mind, experience supreme comfort in body, and think thus: "Those two fighting and disputing bodhisattvas will become far from the wisdom of the Victor, so my purpose is accomplished"—thinking this, they become joyful in mind. In reality as well, the wisdom of those two bodhisattvas becomes distant, and as a cause they will become fierce flesh-eaters, and thus both will degenerate from their previous vows of generating the mind. If one asks, "How will they degenerate?", how could there be awakening for that intention which is hateful and free from patience? There is none. At such a time, Māras along with their factions become utterly joyful in mind; and in particular, if whatever bodhisattva who has not received a prophecy becomes angry in mind and begins to dispute with a bodhisattva who has previously received a prophecy, since they are endowed with the fault of the ashes of afflictions, they must don the armor of patience anew for as many eons as the number of moments of that mind. The antidote to that sin, or the method to avert it, is patience; since all buddhas also touched supreme awakening by meditating on the perfection of patience, if one thinks, "This hateful mind is not good," one generates mindful regret, confesses individually through various antidotes, vows subsequently to refrain from such thoughts and actions, and does not rejoice in mind about what was done previously—that is training in this dharma of the Buddha's teaching.

source: ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དེ་ལ་སྤྱིར་དབང་པོ་ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་གཉིས་ལས། རྣམ་བྱང་གི་དབང་པོ་ནི། དད་པའི་དབང་པོ་དང༌། དྲན་པའི་དང༌། བརྩོན་འགྲུས་ཀྱི་དང༌། ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་གྱི་དང༌། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་དང༌། མི་ཤེས་པ་ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་ཡི་དང༌། ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་དང༌། ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་གྲོལ་བས་དང་བརྒྱད། ཉོན་མོངས་པ་འཁོར་བའི་དང༌། མིག་གི་དབང་པོ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལྔ་དང༌། ཡིད་ཀྱི་དང་ཡིད་བདེ་མི་བདེ་གཉིས་དང༌། ཚོར་བའི་བདེ་སྡུག་བཏང་སྙོམས་གསུམ་དང༌། སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོ་དང༌། ཕོ་མོའི་དབང་པོ་གཉིས་ཏེ་བཅུ་བཞི་དེ་ལྟར་ན་དབང་པོ་ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་གཉིས་ཡོད་པ་ལས། དཔེར་ན་སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོ་གཅིག་པུ་འགགས་ན་དབང་པོ་རྩ་ཅིག་པོ་གཞན། གང་དག་ཇི་སྙེད་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་འགགས་པར་འགྱུར་བས་སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོར་དབང་པོ་གཞན་རྣམས་འདུས་པའོ། །དཔེ་དེ་ལྟར་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པའི་མཁས་པ་མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས། ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་ཐམས་ཅད་མི་དམིགས་པར་ཤེས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདིར་ནི་འདུས་པར་གསུངས་སོ། །
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding that, in general out of the twenty-two faculties, the faculties of purification are the eight: the faculty of faith, of mindfulness, of diligence, of concentration, of wisdom, of coming to know the unknown, of knowing all, and of being liberated through knowing all; and those of afflictive cyclic existence are the fourteen: the five faculties of the eye and so forth, of the mind, the two of mental happiness and unhappiness, the three feelings of pleasure, pain, and equanimity, the life faculty, and the two male and female faculties; out of those twenty-two faculties that thus exist, for example, if the single life faculty ceases, all however many of the other twenty-one faculties will cease, so the other faculties are subsumed in the life faculty. Just like that example, it is said by those who have become supreme wise ones engaging in the perfection of wisdom that all five perfections are subsumed within this perfection of wisdom that knows non-apprehension.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "at that time" up to "sends shooting stars": Furthermore, at that time, Māra, thinking, "This bodhisattva will be victorious over my battle," his mind becomes endowed with a pang of pain, his mind exhausted by sorrow, his body suffering with illness, his feelings mentally unhappy, and he is feeble due to the shrinking of the courage of body and mind. Furthermore, still thinking, "By doing what, how will the mind of this bodhisattva withdraw from the conduct of awakening?", in order to show fear through his actions, he burns the regions in their vicinity with fire and from above sends shooting stars, that is, thunderbolts.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "whenever the wise" up to "how could they": Nevertheless, whenever those wise bodhisattvas, endowed with love and compassion with intense intention, in their application look at the meaning of the supreme perfection of wisdom without difference of day and night. At that time, the body, mind, and speech, the three, of that bodhisattva become free from the two extremes or unharmed, like a bird going in the sky; and even if Māra and the dark partisans included in his retinue look for an opportunity regarding them, how could they find an opportunity? Thus it is said: Regarding this from "whenever a bodhisattva" up to "trains in this dharma of the Buddha": Furthermore, at whatever time some bodhisattvas fight with the body and dispute with speech, and mentally disagree with one another and become endowed with angry minds, at that time Māra and his retinue become joyful in mind, experience supreme comfort in body, and think thus: "Those two fighting and disputing bodhisattvas will become far from the wisdom of the Victor, so my purpose is accomplished"—thinking this, they become joyful in mind. In reality as well, the wisdom of those two bodhisattvas becomes distant, and as a cause they will become fierce flesh-eaters, and thus both will degenerate from their previous vows of generating the mind. If one asks, "How will they degenerate?", how could there be awakening for that intention which is hateful and free from patience? There is none. At such a time, Māras along with their factions become utterly joyful in mind; and in particular, if whatever bodhisattva who has not received a prophecy becomes angry in mind and begins to dispute with a bodhisattva who has previously received a prophecy, since they are endowed with the fault of the ashes of afflictions, they must don the armor of patience anew for as many eons as the number of moments of that mind. The antidote to that sin, or the method to avert it, is patience; since all buddhas also touched supreme awakening by meditating on the perfection of patience, if one thinks, "This hateful mind is not good," one generates mindful regret, confesses individually through various antidotes, vows subsequently to refrain from such thoughts and actions, and does not rejoice in mind about what was done previously—that is training in this dharma of the Buddha's teaching.

translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "the wise bodhisattva" up to "therefore trains": Whatever clear, wise bodhisattva trains for the sake of others in whatever qualities of a śrāvaka there are and similarly in all qualities of a pratyekabuddha, those bodhisattvas do not abide by way of attachment to those qualities, nor do they generate desire for them by way of tasting their flavor. Thinking, "These qualities of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are what is to be trained in by bodhisattvas for the sake of others," they train for that reason for others as well.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "whenever a bodhisattva" up to "trains in this dharma of the Buddha": Furthermore, at whatever time some bodhisattvas fight with the body and dispute with speech, and mentally disagree with one another and become endowed with angry minds, at that time Māra and his retinue become joyful in mind, experience supreme comfort in body, and think thus: "Those two fighting and disputing bodhisattvas will become far from the wisdom of the Victor, so my purpose is accomplished"—thinking this, they become joyful in mind. In reality as well, the wisdom of those two bodhisattvas becomes distant, and as a cause they will become fierce flesh-eaters, and thus both will degenerate from their previous vows of generating the mind. If one asks, "How will they degenerate?", how could there be awakening for that intention which is hateful and free from patience? There is none. At such a time, Māras along with their factions become utterly joyful in mind; and in particular, if whatever bodhisattva who has not received a prophecy becomes angry in mind and begins to dispute with a bodhisattva who has previously received a prophecy, since they are endowed with the fault of the ashes of afflictions, they must don the armor of patience anew for as many eons as the number of moments of that mind. The antidote to that sin, or the method to avert it, is patience; since all buddhas also touched supreme awakening by meditating on the perfection of patience, if one thinks, "This hateful mind is not good," one generates mindful regret, confesses individually through various antidotes, vows subsequently to refrain from such thoughts and actions, and does not rejoice in mind about what was done previously—that is training in this dharma of the Buddha's teaching.

translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "non-returning awakening" up to "gives the gift of dharma": If some person who has thoroughly entered into the supreme non-returning awakening sincerely rejoices in the generation of the mind by another person, as for the example of grasping the limit of permanence: it would be possible to grasp the measure of the number of ounces by weighing on a balance the trichiliocosm together with Mount Meru, or Mount Meru itself, but the virtue arisen from that aforementioned rejoicing is not possible to be grasped in that way. བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཞེས་པ་ནས། དེ་ལྟར་སློབ་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། ཡང་རྟེན་གྱི་གང་ཟག་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གང་ཞིག་དེ་ལྟར་མ་གཏོགས་པའི་བསླབ་པ་འདི་ཤེས་པ་འདི་གཞན་ཡང་བསླབ་པ་གཉིས་པོ་ཉམས་ཤིང་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་འཆལ་བར་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ་ཉམས་པའི་རྒྱུ་མི་དམིགས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ནི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་ཀྱིས་མཉེས་པར་བྱ་བའི་ཕྱིར་ཡུལ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་མཆོག་འདི་ལ་སློབ་སྟེ། དེ་ལྟ་བུའི་བསླབ་པ་དེ་ནི་ལྷག་པའི་སེམས་དེ་དང་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་གཉིས་ལས། བསླབ་པ་འདི་ལྷག་པའི་སེམས་ཀྱི་བསླབ་པ་ཡིན་པས་དེ་ལ་མཁས་ཏེ་དམིགས་པ་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ནི་མ་རིག་པ་སེལ་བ་ལ་མཁས་པའི་འོད་བྱེད་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་མི་དམིགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ལ་དེ་ལྟར་སློབ་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །
[2-228] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "a bodhisattva" up to "trains thus": Furthermore, whatever base person, a bodhisattva, who knows this training not included in that, will also not degenerate in the two trainings and become corrupted in ethical discipline, because they do not apprehend a cause of degeneration. In order to please through the dharma of the Buddha, they train in this supreme perfection of wisdom, the object; regarding such a training, out of those two—higher mind and ethical discipline—this training is the training of higher mind, so they are wise in it, because of non-apprehension. Thus they train in the non-apprehending wisdom of the light-makers who are wise in dispelling ignorance.

[2-229] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དགེ་བ་མ་ཡིན་ཞེས་པ་ནས། མི་གནས་བཞིན་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། དེ་ཡང་དེ་ལྟར་སློབ་པ་དེ་ལ་ཆགས་སྡང་དང་གཏི་མུག་མེད་པས་དགེ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པའི་སེམས་སྐད་ཅིག་ཙམ་ཡང་བསྐྱེད་པར་མི་བྱེད་དོ། །དཔེར་ན་ཉི་མ་མཁའ་ལ་འགྲོ་བ་བཞིན་ནོ། །

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "non-virtuous" up to "as if not abiding": Moreover, since that one training thus does not have attachment, hatred, or delusion, they do not generate a non-virtuous mind even for a mere moment. For example, it is like the sun moving in the sky.

[2-230] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་ཞེས་པ་ནས། འདུས་པར་གསུངས་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། བསྡུ་བྱེད་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་དམིགས་མེད་དུ་བསླབ་པར་བྱས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་ནང་དུ། སྦྱིན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་པོ་ཐམས་ཅད་མི་དམིགས་པར་ཤེས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་དེར་འདུས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །དཔེར་ན་འཇིགས་ཚོགས་ཀྱི་ལྟ་བར་བལྟ་བ་དྲུག་ཅུ་རྩ་གཉིས་འདུས་པ་ལྟར་དུ། དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་པོ་འདི་དག་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་ནང་དུ་འདུས་པར་གསུངས་སོ། །
[2-230] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding this from "perfection of wisdom" up to "is said to be subsumed": Within those trained without apprehension in the perfection of wisdom, which is the subsumer, all five perfections, generosity and so forth, will be subsumed within that wisdom that knows non-apprehension. For example, just as the sixty-two views are subsumed within the view of the transitory collection, similarly to that example, it is said that these five perfections are subsumed within the perfection of wisdom.

[2-231] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དེ་ལ་སྤྱིར་དབང་པོ་ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་གཉིས་ལས། རྣམ་བྱང་གི་དབང་པོ་ནི། དད་པའི་དབང་པོ་དང༌། དྲན་པའི་དང༌། བརྩོན་འགྲུས་ཀྱི་དང༌། ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་གྱི་དང༌། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་དང༌། མི་ཤེས་པ་ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་ཡི་དང༌། ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་དང༌། ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་གྲོལ་བས་དང་བརྒྱད། ཉོན་མོངས་པ་འཁོར་བའི་དང༌། མིག་གི་དབང་པོ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལྔ་དང༌། ཡིད་ཀྱི་དང་ཡིད་བདེ་མི་བདེ་གཉིས་དང༌། ཚོར་བའི་བདེ་སྡུག་བཏང་སྙོམས་གསུམ་དང༌། སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོ་དང༌། ཕོ་མོའི་དབང་པོ་གཉིས་ཏེ་བཅུ་བཞི་དེ་ལྟར་ན་དབང་པོ་ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་གཉིས་ཡོད་པ་ལས། དཔེར་ན་སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོ་གཅིག་པུ་འགགས་ན་དབང་པོ་རྩ་ཅིག་པོ་གཞན། གང་དག་ཇི་སྙེད་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་འགགས་པར་འགྱུར་བས་སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོར་དབང་པོ་གཞན་རྣམས་འདུས་པའོ། །དཔེ་དེ་ལྟར་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པའི་མཁས་པ་མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས། ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་ཐམས་ཅད་མི་དམིགས་པར་ཤེས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདིར་ནི་འདུས་པར་གསུངས་སོ། །
[2-231] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding that, in general out of the twenty-two faculties, the faculties of purification are the eight: the faculty of faith, of mindfulness, of diligence, of concentration, of wisdom, of coming to know the unknown, of knowing all, and of being liberated through knowing all; and those of afflictive cyclic existence are the fourteen: the five faculties of the eye and so forth, of the mind, the two of mental happiness and unhappiness, the three feelings of pleasure, pain, and equanimity, the life faculty, and the two male and female faculties; out of those twenty-two faculties that thus exist, for example, if the single life faculty ceases, all however many of the other twenty-one faculties will cease, so the other faculties are subsumed in the life faculty. Just like that example, it is said by those who have become supreme wise ones engaging in the perfection of wisdom that all five perfections are subsumed within this perfection of wisdom that knows non-apprehension.

[2-232] source:
ཅེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་མཁས་ཞེས་པ་ནས། དེ་ཕྱིར་སློབ་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་མཁས་པ་གསལ་བ་གང་ཞིག་ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་ཡོན་ཏན་གང་ཞིག་ཡོད་པ་དང༌། དེ་བཞིན་དུ་རང་རྒྱལ་བའི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཀུན་ལ་གཞན་དོན་དུ་སློབ་པར་བྱེད་ཅིང༌། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་དག་ཡོན་ཏན་དེ་ལ་ཞེན་པའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་མི་གནས་པ། རོ་མྱང་བའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་འདོད་པ་མི་བསྐྱེད་དོ། །ཉན་རང་གི་ཡོན་ཏན་འདི་ནི་གཞན་དོན་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དག་གི་བསླབ་བྱ་ཡིན་སྙམ་ནས་གཞན་ལ་ཡང་དེའི་ཕྱིར་སློབ་པའོ། །
[2-232] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding this from "the wise bodhisattva" up to "therefore trains": Whatever clear, wise bodhisattva trains for the sake of others in whatever qualities of a śrāvaka there are and similarly in all qualities of a pratyekabuddha, those bodhisattvas do not abide by way of attachment to those qualities, nor do they generate desire for them by way of tasting their flavor. Thinking, "These qualities of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are what is to be trained in by bodhisattvas for the sake of others," they train for that reason for others as well.

heading: **མི་རྟོག་པའི་སྤྱོད་པ་ཐོབ་པ།**
translation: up to "engages in thorough peace": Whatever bodhisattva with a non-conceptual mind thoroughly knows all phenomena, form and so forth, as emptiness empty of essence, signlessness empty of causes, and wishlessness empty of results, this practitioner who does not seek awakening by means of wisdom through the two of apprehender and apprehended, or through the two selflessnesses, strives in the supreme perfection of wisdom that knows non-apprehension. For example, between the space realm of the eastern direction and the space of the western direction, there is no high and low, long and short, or any such contradiction, and no person whatsoever will obtain the meaning of them being different. Just like that example, the three doors of a wise bodhisattva who engages in the wisdom that knows non-apprehension are also without any conceptuality; the example is like space, and for the bodhisattva this conceptuality of near and far is thoroughly pacified and they engage in thorough peace.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "the wise bodhisattva" up to "therefore trains": Whatever clear, wise bodhisattva trains for the sake of others in whatever qualities of a śrāvaka there are and similarly in all qualities of a pratyekabuddha, those bodhisattvas do not abide by way of attachment to those qualities, nor do they generate desire for them by way of tasting their flavor. Thinking, "These qualities of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are what is to be trained in by bodhisattvas for the sake of others," they train for that reason for others as well.

heading: **སྒྱུ་མའི་དཔེ།**
translation: Regarding this from "in the midst of beings" up to "engages without conceptualization": If one says, 'Even so, it is unjustified to perform the activities of adopting and discarding,' there is no contradiction; just like the example of an illusory person, a wise one who engages in wisdom does not think, 'Having realized and attained awakening, I will thoroughly liberate wandering sentient beings from suffering,' yet because they have attained mastery over birth, they are endowed with many activities, such as demonstrating various births to tame whoever needs taming however they need to be tamed, and the four means of gathering. Even while demonstrating the example of an illusory person, they engage in non-conceptual mind.

[2-228] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "a bodhisattva" up to "trains thus": Furthermore, whatever base person, a bodhisattva, who knows this training not included in that, will also not degenerate in the two trainings and become corrupted in ethical discipline, because they do not apprehend a cause of degeneration. In order to please through the dharma of the Buddha, they train in this supreme perfection of wisdom, the object; regarding such a training, out of those two—higher mind and ethical discipline—this training is the training of higher mind, so they are wise in it, because of non-apprehension. Thus they train in the non-apprehending wisdom of the light-makers who are wise in dispelling ignorance.

ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དགེ་བ་མ་ཡིན་ཞེས་པ་ནས། མི་གནས་བཞིན་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། དེ་ཡང་དེ་ལྟར་སློབ་པ་དེ་ལ་ཆགས་སྡང་དང་གཏི་མུག་མེད་པས་དགེ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པའི་སེམས་སྐད་ཅིག་ཙམ་ཡང་བསྐྱེད་པར་མི་བྱེད་དོ། །དཔེར་ན་ཉི་མ་མཁའ་ལ་འགྲོ་བ་བཞིན་ནོ། །

ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་ཞེས་པ་ནས། འདུས་པར་གསུངས་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། བསྡུ་བྱེད་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་དམིགས་མེད་དུ་བསླབ་པར་བྱས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་ནང་དུ། སྦྱིན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་པོ་ཐམས་ཅད་མི་དམིགས་པར་ཤེས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་དེར་འདུས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །དཔེར་ན་འཇིགས་ཚོགས་ཀྱི་ལྟ་བར་བལྟ་བ་དྲུག་ཅུ་རྩ་གཉིས་འདུས་པ་ལྟར་དུ། དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་པོ་འདི་དག་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་ནང་དུ་འདུས་པར་གསུངས་སོ། །

[2-231] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དེ་ལ་སྤྱིར་དབང་པོ་ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་གཉིས་ལས། རྣམ་བྱང་གི་དབང་པོ་ནི། དད་པའི་དབང་པོ་དང༌། དྲན་པའི་དང༌། བརྩོན་འགྲུས་ཀྱི་དང༌། ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་གྱི་དང༌། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་དང༌། མི་ཤེས་པ་ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་ཡི་དང༌། ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་དང༌། ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་གྲོལ་བས་དང་བརྒྱད། ཉོན་མོངས་པ་འཁོར་བའི་དང༌། མིག་གི་དབང་པོ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལྔ་དང༌། ཡིད་ཀྱི་དང་ཡིད་བདེ་མི་བདེ་གཉིས་དང༌། ཚོར་བའི་བདེ་སྡུག་བཏང་སྙོམས་གསུམ་དང༌། སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོ་དང༌། ཕོ་མོའི་དབང་པོ་གཉིས་ཏེ་བཅུ་བཞི་དེ་ལྟར་ན་དབང་པོ་ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་གཉིས་ཡོད་པ་ལས། དཔེར་ན་སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོ་གཅིག་པུ་འགགས་ན་དབང་པོ་རྩ་ཅིག་པོ་གཞན། གང་དག་ཇི་སྙེད་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་འགགས་པར་འགྱུར་བས་སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོར་དབང་པོ་གཞན་རྣམས་འདུས་པའོ། །དཔེ་དེ་ལྟར་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པའི་མཁས་པ་མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས། ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་ཐམས་ཅད་མི་དམིགས་པར་ཤེས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདིར་ནི་འདུས་པར་གསུངས་སོ། །
[2-231] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding that, in general out of the twenty-two faculties, the faculties of purification are the eight: the faculty of faith, of mindfulness, of diligence, of concentration, of wisdom, of coming to know the unknown, of knowing all, and of being liberated through knowing all; and those of afflictive cyclic existence are the fourteen: the five faculties of the eye and so forth, of the mind, the two of mental happiness and unhappiness, the three feelings of pleasure, pain, and equanimity, the life faculty, and the two male and female faculties; out of those twenty-two faculties that thus exist, for example, if the single life faculty ceases, all however many of the other twenty-one faculties will cease, so the other faculties are subsumed in the life faculty. Just like that example, it is said by those who have become supreme wise ones engaging in the perfection of wisdom that all five perfections are subsumed within this perfection of wisdom that knows non-apprehension.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "the wise bodhisattva" up to "therefore trains": Whatever clear, wise bodhisattva trains for the sake of others in whatever qualities of a śrāvaka there are and similarly in all qualities of a pratyekabuddha, those bodhisattvas do not abide by way of attachment to those qualities, nor do they generate desire for them by way of tasting their flavor. Thinking, "These qualities of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are what is to be trained in by bodhisattvas for the sake of others," they train for that reason for others as well.

heading: **སྤྲུལ་པའི་དཔེ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "For example, a buddha" up to "demonstrates all": Just like the example of a buddha's emanation, a wise bodhisattva who engages in the perfection of wisdom that knows non-apprehension also demonstrates all activities of taming wanderers without conceit and pride, like that emanation of a buddha and the illusory person.

[2-228] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "a bodhisattva" up to "trains thus": Furthermore, whatever base person, a bodhisattva, who knows this training not included in that, will also not degenerate in the two trainings and become corrupted in ethical discipline, because they do not apprehend a cause of degeneration. In order to please through the dharma of the Buddha, they train in this supreme perfection of wisdom, the object; regarding such a training, out of those two—higher mind and ethical discipline—this training is the training of higher mind, so they are wise in it, because of non-apprehension. Thus they train in the non-apprehending wisdom of the light-makers who are wise in dispelling ignorance.

ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དགེ་བ་མ་ཡིན་ཞེས་པ་ནས། མི་གནས་བཞིན་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། དེ་ཡང་དེ་ལྟར་སློབ་པ་དེ་ལ་ཆགས་སྡང་དང་གཏི་མུག་མེད་པས་དགེ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པའི་སེམས་སྐད་ཅིག་ཙམ་ཡང་བསྐྱེད་པར་མི་བྱེད་དོ། །དཔེར་ན་ཉི་མ་མཁའ་ལ་འགྲོ་བ་བཞིན་ནོ། །

ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་ཞེས་པ་ནས། འདུས་པར་གསུངས་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། བསྡུ་བྱེད་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་དམིགས་མེད་དུ་བསླབ་པར་བྱས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་ནང་དུ། སྦྱིན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་པོ་ཐམས་ཅད་མི་དམིགས་པར་ཤེས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་དེར་འདུས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །དཔེར་ན་འཇིགས་ཚོགས་ཀྱི་ལྟ་བར་བལྟ་བ་དྲུག་ཅུ་རྩ་གཉིས་འདུས་པ་ལྟར་དུ། དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་པོ་འདི་དག་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་ནང་དུ་འདུས་པར་གསུངས་སོ། །
