For example, just as the sixty-two views are subsumed within the view of the transitory collection, similarly to that example, it is said that these five perfections are subsumed within the perfection of wisdom.

[2-231] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དེ་ལ་སྤྱིར་དབང་པོ་ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་གཉིས་ལས། རྣམ་བྱང་གི་དབང་པོ་ནི། དད་པའི་དབང་པོ་དང༌། དྲན་པའི་དང༌། བརྩོན་འགྲུས་ཀྱི་དང༌། ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་གྱི་དང༌། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་དང༌། མི་ཤེས་པ་ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་ཡི་དང༌། ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་དང༌། ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་གྲོལ་བས་དང་བརྒྱད། ཉོན་མོངས་པ་འཁོར་བའི་དང༌། མིག་གི་དབང་པོ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལྔ་དང༌། ཡིད་ཀྱི་དང་ཡིད་བདེ་མི་བདེ་གཉིས་དང༌། ཚོར་བའི་བདེ་སྡུག་བཏང་སྙོམས་གསུམ་དང༌། སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོ་དང༌། ཕོ་མོའི་དབང་པོ་གཉིས་ཏེ་བཅུ་བཞི་དེ་ལྟར་ན་དབང་པོ་ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་གཉིས་ཡོད་པ་ལས། དཔེར་ན་སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོ་གཅིག་པུ་འགགས་ན་དབང་པོ་རྩ་ཅིག་པོ་གཞན། གང་དག་ཇི་སྙེད་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་འགགས་པར་འགྱུར་བས་སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོར་དབང་པོ་གཞན་རྣམས་འདུས་པའོ། །དཔེ་དེ་ལྟར་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པའི་མཁས་པ་མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས། ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་ཐམས་ཅད་མི་དམིགས་པར་ཤེས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདིར་ནི་འདུས་པར་གསུངས་སོ། །
[2-231] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding that, in general out of the twenty-two faculties, the faculties of purification are the eight: the faculty of faith, of mindfulness, of diligence, of concentration, of wisdom, of coming to know the unknown, of knowing all, and of being liberated through knowing all; and those of afflictive cyclic existence are the fourteen: the five faculties of the eye and so forth, of the mind, the two of mental happiness and unhappiness, the three feelings of pleasure, pain, and equanimity, the life faculty, and the two male and female faculties; out of those twenty-two faculties that thus exist, for example, if the single life faculty ceases, all however many of the other twenty-one faculties will cease, so the other faculties are subsumed in the life faculty. Just like that example, it is said by those who have become supreme wise ones engaging in the perfection of wisdom that all five perfections are subsumed within this perfection of wisdom that knows non-apprehension.

[2-232] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding this from "the wise bodhisattva" up to "therefore trains": Whatever clear, wise bodhisattva trains for the sake of others in whatever qualities of a śrāvaka there are and similarly in all qualities of a pratyekabuddha, those bodhisattvas do not abide by way of attachment to those qualities, nor do they generate desire for them by way of tasting their flavor. Thinking, "These qualities of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are what is to be trained in by bodhisattvas for the sake of others," they train for that reason for others as well.

heading: **ཤིང་གི་སྐྱེས་བུའི་དཔེ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "a carpenter artisan" up to "performs all": Just like the example of a person made by a carpenter artisan, a wise bodhisattva who engages in the perfection of wisdom also appears to perform all activities of pristine wisdom even while having a non-conceptual mind.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "the wise bodhisattva" up to "therefore trains": Whatever clear, wise bodhisattva trains for the sake of others in whatever qualities of a śrāvaka there are and similarly in all qualities of a pratyekabuddha, those bodhisattvas do not abide by way of attachment to those qualities, nor do they generate desire for them by way of tasting their flavor. Thinking, "These qualities of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are what is to be trained in by bodhisattvas for the sake of others," they train for that reason for others as well.

བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཞེས་པ་ནས། དེ་ལྟར་སློབ་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། ཡང་རྟེན་གྱི་གང་ཟག་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གང་ཞིག་དེ་ལྟར་མ་གཏོགས་པའི་བསླབ་པ་འདི་ཤེས་པ་འདི་གཞན་ཡང་བསླབ་པ་གཉིས་པོ་ཉམས་ཤིང་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་འཆལ་བར་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ་ཉམས་པའི་རྒྱུ་མི་དམིགས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ནི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་ཀྱིས་མཉེས་པར་བྱ་བའི་ཕྱིར་ཡུལ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་མཆོག་འདི་ལ་སློབ་སྟེ། དེ་ལྟ་བུའི་བསླབ་པ་དེ་ནི་ལྷག་པའི་སེམས་དེ་དང་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་གཉིས་ལས། བསླབ་པ་འདི་ལྷག་པའི་སེམས་ཀྱི་བསླབ་པ་ཡིན་པས་དེ་ལ་མཁས་ཏེ་དམིགས་པ་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ནི་མ་རིག་པ་སེལ་བ་ལ་མཁས་པའི་འོད་བྱེད་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་མི་དམིགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ལ་དེ་ལྟར་སློབ་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །
[2-228] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "a bodhisattva" up to "trains thus": Furthermore, whatever base person, a bodhisattva, who knows this training not included in that, will also not degenerate in the two trainings and become corrupted in ethical discipline, because they do not apprehend a cause of degeneration. In order to please through the dharma of the Buddha, they train in this supreme perfection of wisdom, the object; regarding such a training, out of those two—higher mind and ethical discipline—this training is the training of higher mind, so they are wise in it, because of non-apprehension. Thus they train in the non-apprehending wisdom of the light-makers who are wise in dispelling ignorance.

[2-229] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དགེ་བ་མ་ཡིན་ཞེས་པ་ནས། མི་གནས་བཞིན་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། དེ་ཡང་དེ་ལྟར་སློབ་པ་དེ་ལ་ཆགས་སྡང་དང་གཏི་མུག་མེད་པས་དགེ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པའི་སེམས་སྐད་ཅིག་ཙམ་ཡང་བསྐྱེད་པར་མི་བྱེད་དོ། །དཔེར་ན་ཉི་མ་མཁའ་ལ་འགྲོ་བ་བཞིན་ནོ། །
[2-229] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding this from "non-virtuous" up to "as if not abiding": Moreover, since that one training thus does not have attachment, hatred, or delusion, they do not generate a non-virtuous mind even for a mere moment. For example, it is like the sun moving in the sky.

[2-230] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་ཞེས་པ་ནས། འདུས་པར་གསུངས་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། བསྡུ་བྱེད་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་དམིགས་མེད་དུ་བསླབ་པར་བྱས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་ནང་དུ། སྦྱིན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་པོ་ཐམས་ཅད་མི་དམིགས་པར་ཤེས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་དེར་འདུས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །དཔེར་ན་འཇིགས་ཚོགས་ཀྱི་ལྟ་བར་བལྟ་བ་དྲུག་ཅུ་རྩ་གཉིས་འདུས་པ་ལྟར་དུ། དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་པོ་འདི་དག་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་ནང་དུ་འདུས་པར་གསུངས་སོ། །
[2-230] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding this from "perfection of wisdom" up to "is said to be subsumed": Within those trained without apprehension in the perfection of wisdom, which is the subsumer, all five perfections, generosity and so forth, will be subsumed within that wisdom that knows non-apprehension. For example, just as the sixty-two views are subsumed within the view of the transitory collection, similarly to that example, it is said that these five perfections are subsumed within the perfection of wisdom.

[2-231] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དེ་ལ་སྤྱིར་དབང་པོ་ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་གཉིས་ལས། རྣམ་བྱང་གི་དབང་པོ་ནི། དད་པའི་དབང་པོ་དང༌། དྲན་པའི་དང༌། བརྩོན་འགྲུས་ཀྱི་དང༌། ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་གྱི་དང༌། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་དང༌། མི་ཤེས་པ་ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་ཡི་དང༌། ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་དང༌། ཀུན་ཤེས་པ་གྲོལ་བས་དང་བརྒྱད། ཉོན་མོངས་པ་འཁོར་བའི་དང༌། མིག་གི་དབང་པོ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལྔ་དང༌། ཡིད་ཀྱི་དང་ཡིད་བདེ་མི་བདེ་གཉིས་དང༌། ཚོར་བའི་བདེ་སྡུག་བཏང་སྙོམས་གསུམ་དང༌། སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོ་དང༌། ཕོ་མོའི་དབང་པོ་གཉིས་ཏེ་བཅུ་བཞི་དེ་ལྟར་ན་དབང་པོ་ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་གཉིས་ཡོད་པ་ལས། དཔེར་ན་སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོ་གཅིག་པུ་འགགས་ན་དབང་པོ་རྩ་ཅིག་པོ་གཞན། གང་དག་ཇི་སྙེད་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་འགགས་པར་འགྱུར་བས་སྲོག་གི་དབང་པོར་དབང་པོ་གཞན་རྣམས་འདུས་པའོ། །དཔེ་དེ་ལྟར་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པའི་མཁས་པ་མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས། ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལྔ་ཐམས་ཅད་མི་དམིགས་པར་ཤེས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདིར་ནི་འདུས་པར་གསུངས་སོ། །
[2-231] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding that, in general out of the twenty-two faculties, the faculties of purification are the eight: the faculty of faith, of mindfulness, of diligence, of concentration, of wisdom, of coming to know the unknown, of knowing all, and of being liberated through knowing all; and those of afflictive cyclic existence are the fourteen: the five faculties of the eye and so forth, of the mind, the two of mental happiness and unhappiness, the three feelings of pleasure, pain, and equanimity, the life faculty, and the two male and female faculties; out of those twenty-two faculties that thus exist, for example, if the single life faculty ceases, all however many of the other twenty-one faculties will cease, so the other faculties are subsumed in the life faculty. Just like that example, it is said by those who have become supreme wise ones engaging in the perfection of wisdom that all five perfections are subsumed within this perfection of wisdom that knows non-apprehension.

[2-232] source:
ཅེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་མཁས་ཞེས་པ་ནས། དེ་ཕྱིར་སློབ་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་མཁས་པ་གསལ་བ་གང་ཞིག་ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་ཡོན་ཏན་གང་ཞིག་ཡོད་པ་དང༌། དེ་བཞིན་དུ་རང་རྒྱལ་བའི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཀུན་ལ་གཞན་དོན་དུ་སློབ་པར་བྱེད་ཅིང༌། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་དག་ཡོན་ཏན་དེ་ལ་ཞེན་པའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་མི་གནས་པ། རོ་མྱང་བའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་འདོད་པ་མི་བསྐྱེད་དོ། །ཉན་རང་གི་ཡོན་ཏན་འདི་ནི་གཞན་དོན་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དག་གི་བསླབ་བྱ་ཡིན་སྙམ་ནས་གཞན་ལ་ཡང་དེའི་ཕྱིར་སློབ་པའོ། །
[2-232] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding this from "the wise bodhisattva" up to "therefore trains": Whatever clear, wise bodhisattva trains for the sake of others in whatever qualities of a śrāvaka there are and similarly in all qualities of a pratyekabuddha, those bodhisattvas do not abide by way of attachment to those qualities, nor do they generate desire for them by way of tasting their flavor. Thinking, "These qualities of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are what is to be trained in by bodhisattvas for the sake of others," they train for that reason for others as well.

heading: **ལྷས་བསྐུལ་བ།**
translation: Regarding this from "Wise ones who engage thus" up to "pay homage": The many hosts of gods of the desire and form realms join their palms, bow down, and pay homage in the direction where that bodhisattva, those wise ones who engage in such a manner and are revered by the gods, dwells.

heading: **བདུད་ཀྱིས་མི་རྫི་བ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "equal to the river Ganges" up to "endowed with the blessings": Furthermore, even if all however many sentient beings there are in fields equal to the sand grains of the river Ganges assume a completely contrived intention and become māras, and even if from each single hair pore of each of those who have become māras, they emanate that many māras of the east, all those māras would not be able to create obstacles for that wise bodhisattva. Thus, due to four causes, the bodhisattva who is skillful in means and endowed with the power of wisdom is difficult to defeat by the four māras such as the māra of the deity's son, and they cannot produce even the slightest obstacle. What are the four causes? (1) Because their own mind abides in the natural state as empty, there is no one who creates obstacles ultimately; (2) conventionally, they do not completely abandon with great compassion the sentient beings who have not realized the ultimate; (3) they act without degenerating from whatever they have said and promised; and (4) such a one is blessed by the sugatas who are endowed with blessings.

heading: **བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ངོས་བཟུང་བ།**
translation: Regarding this from "dharmadhātu suchness" up to "is not the station": They will not abide by way of mental clinging to the basis, the dharmadhātu suchness, and regarding non-abiding, for example, they abide without abiding on any object of observation whatsoever, like clouds abiding in the sky. Furthermore, for example, a mantra-holder also desires to move and abide in the sky without abiding, and furthermore, through the power of accomplishing mantras, they bless a dry tree to possess flowers at a time that is not the season for them to grow, like winter. Like those examples, whatever bodhisattva engages in that way, who is skillful in means and endowed with bright faculties and intelligent intellect, will not observe the path that makes oneself empty, the result, the qualities of a buddha, the powers, and so forth. They do not observe looking at the master who explains the Dharma and the student who desires the Dharma, because they are indivisible. It is not appropriate to be the station or basis of a bodhisattva who rejoices in accomplishing the qualities, desiring to pacify the suffering of oneself and others.

translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "arhats' liberation" up to "will not pass away": Furthermore, apart from the eight liberations of the arhats and the liberations possessed in the continuums of the tathāgatas, this station of the bodhisattvas is the supreme and the highest of all however many stations there are of the noble śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, which are endowed with physical bliss and where the mind is thoroughly joyful through the undefiled bliss of the meditative concentration of dhyāna that pacifies afflictions. If one says that it is not tenable that, if one meditates on non-observation, the afflictions will be exhausted and one will not pass into nirvāṇa, it is tenable: just as a bird abides in the empty sky but does not fall down, and a fish abides in water but does not die by suffocating in the water; likewise, the bodhisattva goes to the other shore of saṃsāra through the four dhyānas of non-abiding and the ten powers, and although they abide in the emptiness of wisdom, through the means of great compassion they will not attain nirvāṇa.

Thus, due to four causes, the bodhisattva who is skillful in means and endowed with the power of wisdom is difficult to defeat by the four māras such as the māra of the deity's son, and they cannot produce even the slightest obstacle. What are the four causes? (1) Because their own mind abides in the natural state as empty, there is no one who creates obstacles ultimately; (2) conventionally, they do not completely abandon with great compassion the sentient beings who have not realized the ultimate; (3) they act without degenerating from whatever they have said and promised; and (4) such a one is blessed by the sugatas who are endowed with blessings.

Furthermore, for example, a mantra-holder also desires to move and abide in the sky without abiding, and furthermore, through the power of accomplishing mantras, they bless a dry tree to possess flowers at a time that is not the season for them to grow, like winter. Like those examples, whatever bodhisattva engages in that way, who is skillful in means and endowed with bright faculties and intelligent intellect, will not observe the path that makes oneself empty, the result, the qualities of a buddha, the powers, and so forth. They do not observe looking at the master who explains the Dharma and the student who desires the Dharma, because they are indivisible. Thus, due to four causes, the bodhisattva who is skillful in means and endowed with the power of wisdom is difficult to defeat by the four māras such as the māra of the deity's son, and they cannot produce even the slightest obstacle. What are the four causes? (1) Because their own mind abides in the natural state as empty, there is no one who creates obstacles ultimately; (2) conventionally, they do not completely abandon with great compassion the sentient beings who have not realized the ultimate; (3) they act without degenerating from whatever they have said and promised; and (4) such a one is blessed by the sugatas who are endowed with blessings.

Regarding this from "dharmadhātu suchness" up to "is not the station": They will not abide by way of mental clinging to the basis, the dharmadhātu suchness, and regarding non-abiding, for example, they abide without abiding on any object of observation whatsoever, like clouds abiding in the sky. Furthermore, for example, a mantra-holder also desires to move and abide in the sky without abiding, and furthermore, through the power of accomplishing mantras, they bless a dry tree to possess flowers at a time that is not the season for them to grow, like winter. Like those examples, whatever bodhisattva engages in that way, who is skillful in means and endowed with bright faculties and intelligent intellect, will not observe the path that makes oneself empty, the result, the qualities of a buddha, the powers, and so forth. They do not observe looking at the master who explains the Dharma and the student who desires the Dharma, because they are indivisible. It is not appropriate to be the station or basis of a bodhisattva who rejoices in accomplishing the qualities, desiring to pacify the suffering of oneself and others.

heading: **མཆོག་གི་རྒྱུ་བསླབ་བྱ་བསྟན་པ།**
translation: Regarding this from "this training" up to "train in this perfection": This training of non-abiding is thoroughly proclaimed by the guides to be the training of the Mahāyāna path, and among all however many trainings are proclaimed, such as the training in higher ethical discipline and the training in higher mind, there is nothing more supreme and higher than this training in wisdom. Therefore, whichever wise ones desire to go to the perfection of all trainings should train in this perfection of wisdom, the training that is the unshared path of the buddhas.

Like those examples, whatever bodhisattva engages in that way, who is skillful in means and endowed with bright faculties and intelligent intellect, will not observe the path that makes oneself empty, the result, the qualities of a buddha, the powers, and so forth. They do not observe looking at the master who explains the Dharma and the student who desires the Dharma, because they are indivisible. It is not appropriate to be the station or basis of a bodhisattva who rejoices in accomplishing the qualities, desiring to pacify the suffering of oneself and others.

Furthermore, for example, a mantra-holder also desires to move and abide in the sky without abiding, and furthermore, through the power of accomplishing mantras, they bless a dry tree to possess flowers at a time that is not the season for them to grow, like winter. Like those examples, whatever bodhisattva engages in that way, who is skillful in means and endowed with bright faculties and intelligent intellect, will not observe the path that makes oneself empty, the result, the qualities of a buddha, the powers, and so forth. They do not observe looking at the master who explains the Dharma and the student who desires the Dharma, because they are indivisible. It is not appropriate to be the station or basis of a bodhisattva who rejoices in accomplishing the qualities, desiring to pacify the suffering of oneself and others.

heading: **འབྲས་བུ་ཡོན་ཏན་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི་འབྱུང་གནས།**
translation: Regarding this from "This is the supreme Dharma treasure" up to "the treasury that generates": Since this training is endowed with inexhaustible qualities, it is endowed with the supreme treasure of Dharma, and since it is the source of the powers and so forth, it is also the holy treasury of Dharma. It is the cause or family of the buddhas, and it is the treasury that generates the bliss and meditative concentrations of migrators.

Like those examples, whatever bodhisattva engages in that way, who is skillful in means and endowed with bright faculties and intelligent intellect, will not observe the path that makes oneself empty, the result, the qualities of a buddha, the powers, and so forth. It is not appropriate to be the station or basis of a bodhisattva who rejoices in accomplishing the qualities, desiring to pacify the suffering of oneself and others.

Furthermore, for example, a mantra-holder also desires to move and abide in the sky without abiding, and furthermore, through the power of accomplishing mantras, they bless a dry tree to possess flowers at a time that is not the season for them to grow, like winter. Like those examples, whatever bodhisattva engages in that way, who is skillful in means and endowed with bright faculties and intelligent intellect, will not observe the path that makes oneself empty, the result, the qualities of a buddha, the powers, and so forth. They do not observe looking at the master who explains the Dharma and the student who desires the Dharma, because they are indivisible. It is not appropriate to be the station or basis of a bodhisattva who rejoices in accomplishing the qualities, desiring to pacify the suffering of oneself and others.

heading: **ཕྱི་རྟེན་འབྲེལ།**
translation: Regarding this from "Trees and fruits" up to "no increase": Also, in the manner of subsequent accordance, like external dependent origination, the bliss of all migrators and all however many generated dharmas there are arise from having practiced the supreme perfection of wisdom. Yet the wisdom from which they arise is never exhausted by becoming less, nor is there any increase by becoming more.

source: ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། སེམས་ཅན་ཐ་མ་འབྲིང་དང་ཞེས་པ་ནས། ཐོབ་པར་འགྱུར་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། ཡང་ན་རྟེན་ཅིང་འབྲེལ་བར་འབྱུང་བ་སེམས་ཅན་ཐ་མ་ངན་འགྲོ་གསུམ། འབྲིང་མི་དང༌། མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པའི་རིགས་ཇི་སྙེད་ཡོད་པ་དེ་དག་ཀུན་ཏུ་རྒྱུ་འབྲས་དང༌། དེ་ཁོ་ན་ཉིད་མི་ཤེས་པའི་རྒྱུ་མ་རིག་པ་ལས་འབྱུང་བར་བདེ་བར་གཤེགས་པས་གསུངས་སོ། །དེ་ལས་དང་ཉོན་མོངས་པའི་རྐྱེན་རྣམས་འཚོགས་ནས་ཁམས་གསུམ་གྱི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་གྱི་འཁྲུལ་འཁོར་རབ་ཏུ་འབྱུང་ལ། རྒྱུ་མ་རིག་པའི་འཁྲུལ་འཁོར་དེ་ནི་ཟད་པའང་མེད་ལ་འཕེལ་བ་ཡང་མེད་དོ། །དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་མཐར་ཕྱིན་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་ཚུལ་ཅེས་པས་བསྒོམ་པའི་ལམ་དང༌། སྒོ་ཅེས་པས་མཐོང་བའི་ལམ་དང༌། ཐབས་ཅེས་པས་སྦྱོར་བའི་ལམ་དང༌། རྩ་བ་ཅེས་པས་ཚོགས་ལམ་སོགས་ཇི་སྙེད་པ་ཀུན་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་མཆོག་འདི་ལས་འབྱུང་ངོ༌། །མ་རིག་པའི་བག་ཆགས་ཀྱི་ས་དང་ཟག་པ་མེད་པའི་ལས་ཀྱི་རྐྱེན་རྣམས་འཚོགས་ནས་བསམ་གྱིས་མི་ཁྱབ་པའི་འཆི་འཕོ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ལས་ཀྱི་འཁྲུལ་འཁོར་རབ་ཏུ་བྱུང་ལ། ཆོས་ཀྱི་དབྱིངས་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་ཟད་པ་མེད་ཅིང་འཕེལ་བའང་མེད་དོ། །བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གང་ལ་ལ་ཞིག་ངོ་བོ་རྟེན་ཅིང་འབྲེལ་བར་འབྱུང་བ་ལ། རང་བཞིན་སྐྱེ་བ་མེད་པ་དང་ཟད་ཅིང་འགག་པ་མེད་པར་ཤེས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་འདི་ཤེས་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་ཉི་མ་སྤྲིན་མེད་པའི་འོད་ཟེར་འཕྲོ་བས། མུན་པའི་ཚོགས་བསལ་བ་ལྟར། ཐོག་མ་མེད་པའི་དུས་ཀྱི་མ་རིག་པ་གཉིས་ཀྱི་འཐིབས་པོ་བཅོམ་ནས་མཐོང་ལམ་དང་བསྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་རང་འབྱུང་གི་ཡེ་ཤེས་ཐོབ་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །དེ་ཡན་ཆད་ཀྱིས་གཙོ་བོ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་རྒྱས་པར་བསྟན་ཏོ། །
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "Sentient beings, lowest, middling, and" up to "will attain": Alternatively, the Sugata has stated that all however many classes there are—dependent origination, the lowest sentient beings of the three lower realms, the middling human beings, and the supreme—arise from the cause, ignorance, which is the non-knowing of cause and effect and suchness everywhere. From that, the conditions of karma and afflictions assemble, and the machine of suffering of the three realms comes forth; and that machine of the cause, ignorance, is neither exhausted nor does it increase. Just like that example, all however many things—the path of meditation indicated by "way of perfected pristine wisdom," the path of seeing indicated by "door," the path of preparation indicated by "method," and the path of accumulation and so forth indicated by "root"—arise from this supreme perfection of wisdom. Having assembled the ground of habitual tendencies of ignorance and the conditions of uncontaminated karma, the machine of karma of inconceivable death and transference and so forth comes forth; yet in the dharmadhātu, the perfection of wisdom, there is no exhaustion and there is no increase. Whichever bodhisattva knows this wisdom that knows the essence of dependent origination to be by nature unarising and without exhaustion and cessation—for example, just as the sun shining with cloudless light rays clears away the masses of darkness, having destroyed the thick darkness of the two ignorances of beginningless time, will attain the naturally arising pristine wisdom of the path of seeing and the path of meditation. Up to here, the main point, the perfection of wisdom, has been taught extensively.

heading: འབྲས་བུ་དམ་པའི་རྟེན་བྱེད་པ།
translation: Regarding this from "Endowed with great power" up to "does not train in order to exhaust": Endowed with the strength of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva endowed with great power dwells for the sake of others even through the four such as being endowed with meditative concentration; and while many rely upon them by apprehending them as signs and tasting them, they do not dwell in them continuously, and even while not doing so, they enter into them. Nevertheless, in these four, along with the six or eighteen branches of the four meditative concentrations, a Mahāyāna bodhisattva becomes the basis for attaining the path of seeing and holy or supreme perfect buddhahood. Having attained the supreme perfection of wisdom endowed with all of these, dwelling in uncontaminated meditative concentration means that even the four holy meditative concentrations of the four formless sense sources are experienced just for a while for the sake of others. For what purpose? These meditative concentrations and absorptions are for the sake of holy awakening; a bodhisattva does not train in order to exhaust their own contaminations like a śrāvaka.

heading: **མ་ཆགས་པའི་ཁྱད་པར།**
translation: Regarding this from "This accumulation of qualities" up to "does not dwell in dharmas": Who is this wondrous bodhisattva, this accumulation of qualities? Dwelling in the meditative concentrations of the four dhyānas and the four formless realms, a bodhisattva does not taste them by way of apprehending signs. Having made aspiration prayers for the desire realm, if those who dwell in them were to have this body perish, even though they are free from desire for the desire realm, they are born again as before in the desire realm in accordance with the intention of their aspiration prayers. Moreover, for example, it is just as if a person like the King of Jambudvīpa, Anantakīrti, who had never gone to the supreme divine city of the divine realm before, later went there, and after having seen and enjoyed those places possessed by the gods there, returned again to this Jambudvīpa with an indifferent mind, they do not generate attachment for the divine realm. Just like that example, a bodhisattva is a practitioner who strives through holding supreme qualities by means of non-apprehending meditative concentration; having formerly dwelt in the four dhyānas and the four meditative concentrations, they dwell again in the desire realm and have no attachment to the taste of the former dhyānas. For example, just as a lotus in the water is unstained by the water, even though born in the desire realm, they do not dwell in the dharmas of childish desires.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "Sentient beings, lowest, middling, and" up to "will attain": Alternatively, the Sugata has stated that all however many classes there are—dependent origination, the lowest sentient beings of the three lower realms, the middling human beings, and the supreme—arise from the cause, ignorance, which is the non-knowing of cause and effect and suchness everywhere. From that, the conditions of karma and afflictions assemble, and the machine of suffering of the three realms comes forth; and that machine of the cause, ignorance, is neither exhausted nor does it increase. Just like that example, all however many things—the path of meditation indicated by "way of perfected pristine wisdom," the path of seeing indicated by "door," the path of preparation indicated by "method," and the path of accumulation and so forth indicated by "root"—arise from this supreme perfection of wisdom. Having assembled the ground of habitual tendencies of ignorance and the conditions of uncontaminated karma, the machine of karma of inconceivable death and transference and so forth comes forth; yet in the dharmadhātu, the perfection of wisdom, there is no exhaustion and there is no increase. Whichever bodhisattva knows this wisdom that knows the essence of dependent origination to be by nature unarising and without exhaustion and cessation—for example, just as the sun shining with cloudless light rays clears away the masses of darkness, having destroyed the thick darkness of the two ignorances of beginningless time, will attain the naturally arising pristine wisdom of the path of seeing and the path of meditation. Up to here, the main point, the perfection of wisdom, has been taught extensively.

Nevertheless, in these four, along with the six or eighteen branches of the four meditative concentrations, a Mahāyāna bodhisattva becomes the basis for attaining the path of seeing and holy or supreme perfect buddhahood. Having attained the supreme perfection of wisdom endowed with all of these, dwelling in uncontaminated meditative concentration means that even the four holy meditative concentrations of the four formless sense sources are experienced just for a while for the sake of others. For what purpose? These meditative concentrations and absorptions are for the sake of holy awakening; a bodhisattva does not train in order to exhaust their own contaminations like a śrāvaka.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "Sentient beings, lowest, middling, and" up to "will attain": Alternatively, the Sugata has stated that all however many classes there are—dependent origination, the lowest sentient beings of the three lower realms, the middling human beings, and the supreme—arise from the cause, ignorance, which is the non-knowing of cause and effect and suchness everywhere. From that, the conditions of karma and afflictions assemble, and the machine of suffering of the three realms comes forth; and that machine of the cause, ignorance, is neither exhausted nor does it increase. Just like that example, all however many things—the path of meditation indicated by "way of perfected pristine wisdom," the path of seeing indicated by "door," the path of preparation indicated by "method," and the path of accumulation and so forth indicated by "root"—arise from this supreme perfection of wisdom. Having assembled the ground of habitual tendencies of ignorance and the conditions of uncontaminated karma, the machine of karma of inconceivable death and transference and so forth comes forth; yet in the dharmadhātu, the perfection of wisdom, there is no exhaustion and there is no increase. Whichever bodhisattva knows this wisdom that knows the essence of dependent origination to be by nature unarising and without exhaustion and cessation—for example, just as the sun shining with cloudless light rays clears away the masses of darkness, having destroyed the thick darkness of the two ignorances of beginningless time, will attain the naturally arising pristine wisdom of the path of seeing and the path of meditation. Up to here, the main point, the perfection of wisdom, has been taught extensively.

Regarding this from "Endowed with great power" up to "does not train in order to exhaust": Endowed with the strength of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva endowed with great power dwells for the sake of others even through the four such as being endowed with meditative concentration; and while many rely upon them by apprehending them as signs and tasting them, they do not dwell in them continuously, and even while not doing so, they enter into them. Nevertheless, in these four, along with the six or eighteen branches of the four meditative concentrations, a Mahāyāna bodhisattva becomes the basis for attaining the path of seeing and holy or supreme perfect buddhahood. Having attained the supreme perfection of wisdom endowed with all of these, dwelling in uncontaminated meditative concentration means that even the four holy meditative concentrations of the four formless sense sources are experienced just for a while for the sake of others. For what purpose? These meditative concentrations and absorptions are for the sake of holy awakening; a bodhisattva does not train in order to exhaust their own contaminations like a śrāvaka.

heading: **རང་གི་བྱ་བ་བསྒྲུབ་པ།**
translation: Regarding this from "Great being" up to "does not seek": That great being acts solely for the purpose of completely ripening sentient beings to be tamed, completely purifying buddha-fields, and perfecting their own accumulation of the six perfections; it is not in order to be attached to the bliss of desires. "Well then, by dwelling in that meditative concentration, are they born in the formless realm?" They are not born there, since they would come to fall away from accomplishing the qualities and perfections of a bodhisattva. Thus, they do not seek out taking birth in the formless realm.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "Sentient beings, lowest, middling, and" up to "will attain": Alternatively, the Sugata has stated that all however many classes there are—dependent origination, the lowest sentient beings of the three lower realms, the middling human beings, and the supreme—arise from the cause, ignorance, which is the non-knowing of cause and effect and suchness everywhere. From that, the conditions of karma and afflictions assemble, and the machine of suffering of the three realms comes forth; and that machine of the cause, ignorance, is neither exhausted nor does it increase. Just like that example, all however many things—the path of meditation indicated by "way of perfected pristine wisdom," the path of seeing indicated by "door," the path of preparation indicated by "method," and the path of accumulation and so forth indicated by "root"—arise from this supreme perfection of wisdom. Having assembled the ground of habitual tendencies of ignorance and the conditions of uncontaminated karma, the machine of karma of inconceivable death and transference and so forth comes forth; yet in the dharmadhātu, the perfection of wisdom, there is no exhaustion and there is no increase. Whichever bodhisattva knows this wisdom that knows the essence of dependent origination to be by nature unarising and without exhaustion and cessation—for example, just as the sun shining with cloudless light rays clears away the masses of darkness, having destroyed the thick darkness of the two ignorances of beginningless time, will attain the naturally arising pristine wisdom of the path of seeing and the path of meditation. Up to here, the main point, the perfection of wisdom, has been taught extensively.

མཐུ་ཆེན་ལྡན་པ་ཞེས་པ་ནས། ཟད་ཕྱིར་སློབ་པ་མིན་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་སྟོབས་དང་ལྡན་ཞིང་མཐུ་ཆེན་པོ་དང་ལྡན་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་བསམ་གཏན་དང་ལྡན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པ་བཞིས་ཀྱང་གཞན་དོན་དུ་གནས་པར་བྱེད་ལ། དེ་དག་ལ་མཚན་མར་འཛིན་ཅིང་རོ་མྱང་བའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་བརྟེན་པར་བྱེད་པ་མང་ཞིང༌། དེ་དག་ལ་རྒྱུན་དུ་གནས་པར་བྱེད་པ་མེད་ལ། མེད་བཞིན་དུ་ཡང་དེ་དག་ལ་འཇུག་པ་ནི། འོན་ཀྱང་བསམ་གཏན་བཞིའི་ཡན་ལག་དྲུག་གམ་བཅོ་བརྒྱད་བཅས་པ་བཞི་པོ་འདིར། ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་མཐོང་ལམ་དང༌། དམ་པའམ་མཆོག་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཐོབ་པའི་རྟེན་དུ་འགྱུར་ལ། དེ་རྣམས་ཐམས་ཅད་ལྡན་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་མཆོག་ཐོབ་ནས། ཟག་མེད་ཀྱི་བསམ་གཏན་གནས་པ་ནི་གཟུགས་མེད་སྐྱེ་མཆེད་མུ་བཞིའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་དམ་པ་བཞི་ཡང༌། གཞན་དོན་དུ་རེ་ཤིག་ཙམ་ཉམས་སུ་མྱོང་བར་བྱེད་དོ། །དགོས་པ་ཅིའི་ཆེད་དུ་ཞེ་ན། བསམ་གཏན་དང་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་འདི་དག་བྱང་ཆུབ་དམ་པའི་ཕྱིར་ཡིན་གྱི། ཉན་ཐོས་ལྟར་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རང་གི་ཟག་པ་ཟད་པར་བྱ་བའི་ཕྱིར་སློབ་པ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །
[2-260] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "Endowed with great power" up to "does not train in order to exhaust": Endowed with the strength of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva endowed with great power dwells for the sake of others even through the four such as being endowed with meditative concentration; and while many rely upon them by apprehending them as signs and tasting them, they do not dwell in them continuously, and even while not doing so, they enter into them. Nevertheless, in these four, along with the six or eighteen branches of the four meditative concentrations, a Mahāyāna bodhisattva becomes the basis for attaining the path of seeing and holy or supreme perfect buddhahood. Having attained the supreme perfection of wisdom endowed with all of these, dwelling in uncontaminated meditative concentration means that even the four holy meditative concentrations of the four formless sense sources are experienced just for a while for the sake of others. For what purpose? These meditative concentrations and absorptions are for the sake of holy awakening; a bodhisattva does not train in order to exhaust their own contaminations like a śrāvaka.

heading: **སེམས་ཅན་ལ་བདེ་བ་སྦྱིན་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "For example, a person" up to "enters the desire realm": Just like the example of a person who finds a treasure of jewels, a bodhisattva who is endowed with training and is wise, who rejoices in acting for the benefit of others and who gives bliss to others, having attained the four peace of the four dhyānas and the four meditative concentrations, without being attached even to that, being endowed with the bliss of the dhyānas, relinquishes the attained meditative concentrations of the dhyānas, and being endowed with compassion for migrating beings, wishes to enter again into the desire realm.

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "Sentient beings, lowest, middling, and" up to "will attain": Alternatively, the Sugata has stated that all however many classes there are—dependent origination, the lowest sentient beings of the three lower realms, the middling human beings, and the supreme—arise from the cause, ignorance, which is the non-knowing of cause and effect and suchness everywhere. From that, the conditions of karma and afflictions assemble, and the machine of suffering of the three realms comes forth; and that machine of the cause, ignorance, is neither exhausted nor does it increase. Just like that example, all however many things—the path of meditation indicated by "way of perfected pristine wisdom," the path of seeing indicated by "door," the path of preparation indicated by "method," and the path of accumulation and so forth indicated by "root"—arise from this supreme perfection of wisdom. Having assembled the ground of habitual tendencies of ignorance and the conditions of uncontaminated karma, the machine of karma of inconceivable death and transference and so forth comes forth; yet in the dharmadhātu, the perfection of wisdom, there is no exhaustion and there is no increase. Whichever bodhisattva knows this wisdom that knows the essence of dependent origination to be by nature unarising and without exhaustion and cessation—for example, just as the sun shining with cloudless light rays clears away the masses of darkness, having destroyed the thick darkness of the two ignorances of beginningless time, will attain the naturally arising pristine wisdom of the path of seeing and the path of meditation. Up to here, the main point, the perfection of wisdom, has been taught extensively.

heading: བསམ་པའི་དབང་གི་མཆོག་དམན་དུ་དབྱེ་བ།
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "If a bodhisattva" up to "should be known as": If a bodhisattva has attained and dwells in the aforementioned meditative concentrations and dhyānas, yet the thought arises desiring to attain the purpose of the vehicle of arhats and pratyekabuddhas, then even though they are resting evenly, they are agitated, and even while the mind dwells in dhyāna, they become distracted by flowing out to the discordant factors of the Mahāyāna and so on, because they completely fall away from attaining the qualities of a buddha, such as the powers, for example, just like a ship destroyed upon the perilous ocean. On the other hand, even if a bodhisattva engages in and strives toward form, sound, and likewise smell, taste, touch, and the five qualities of desire without attachment, yet they are free from the discordant factors of the vehicle of arhats and pratyekabuddhas, and their mind rejoices in attaining holy perfect awakening, then since their mind does not waver from what is to be attained, the heroic bodhisattva should be known as constantly resting evenly. Up to here the context of the peak has been taught. From then on, regarding conduct, since the subsequent attainment mainly becomes gradual and momentary, the nature of the gradual application of the sixth context is meditating without apprehending the meaning of the dharmakāya—the three of the basis, path, and result—which is experiencing the gradual conduct of awakening. Moreover, since this is a virtuous practice of action without attachment to the appearances of the subsequent attainment, in this text it is taught from joyous effort down to generosity. Jñānapāda asserts that it is taught through the six temporary benefits. There are thirteen divisions of this, which are complete in meaning without being rigidly arranged in this text.

Dwelling in the meditative concentrations of the four dhyānas and the four formless realms, a bodhisattva does not taste them by way of apprehending signs. Having made aspiration prayers for the desire realm, if those who dwell in them were to have this body perish, even though they are free from desire for the desire realm, they are born again as before in the desire realm in accordance with the intention of their aspiration prayers. Moreover, for example, it is just as if a person like the King of Jambudvīpa, Anantakīrti, who had never gone to the supreme divine city of the divine realm before, later went there, and after having seen and enjoyed those places possessed by the gods there, returned again to this Jambudvīpa with an indifferent mind, they do not generate attachment for the divine realm. Just like that example, a bodhisattva is a practitioner who strives through holding supreme qualities by means of non-apprehending meditative concentration; having formerly dwelt in the four dhyānas and the four meditative concentrations, they dwell again in the desire realm and have no attachment to the taste of the former dhyānas. For example, just as a lotus in the water is unstained by the water, even though born in the desire realm, they do not dwell in the dharmas of childish desires.

Regarding this from "Endowed with great power" up to "does not train in order to exhaust": Endowed with the strength of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva endowed with great power dwells for the sake of others even through the four such as being endowed with meditative concentration; and while many rely upon them by apprehending them as signs and tasting them, they do not dwell in them continuously, and even while not doing so, they enter into them. Nevertheless, in these four, along with the six or eighteen branches of the four meditative concentrations, a Mahāyāna bodhisattva becomes the basis for attaining the path of seeing and holy or supreme perfect buddhahood. Having attained the supreme perfection of wisdom endowed with all of these, dwelling in uncontaminated meditative concentration means that even the four holy meditative concentrations of the four formless sense sources are experienced just for a while for the sake of others. For what purpose? These meditative concentrations and absorptions are for the sake of holy awakening; a bodhisattva does not train in order to exhaust their own contaminations like a śrāvaka.

Regarding this from "This accumulation of qualities" up to "does not dwell in dharmas": Who is this wondrous bodhisattva, this accumulation of qualities? Dwelling in the meditative concentrations of the four dhyānas and the four formless realms, a bodhisattva does not taste them by way of apprehending signs. Having made aspiration prayers for the desire realm, if those who dwell in them were to have this body perish, even though they are free from desire for the desire realm, they are born again as before in the desire realm in accordance with the intention of their aspiration prayers. Moreover, for example, it is just as if a person like the King of Jambudvīpa, Anantakīrti, who had never gone to the supreme divine city of the divine realm before, later went there, and after having seen and enjoyed those places possessed by the gods there, returned again to this Jambudvīpa with an indifferent mind, they do not generate attachment for the divine realm. Just like that example, a bodhisattva is a practitioner who strives through holding supreme qualities by means of non-apprehending meditative concentration; having formerly dwelt in the four dhyānas and the four meditative concentrations, they dwell again in the desire realm and have no attachment to the taste of the former dhyānas. For example, just as a lotus in the water is unstained by the water, even though born in the desire realm, they do not dwell in the dharmas of childish desires.

Regarding this from "Great being" up to "does not seek": That great being acts solely for the purpose of completely ripening sentient beings to be tamed, completely purifying buddha-fields, and perfecting their own accumulation of the six perfections; it is not in order to be attached to the bliss of desires. "Well then, by dwelling in that meditative concentration, are they born in the formless realm?" They are not born there, since they would come to fall away from accomplishing the qualities and perfections of a bodhisattva. Thus, they do not seek out taking birth in the formless realm.

heading: **གུས་པས་འགྲོ་བ།**
translation: Regarding this from "Sentient beings and persons" up to "burns them up": The completely pure example of the joyous effort of the rituals of other sentient beings and persons is experiencing non-apprehension while manifesting joyous effort toward the perfection of joyous effort conventionally. Just like the example of a servant girl, bodhisattvas who have entered into the supreme intention for the sake of great awakening, which is to be attained, should also dwell in intention and application as if becoming a servant to all migrating sentient beings. By doing so, through this they will attain awakening and the temporary qualities will be perfected. Otherwise, if they act with arrogance and hatred, their own continuum will be burned; for example, just as fire arises from grass and wood and burns up that very grass and wood.

Regarding this from "Endowed with great power" up to "does not train in order to exhaust": Endowed with the strength of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva endowed with great power dwells for the sake of others even through the four such as being endowed with meditative concentration; and while many rely upon them by apprehending them as signs and tasting them, they do not dwell in them continuously, and even while not doing so, they enter into them. Nevertheless, in these four, along with the six or eighteen branches of the four meditative concentrations, a Mahāyāna bodhisattva becomes the basis for attaining the path of seeing and holy or supreme perfect buddhahood. Having attained the supreme perfection of wisdom endowed with all of these, dwelling in uncontaminated meditative concentration means that even the four holy meditative concentrations of the four formless sense sources are experienced just for a while for the sake of others. For what purpose? These meditative concentrations and absorptions are for the sake of holy awakening; a bodhisattva does not train in order to exhaust their own contaminations like a śrāvaka.

Regarding this from "This accumulation of qualities" up to "does not dwell in dharmas": Who is this wondrous bodhisattva, this accumulation of qualities? Dwelling in the meditative concentrations of the four dhyānas and the four formless realms, a bodhisattva does not taste them by way of apprehending signs. Having made aspiration prayers for the desire realm, if those who dwell in them were to have this body perish, even though they are free from desire for the desire realm, they are born again as before in the desire realm in accordance with the intention of their aspiration prayers. Moreover, for example, it is just as if a person like the King of Jambudvīpa, Anantakīrti, who had never gone to the supreme divine city of the divine realm before, later went there, and after having seen and enjoyed those places possessed by the gods there, returned again to this Jambudvīpa with an indifferent mind, they do not generate attachment for the divine realm. Just like that example, a bodhisattva is a practitioner who strives through holding supreme qualities by means of non-apprehending meditative concentration; having formerly dwelt in the four dhyānas and the four meditative concentrations, they dwell again in the desire realm and have no attachment to the taste of the former dhyānas. For example, just as a lotus in the water is unstained by the water, even though born in the desire realm, they do not dwell in the dharmas of childish desires.

Regarding this from "Great being" up to "does not seek": That great being acts solely for the purpose of completely ripening sentient beings to be tamed, completely purifying buddha-fields, and perfecting their own accumulation of the six perfections; it is not in order to be attached to the bliss of desires. "Well then, by dwelling in that meditative concentration, are they born in the formless realm?" They are not born there, since they would come to fall away from accomplishing the qualities and perfections of a bodhisattva. Thus, they do not seek out taking birth in the formless realm.

Regarding this from "Endowed with great power" up to "does not train in order to exhaust": Endowed with the strength of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva endowed with great power dwells for the sake of others even through the four such as being endowed with meditative concentration; and while many rely upon them by apprehending them as signs and tasting them, they do not dwell in them continuously, and even while not doing so, they enter into them. Nevertheless, in these four, along with the six or eighteen branches of the four meditative concentrations, a Mahāyāna bodhisattva becomes the basis for attaining the path of seeing and holy or supreme perfect buddhahood. Having attained the supreme perfection of wisdom endowed with all of these, dwelling in uncontaminated meditative concentration means that even the four holy meditative concentrations of the four formless sense sources are experienced just for a while for the sake of others. For what purpose? These meditative concentrations and absorptions are for the sake of holy awakening; a bodhisattva does not train in order to exhaust their own contaminations like a śrāvaka.

ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ།
[2-261] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said:

[2-262] source:
འདི་ནི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཚོགས་ཞེས་པ་ནས། ཆོས་མི་གནས་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། འདི་ནི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཚོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རྨད་བྱུང་འདི་གང་ཞེ་ན། བསམ་གཏན་བཞི་དང་གཟུགས་མེད་བཞིའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ལ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གནས་ནས་མཚན་མར་འཛིན་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་རོ་མྱང་བ་མེད་ལ། དེ་ལ་གནས་པ་རྣམས་འདོད་ཁམས་སུ་སྨོན་ལམ་བཏབ་ནས་གལ་ཏེ་ལུས་འདི་ཞིག་པར་འགྱུར་ན། འདོད་པའི་འདོད་ཆགས་དང་བྲལ་ཡང་སྨོན་ལམ་གྱི་བསམ་པ་ཇི་ལྟ་བ་བཞིན་དུ་འདོད་པའི་ཁམས་སུ་སྔར་བཞིན་དུ་ཡང་སྐྱེའོ། །དེ་ཡང་དཔེར་ན་འཛམ་གླིང་རྒྱལ་པོ་གྲགས་པ་མཐའ་ཡས་ལྟ་བུའི་མི་ཞིག་གིས་སྔོན་ཆད་ལྷའི་ཡུལ་གྱི་ལྷའི་གྲོང་ཁྱེར་མཆོག་ཏུ་སྔར་མ་ཕྱིན་པར་ཕྱིས་སོང་སྟེ། དེ་ན་ལྷ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ཡོངས་སུ་བཟུང་པའི་ཡུལ་དེ་རྣམས་མཐོང་ཞིང་ལོངས་སྤྱད་ནས། ངན་སེམས་ཀྱིས་ཕྱིར་འཛམ་བུའི་གླིང་འདིར་འོང་བར་གྱུར་ན་ལྷ་ཡུལ་ལ་འཆགས་པར་མི་བྱེད་པ་ལྟར། དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་མི་དམིགས་པའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་གྱིས་ཡོན་ཏན་མཆོག་འཆང་བ་ལས་རྣལ་འབྱོར་པ་བརྩོན་པ་སྟེ། སྔར་བསམ་གཏན་བཞི་དང་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་བཞི་ལ་གནས་ཏེ། ཕྱིར་ཡང་འདོད་པའི་ཁམས་སུ་གནས་ཏེ་སྔར་གྱི་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་རོ་ལ་ཆགས་པ་མེད་དེ། དཔེར་ན་ཆུའི་པད་མ་ཆུས་མ་གོས་པ་བཞིན་དུ། འདོད་ཁམས་སུ་སྐྱེས་ཀྱང་བྱིས་པ་འདོད་པའི་ཆོས་ལ་མི་གནས་སོ། །
[2-262] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "This accumulation of qualities" up to "does not dwell in dharmas": Who is this wondrous bodhisattva, this accumulation of qualities? Dwelling in the meditative concentrations of the four dhyānas and the four formless realms, a bodhisattva does not taste them by way of apprehending signs. Having made aspiration prayers for the desire realm, if those who dwell in them were to have this body perish, even though they are free from desire for the desire realm, they are born again as before in the desire realm in accordance with the intention of their aspiration prayers. Moreover, for example, it is just as if a person like the King of Jambudvīpa, Anantakīrti, who had never gone to the supreme divine city of the divine realm before, later went there, and after having seen and enjoyed those places possessed by the gods there, returned again to this Jambudvīpa with an indifferent mind, they do not generate attachment for the divine realm. Just like that example, a bodhisattva is a practitioner who strives through holding supreme qualities by means of non-apprehending meditative concentration; having formerly dwelt in the four dhyānas and the four meditative concentrations, they dwell again in the desire realm and have no attachment to the taste of the former dhyānas. For example, just as a lotus in the water is unstained by the water, even though born in the desire realm, they do not dwell in the dharmas of childish desires.

[2-263] source:

[2-263] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said:

[2-264] source:
བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ་ཞེས་པ་ནས། གཉེར་མི་བྱེད་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ་དེ་གདུལ་བྱ་སེམས་ཅན་ཡོངས་སུ་སྨིན་པར་བྱ་བ་དང༌། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཞིང་ཡོངས་སུ་སྦྱོང་བ་དང༌། རང་གི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དྲུག་གི་ཚོགས་རྫོགས་པའི་དོན་བྱེད་པ་ཁོ་ནར་ཟད་ཀྱིས་འདོད་པའི་བདེ་བ་ཆགས་པའི་ཕྱིར་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །འོ་ན་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་དེ་ལ་གནས་པས་གཟུགས་མེད་དུ་ཅང་སྐྱེ་འམ། ཞེ་ན་མི་སྐྱེ་སྟེ། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་བསྒྲུབ་པ་ལས་ཉམས་པར་འགྱུར་དུ་འོང་ངོ༌། །ཞེས་གཟུགས་མེད་ཀྱི་ཁམས་སུ་སྐྱེ་བ་ལེན་པ་དོན་དུ་གཉེར་བར་མི་བྱེད་དོ། །
[2-264] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "Great being" up to "does not seek": That great being acts solely for the purpose of completely ripening sentient beings to be tamed, completely purifying buddha-fields, and perfecting their own accumulation of the six perfections; it is not in order to be attached to the bliss of desires. "Well then, by dwelling in that meditative concentration, are they born in the formless realm?" They are not born there, since they would come to fall away from accomplishing the qualities and perfections of a bodhisattva. Thus, they do not seek out taking birth in the formless realm.

[2-265] source:
ཅེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་མི་ཞིག་ཞེས་པ་ནས། འདོད་ཁམས་འཇུག་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། རིན་པོ་ཆེའི་གཏེར་རྙེད་པའི་མིའི་དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སྦྱངས་པ་དང་ལྡན་པ་མཁས་པ་གཞན་གྱི་དོན་བྱེད་པ་ལས་དགའ་བ་དང༌། གཞན་ལ་བདེ་བ་སྦྱིན་པ་ཡང་བསམ་གཏན་བཞི་དང་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་བཞིའི་ཞི་བ་བཞི་ཐོབ་ནས། དེ་ལ་ཡང་མ་ཆགས་པར་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་བདེ་བ་དང་ལྡན་པས་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ཐོབ་པའི་ཕྱིར་བཏང་སྟེ། འགྲོ་བ་རྣམས་ལ་སྙིང་བརྩེ་བ་དང་ལྡན་པས་ཕྱིར་ཡང་འདོད་པའི་ཁམས་སུ་འཇུག་པར་འདོད་དོ། །
[2-265] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding this from "For example, a person" up to "enters the desire realm": Just like the example of a person who finds a treasure of jewels, a bodhisattva who is endowed with training and is wise, who rejoices in acting for the benefit of others and who gives bliss to others, having attained the four peace of the four dhyānas and the four meditative concentrations, without being attached even to that, being endowed with the bliss of the dhyānas, relinquishes the attained meditative concentrations of the dhyānas, and being endowed with compassion for migrating beings, wishes to enter again into the desire realm.

heading: **གཞན་གྱི་དོན་ལ་མི་སྐྱོ་བ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "To an only child" up to "should dwell": In that manner, just as a mother affectionately serves an only child, one should dwell in acting for the purpose of others with a resolute intention and a mind completely free from weariness. Through this, the context of the dharmakāya has been taught.

[2-260] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "Endowed with great power" up to "does not train in order to exhaust": Endowed with the strength of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva endowed with great power dwells for the sake of others even through the four such as being endowed with meditative concentration; and while many rely upon them by apprehending them as signs and tasting them, they do not dwell in them continuously, and even while not doing so, they enter into them. Nevertheless, in these four, along with the six or eighteen branches of the four meditative concentrations, a Mahāyāna bodhisattva becomes the basis for attaining the path of seeing and holy or supreme perfect buddhahood. Having attained the supreme perfection of wisdom endowed with all of these, dwelling in uncontaminated meditative concentration means that even the four holy meditative concentrations of the four formless sense sources are experienced just for a while for the sake of others. For what purpose? These meditative concentrations and absorptions are for the sake of holy awakening; a bodhisattva does not train in order to exhaust their own contaminations like a śrāvaka.

[2-262] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "This accumulation of qualities" up to "does not dwell in dharmas": Who is this wondrous bodhisattva, this accumulation of qualities? Dwelling in the meditative concentrations of the four dhyānas and the four formless realms, a bodhisattva does not taste them by way of apprehending signs. Having made aspiration prayers for the desire realm, if those who dwell in them were to have this body perish, even though they are free from desire for the desire realm, they are born again as before in the desire realm in accordance with the intention of their aspiration prayers. Moreover, for example, it is just as if a person like the King of Jambudvīpa, Anantakīrti, who had never gone to the supreme divine city of the divine realm before, later went there, and after having seen and enjoyed those places possessed by the gods there, returned again to this Jambudvīpa with an indifferent mind, they do not generate attachment for the divine realm. Just like that example, a bodhisattva is a practitioner who strives through holding supreme qualities by means of non-apprehending meditative concentration; having formerly dwelt in the four dhyānas and the four meditative concentrations, they dwell again in the desire realm and have no attachment to the taste of the former dhyānas. For example, just as a lotus in the water is unstained by the water, even though born in the desire realm, they do not dwell in the dharmas of childish desires.

བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ་ཞེས་པ་ནས། གཉེར་མི་བྱེད་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ་དེ་གདུལ་བྱ་སེམས་ཅན་ཡོངས་སུ་སྨིན་པར་བྱ་བ་དང༌། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཞིང་ཡོངས་སུ་སྦྱོང་བ་དང༌། རང་གི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དྲུག་གི་ཚོགས་རྫོགས་པའི་དོན་བྱེད་པ་ཁོ་ནར་ཟད་ཀྱིས་འདོད་པའི་བདེ་བ་ཆགས་པའི་ཕྱིར་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །འོ་ན་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་དེ་ལ་གནས་པས་གཟུགས་མེད་དུ་ཅང་སྐྱེ་འམ། ཞེ་ན་མི་སྐྱེ་སྟེ། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་བསྒྲུབ་པ་ལས་ཉམས་པར་འགྱུར་དུ་འོང་ངོ༌། །ཞེས་གཟུགས་མེད་ཀྱི་ཁམས་སུ་སྐྱེ་བ་ལེན་པ་དོན་དུ་གཉེར་བར་མི་བྱེད་དོ། །
[2-264] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "Great being" up to "does not seek": That great being acts solely for the purpose of completely ripening sentient beings to be tamed, completely purifying buddha-fields, and perfecting their own accumulation of the six perfections; it is not in order to be attached to the bliss of desires. "Well then, by dwelling in that meditative concentration, are they born in the formless realm?" They are not born there, since they would come to fall away from accomplishing the qualities and perfections of a bodhisattva. Thus, they do not seek out taking birth in the formless realm.

[2-265] source:
ཅེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་མི་ཞིག་ཞེས་པ་ནས། འདོད་ཁམས་འཇུག་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། རིན་པོ་ཆེའི་གཏེར་རྙེད་པའི་མིའི་དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སྦྱངས་པ་དང་ལྡན་པ་མཁས་པ་གཞན་གྱི་དོན་བྱེད་པ་ལས་དགའ་བ་དང༌། གཞན་ལ་བདེ་བ་སྦྱིན་པ་ཡང་བསམ་གཏན་བཞི་དང་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་བཞིའི་ཞི་བ་བཞི་ཐོབ་ནས། དེ་ལ་ཡང་མ་ཆགས་པར་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་བདེ་བ་དང་ལྡན་པས་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ཐོབ་པའི་ཕྱིར་བཏང་སྟེ། འགྲོ་བ་རྣམས་ལ་སྙིང་བརྩེ་བ་དང་ལྡན་པས་ཕྱིར་ཡང་འདོད་པའི་ཁམས་སུ་འཇུག་པར་འདོད་དོ། །

Thus it is said: Regarding this from "For example, a person" up to "enters the desire realm": Just like the example of a person who finds a treasure of jewels, a bodhisattva who is endowed with training and is wise, who rejoices in acting for the benefit of others and who gives bliss to others, having attained the four peace of the four dhyānas and the four meditative concentrations, without being attached even to that, being endowed with the bliss of the dhyānas, relinquishes the attained meditative concentrations of the dhyānas, and being endowed with compassion for migrating beings, wishes to enter again into the desire realm.

Work: འཕགས་པ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་སྡུད་པ་ཚིགས་སུ་བཅད་པའི་ཊཱི་ཀ་ཡིད་བཞིན་གྱི་ནོར་བུ་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་ལྟ་བུ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་རྒྱ་མཚོའི་སྡེ། (Commentaries on the Short Prajnaparamita Sutras:The Ocean of Perfection.), author: null. [2-260] source:
མཐུ་ཆེན་ལྡན་པ་ཞེས་པ་ནས། ཟད་ཕྱིར་སློབ་པ་མིན་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་སྟོབས་དང་ལྡན་ཞིང་མཐུ་ཆེན་པོ་དང་ལྡན་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་བསམ་གཏན་དང་ལྡན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པ་བཞིས་ཀྱང་གཞན་དོན་དུ་གནས་པར་བྱེད་ལ། དེ་དག་ལ་མཚན་མར་འཛིན་ཅིང་རོ་མྱང་བའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་བརྟེན་པར་བྱེད་པ་མང་ཞིང༌། དེ་དག་ལ་རྒྱུན་དུ་གནས་པར་བྱེད་པ་མེད་ལ། མེད་བཞིན་དུ་ཡང་དེ་དག་ལ་འཇུག་པ་ནི། འོན་ཀྱང་བསམ་གཏན་བཞིའི་ཡན་ལག་དྲུག་གམ་བཅོ་བརྒྱད་བཅས་པ་བཞི་པོ་འདིར། ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་མཐོང་ལམ་དང༌། དམ་པའམ་མཆོག་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཐོབ་པའི་རྟེན་དུ་འགྱུར་ལ། དེ་རྣམས་ཐམས་ཅད་ལྡན་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་མཆོག་ཐོབ་ནས། ཟག་མེད་ཀྱི་བསམ་གཏན་གནས་པ་ནི་གཟུགས་མེད་སྐྱེ་མཆེད་མུ་བཞིའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་དམ་པ་བཞི་ཡང༌། གཞན་དོན་དུ་རེ་ཤིག་ཙམ་ཉམས་སུ་མྱོང་བར་བྱེད་དོ། །དགོས་པ་ཅིའི་ཆེད་དུ་ཞེ་ན། བསམ་གཏན་དང་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་འདི་དག་བྱང་ཆུབ་དམ་པའི་ཕྱིར་ཡིན་གྱི། ཉན་ཐོས་ལྟར་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རང་གི་ཟག་པ་ཟད་པར་བྱ་བའི་ཕྱིར་སློབ་པ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །
[2-260] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "Endowed with great power" up to "does not train in order to exhaust": Endowed with the strength of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva endowed with great power dwells for the sake of others even through the four such as being endowed with meditative concentration; and while many rely upon them by apprehending them as signs and tasting them, they do not dwell in them continuously, and even while not doing so, they enter into them. Nevertheless, in these four, along with the six or eighteen branches of the four meditative concentrations, a Mahāyāna bodhisattva becomes the basis for attaining the path of seeing and holy or supreme perfect buddhahood. Having attained the supreme perfection of wisdom endowed with all of these, dwelling in uncontaminated meditative concentration means that even the four holy meditative concentrations of the four formless sense sources are experienced just for a while for the sake of others. For what purpose? These meditative concentrations and absorptions are for the sake of holy awakening; a bodhisattva does not train in order to exhaust their own contaminations like a śrāvaka.

[2-261] source:
ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ།
[2-261] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said:

[2-262] source:
འདི་ནི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཚོགས་ཞེས་པ་ནས། ཆོས་མི་གནས་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། འདི་ནི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཚོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རྨད་བྱུང་འདི་གང་ཞེ་ན། བསམ་གཏན་བཞི་དང་གཟུགས་མེད་བཞིའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ལ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གནས་ནས་མཚན་མར་འཛིན་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་རོ་མྱང་བ་མེད་ལ། དེ་ལ་གནས་པ་རྣམས་འདོད་ཁམས་སུ་སྨོན་ལམ་བཏབ་ནས་གལ་ཏེ་ལུས་འདི་ཞིག་པར་འགྱུར་ན། འདོད་པའི་འདོད་ཆགས་དང་བྲལ་ཡང་སྨོན་ལམ་གྱི་བསམ་པ་ཇི་ལྟ་བ་བཞིན་དུ་འདོད་པའི་ཁམས་སུ་སྔར་བཞིན་དུ་ཡང་སྐྱེའོ། །དེ་ཡང་དཔེར་ན་འཛམ་གླིང་རྒྱལ་པོ་གྲགས་པ་མཐའ་ཡས་ལྟ་བུའི་མི་ཞིག་གིས་སྔོན་ཆད་ལྷའི་ཡུལ་གྱི་ལྷའི་གྲོང་ཁྱེར་མཆོག་ཏུ་སྔར་མ་ཕྱིན་པར་ཕྱིས་སོང་སྟེ། དེ་ན་ལྷ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ཡོངས་སུ་བཟུང་པའི་ཡུལ་དེ་རྣམས་མཐོང་ཞིང་ལོངས་སྤྱད་ནས། ངན་སེམས་ཀྱིས་ཕྱིར་འཛམ་བུའི་གླིང་འདིར་འོང་བར་གྱུར་ན་ལྷ་ཡུལ་ལ་འཆགས་པར་མི་བྱེད་པ་ལྟར། དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་མི་དམིགས་པའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་གྱིས་ཡོན་ཏན་མཆོག་འཆང་བ་ལས་རྣལ་འབྱོར་པ་བརྩོན་པ་སྟེ། སྔར་བསམ་གཏན་བཞི་དང་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་བཞི་ལ་གནས་ཏེ། ཕྱིར་ཡང་འདོད་པའི་ཁམས་སུ་གནས་ཏེ་སྔར་གྱི་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་རོ་ལ་ཆགས་པ་མེད་དེ། དཔེར་ན་ཆུའི་པད་མ་ཆུས་མ་གོས་པ་བཞིན་དུ། འདོད་ཁམས་སུ་སྐྱེས་ཀྱང་བྱིས་པ་འདོད་པའི་ཆོས་ལ་མི་གནས་སོ། །
[2-262] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "This accumulation of qualities" up to "does not dwell in dharmas": Who is this wondrous bodhisattva, this accumulation of qualities? Dwelling in the meditative concentrations of the four dhyānas and the four formless realms, a bodhisattva does not taste them by way of apprehending signs. Having made aspiration prayers for the desire realm, if those who dwell in them were to have this body perish, even though they are free from desire for the desire realm, they are born again as before in the desire realm in accordance with the intention of their aspiration prayers. Moreover, for example, it is just as if a person like the King of Jambudvīpa, Anantakīrti, who had never gone to the supreme divine city of the divine realm before, later went there, and after having seen and enjoyed those places possessed by the gods there, returned again to this Jambudvīpa with an indifferent mind, they do not generate attachment for the divine realm. Just like that example, a bodhisattva is a practitioner who strives through holding supreme qualities by means of non-apprehending meditative concentration; having formerly dwelt in the four dhyānas and the four meditative concentrations, they dwell again in the desire realm and have no attachment to the taste of the former dhyānas. For example, just as a lotus in the water is unstained by the water, even though born in the desire realm, they do not dwell in the dharmas of childish desires.

[2-263] source:
ཅེས་གསུངས་ཏེ།
[2-263] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said:

[2-264] source:
བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ་ཞེས་པ་ནས། གཉེར་མི་བྱེད་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ་དེ་གདུལ་བྱ་སེམས་ཅན་ཡོངས་སུ་སྨིན་པར་བྱ་བ་དང༌། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཞིང་ཡོངས་སུ་སྦྱོང་བ་དང༌། རང་གི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དྲུག་གི་ཚོགས་རྫོགས་པའི་དོན་བྱེད་པ་ཁོ་ནར་ཟད་ཀྱིས་འདོད་པའི་བདེ་བ་ཆགས་པའི་ཕྱིར་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །འོ་ན་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་དེ་ལ་གནས་པས་གཟུགས་མེད་དུ་ཅང་སྐྱེ་འམ། ཞེ་ན་མི་སྐྱེ་སྟེ། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་བསྒྲུབ་པ་ལས་ཉམས་པར་འགྱུར་དུ་འོང་ངོ༌། །ཞེས་གཟུགས་མེད་ཀྱི་ཁམས་སུ་སྐྱེ་བ་ལེན་པ་དོན་དུ་གཉེར་བར་མི་བྱེད་དོ། །
[2-264] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "Great being" up to "does not seek": That great being acts solely for the purpose of completely ripening sentient beings to be tamed, completely purifying buddha-fields, and perfecting their own accumulation of the six perfections; it is not in order to be attached to the bliss of desires. "Well then, by dwelling in that meditative concentration, are they born in the formless realm?" They are not born there, since they would come to fall away from accomplishing the qualities and perfections of a bodhisattva. Thus, they do not seek out taking birth in the formless realm.

[2-265] source:
ཅེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་མི་ཞིག་ཞེས་པ་ནས། འདོད་ཁམས་འཇུག་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། རིན་པོ་ཆེའི་གཏེར་རྙེད་པའི་མིའི་དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སྦྱངས་པ་དང་ལྡན་པ་མཁས་པ་གཞན་གྱི་དོན་བྱེད་པ་ལས་དགའ་བ་དང༌། གཞན་ལ་བདེ་བ་སྦྱིན་པ་ཡང་བསམ་གཏན་བཞི་དང་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་བཞིའི་ཞི་བ་བཞི་ཐོབ་ནས། དེ་ལ་ཡང་མ་ཆགས་པར་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་བདེ་བ་དང་ལྡན་པས་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ཐོབ་པའི་ཕྱིར་བཏང་སྟེ། འགྲོ་བ་རྣམས་ལ་སྙིང་བརྩེ་བ་དང་ལྡན་པས་ཕྱིར་ཡང་འདོད་པའི་ཁམས་སུ་འཇུག་པར་འདོད་དོ། །
[2-265] translation already produced for this document:
Thus it is said: Regarding this from "For example, a person" up to "enters the desire realm": Just like the example of a person who finds a treasure of jewels, a bodhisattva who is endowed with training and is wise, who rejoices in acting for the benefit of others and who gives bliss to others, having attained the four peace of the four dhyānas and the four meditative concentrations, without being attached even to that, being endowed with the bliss of the dhyānas, relinquishes the attained meditative concentrations of the dhyānas, and being endowed with compassion for migrating beings, wishes to enter again into the desire realm.

heading: **སྤྱིར་བསྟན་པ།**
translation: Regarding this from "A bodhisattva" up to "without slacking": Whichever bodhisattva wishes to dwell in saṃsāra for a long time still, and is a practitioner who strives in the activities there of acting for the purpose of sentient beings, preparing a buddha-field, and perfecting their own accumulations, if they do not generate even a subtle atom of a mind of weariness toward the difficult application and long duration of time, then they are endowed with the perfection of joyous effort and are without slacking from the intention and application of the Mahāyāna.
style_instruction: Translate this passage of a Tibetan Buddhist commentary on the Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom (Ratnaguṇasañcayagāthā) into clear, accurate English prose. [2-260] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "Endowed with great power" up to "does not train in order to exhaust": Endowed with the strength of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva endowed with great power dwells for the sake of others even through the four such as being endowed with meditative concentration; and while many rely upon them by apprehending them as signs and tasting them, they do not dwell in them continuously, and even while not doing so, they enter into them. Nevertheless, in these four, along with the six or eighteen branches of the four meditative concentrations, a Mahāyāna bodhisattva becomes the basis for attaining the path of seeing and holy or supreme perfect buddhahood. Having attained the supreme perfection of wisdom endowed with all of these, dwelling in uncontaminated meditative concentration means that even the four holy meditative concentrations of the four formless sense sources are experienced just for a while for the sake of others. For what purpose? These meditative concentrations and absorptions are for the sake of holy awakening; a bodhisattva does not train in order to exhaust their own contaminations like a śrāvaka.

[2-262] source:
འདི་ནི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཚོགས་ཞེས་པ་ནས། ཆོས་མི་གནས་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། འདི་ནི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཚོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རྨད་བྱུང་འདི་གང་ཞེ་ན། བསམ་གཏན་བཞི་དང་གཟུགས་མེད་བཞིའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ལ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གནས་ནས་མཚན་མར་འཛིན་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་རོ་མྱང་བ་མེད་ལ། དེ་ལ་གནས་པ་རྣམས་འདོད་ཁམས་སུ་སྨོན་ལམ་བཏབ་ནས་གལ་ཏེ་ལུས་འདི་ཞིག་པར་འགྱུར་ན། འདོད་པའི་འདོད་ཆགས་དང་བྲལ་ཡང་སྨོན་ལམ་གྱི་བསམ་པ་ཇི་ལྟ་བ་བཞིན་དུ་འདོད་པའི་ཁམས་སུ་སྔར་བཞིན་དུ་ཡང་སྐྱེའོ། །དེ་ཡང་དཔེར་ན་འཛམ་གླིང་རྒྱལ་པོ་གྲགས་པ་མཐའ་ཡས་ལྟ་བུའི་མི་ཞིག་གིས་སྔོན་ཆད་ལྷའི་ཡུལ་གྱི་ལྷའི་གྲོང་ཁྱེར་མཆོག་ཏུ་སྔར་མ་ཕྱིན་པར་ཕྱིས་སོང་སྟེ། དེ་ན་ལྷ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ཡོངས་སུ་བཟུང་པའི་ཡུལ་དེ་རྣམས་མཐོང་ཞིང་ལོངས་སྤྱད་ནས། ངན་སེམས་ཀྱིས་ཕྱིར་འཛམ་བུའི་གླིང་འདིར་འོང་བར་གྱུར་ན་ལྷ་ཡུལ་ལ་འཆགས་པར་མི་བྱེད་པ་ལྟར། དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་མི་དམིགས་པའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་གྱིས་ཡོན་ཏན་མཆོག་འཆང་བ་ལས་རྣལ་འབྱོར་པ་བརྩོན་པ་སྟེ། སྔར་བསམ་གཏན་བཞི་དང་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་བཞི་ལ་གནས་ཏེ། ཕྱིར་ཡང་འདོད་པའི་ཁམས་སུ་གནས་ཏེ་སྔར་གྱི་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་རོ་ལ་ཆགས་པ་མེད་དེ། དཔེར་ན་ཆུའི་པད་མ་ཆུས་མ་གོས་པ་བཞིན་དུ། འདོད་ཁམས་སུ་སྐྱེས་ཀྱང་བྱིས་པ་འདོད་པའི་ཆོས་ལ་མི་གནས་སོ། །
[2-262] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "This accumulation of qualities" up to "does not dwell in dharmas": Who is this wondrous bodhisattva, this accumulation of qualities? Dwelling in the meditative concentrations of the four dhyānas and the four formless realms, a bodhisattva does not taste them by way of apprehending signs. Having made aspiration prayers for the desire realm, if those who dwell in them were to have this body perish, even though they are free from desire for the desire realm, they are born again as before in the desire realm in accordance with the intention of their aspiration prayers. Moreover, for example, it is just as if a person like the King of Jambudvīpa, Anantakīrti, who had never gone to the supreme divine city of the divine realm before, later went there, and after having seen and enjoyed those places possessed by the gods there, returned again to this Jambudvīpa with an indifferent mind, they do not generate attachment for the divine realm. Just like that example, a bodhisattva is a practitioner who strives through holding supreme qualities by means of non-apprehending meditative concentration; having formerly dwelt in the four dhyānas and the four meditative concentrations, they dwell again in the desire realm and have no attachment to the taste of the former dhyānas. For example, just as a lotus in the water is unstained by the water, even though born in the desire realm, they do not dwell in the dharmas of childish desires.

[2-264] source:
བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ་ཞེས་པ་ནས། གཉེར་མི་བྱེད་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ་དེ་གདུལ་བྱ་སེམས་ཅན་ཡོངས་སུ་སྨིན་པར་བྱ་བ་དང༌། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཞིང་ཡོངས་སུ་སྦྱོང་བ་དང༌། རང་གི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དྲུག་གི་ཚོགས་རྫོགས་པའི་དོན་བྱེད་པ་ཁོ་ནར་ཟད་ཀྱིས་འདོད་པའི་བདེ་བ་ཆགས་པའི་ཕྱིར་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །འོ་ན་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་དེ་ལ་གནས་པས་གཟུགས་མེད་དུ་ཅང་སྐྱེ་འམ། ཞེ་ན་མི་སྐྱེ་སྟེ། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་བསྒྲུབ་པ་ལས་ཉམས་པར་འགྱུར་དུ་འོང་ངོ༌། །ཞེས་གཟུགས་མེད་ཀྱི་ཁམས་སུ་སྐྱེ་བ་ལེན་པ་དོན་དུ་གཉེར་བར་མི་བྱེད་དོ། །
[2-264] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this from "Great being" up to "does not seek": That great being acts solely for the purpose of completely ripening sentient beings to be tamed, completely purifying buddha-fields, and perfecting their own accumulation of the six perfections; it is not in order to be attached to the bliss of desires. "Well then, by dwelling in that meditative concentration, are they born in the formless realm?" They are not born there, since they would come to fall away from accomplishing the qualities and perfections of a bodhisattva. Thus, they do not seek out taking birth in the formless realm.

[2-265] source:
ཅེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་མི་ཞིག་ཞེས་པ་ནས། འདོད་ཁམས་འཇུག་ཞེས་པའི་བར་ལ། རིན་པོ་ཆེའི་གཏེར་རྙེད་པའི་མིའི་དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སྦྱངས་པ་དང་ལྡན་པ་མཁས་པ་གཞན་གྱི་དོན་བྱེད་པ་ལས་དགའ་བ་དང༌། གཞན་ལ་བདེ་བ་སྦྱིན་པ་ཡང་བསམ་གཏན་བཞི་དང་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་བཞིའི་ཞི་བ་བཞི་ཐོབ་ནས། དེ་ལ་ཡང་མ་ཆགས་པར་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་བདེ་བ་དང་ལྡན་པས་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ཐོབ་པའི་ཕྱིར་བཏང་སྟེ། འགྲོ་བ་རྣམས་ལ་སྙིང་བརྩེ་བ་དང་ལྡན་པས་ཕྱིར་ཡང་འདོད་པའི་ཁམས་སུ་འཇུག་པར་འདོད་དོ། །

heading: **དུས་ཡུན་རིང་བས་ཞུམ་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "A bodhisattva" up to "lazy": Moreover, reversing that, some bodhisattvas who are unskilled in the meaning of the Mahāyāna count the accumulations gathered over tens of millions of eons and so forth. If they accomplish awakening with a mind distressed by the perception of that long duration and the difficulty of the application, and accomplish the perfectly pure dharma to be accomplished, at that time, due to the disease of that very conception, they will experience suffering for a long duration of time. Therefore, because they have degenerated from the perfection of armored joyous effort, they are despondently lazy.

heading: **དུས་ཡུན་རིང་བས་མ་ཞུམ་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "For supreme awakening" up to "should be known": Furthermore, if any person, from the time they are endowed with the aspiration of generating the mind for awakening up until they attain the final result of unsurpassable awakening, thinks in their mind for merely a single fraction of a day or night, it should be known that, being skilled through prior training and lucid through present awareness, they have undertaken the perfection of joyous effort of the genuine armor.

heading: **སྦྱོར་བ་བྱ་དཀའ་བས་མ་ཞུམ་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "But if they" up to "will attain the supreme": Moreover, reversing that, if that bodhisattva says, "If awakening is attained by merely the measure of this example, how is that difficult?", and generates a mind thinking, "In a swift time of merely an instant, I myself am able to destroy even Mount Meru into dust," then that very bodhisattva is skilled, lucid, and endowed with having undertaken armored joyous effort. Without being delayed for a long time, they will attain that supreme awakening attained by the guides, the buddhas.

heading: **བཟློག་པ།**
translation: Regarding this from "Having completely" up to "like sky and earth": Some persons who apprehend entities think, "Having completely ripened migrating beings, I will act for their purpose." If they manifest joyous effort with a body, speech, and mind apprehended as a self, because the conception of a true self of a person remains, by the power of that they become lazy. The example for such a person becoming far from attaining the omniscience of buddhahood is like the space between the sky and the earth.

heading: **ཡང་དག་པ།**
translation: Thus it is said: Regarding this from "Whenever body and" up to "has been spoken by the Benefactor": Whenever there is no conception of a body and mind apprehended as a self nor of the sentient beings for whose sake one acts, and having completely reversed all conceptions of the three spheres or of action and agent, one practices the dharma that is non-dual with respect to action and agent, this is the perfection of joyous effort of bodhisattvas who do not degenerate into realizing peaceful awakening because they desire the purpose of others, and who desire to attain the supreme. Thus it has been spoken by the Buddha, the Benefactor. Through the above, the meaning of the perfection of joyous effort has been taught.

Thus it has been spoken by the Buddha, the Benefactor. Through the above, the meaning of the perfection of joyous effort has been taught.

heading: **ངོ་བོ།**
translation: Regarding this from "If from others" up to "is wise": If one were to hear harsh words speaking badly to oneself, such as threatening to kill, from other persons, that skilled bodhisattva is joyful in mind, thinking, "Conventionally, my cultivating patience is like happiness." And ultimately, if one practices by apprehending, "Who is the speaker who speaks? Who is the person who hears? By what reason, what is to be expressed, and for what purpose?"—because they are endowed with the supreme perfection of patience of reflecting on the dharmas apprehending those, they are wise.

heading: **འབྲས་བུ།**
translation: Regarding this from "Whichever bodhisattva" up to "wise, is joyful": Whichever such aforementioned bodhisattva is endowed with the excellent dharmas of the benefits of patience in that way—even if someone were to fill this great trichiliocosm with the seven kinds of precious substances and offer them with faith and respect to the buddhas who know the world, as well as to śrāvaka arhats and pratyekabuddhas, by that aggregate of generosity they cannot match even a hundredth part up to a hundred ten-millionth part of the merit of that cultivated patience. The body of one who abides in patience in that way becomes completely pure, being endowed with the marks and signs, or radiance and strength; the thirty-two marks such as the wheels on the hands and feet and infinite power and strength will arise, and they will also proclaim the supreme emptiness of dharmas to other sentient beings; they are wise because they know such reality, that migrating beings will become faithful and joyful towards the one endowed with patience.
